# The Binding of the Manuscript

->**Description of the Exterior**<-

This ornate, historical book binding, likely dating from the sixteenth or seventeenth century, serves as a protective and decorative shell for the manuscript. The cover is crafted from dark, reddish-brown leather featuring extensive **blind-tooled** <term>blind-tooling: a technique where decorative patterns are pressed into leather using heated tools without the application of gold leaf or color</term> patterns. The design consists of several concentric rectangular borders filled with intricate **Renaissance-style** floral motifs, **arabesques** <term>arabesque: a form of artistic decoration consisting of surface decorations based on rhythmic linear patterns of scrolling and interlacing foliage</term>, and small circular medallions containing figures or portraits.

The binding is heavily reinforced with decorative brass or bronze hardware, often referred to as "furniture":

*   **Corner Pieces:** Four metal corner guards with embossed floral designs and large raised studs to protect the leather from wear.
*   **Clasp Hinges:** Two heavy metal hinges for clasps are attached to the right edge, though the corresponding leather straps are now missing.
*   **Central Boss:** A prominent, diamond-shaped metal **boss** <term>boss: a raised metal ornament placed in the center of a book cover to protect the leather when the volume is laid flat</term> sits at the heart of the cover, featuring a raised circular center and four stylized leaves or shells extending toward the corners.
*   **Spine and Edge:** A vertical metal strip runs along the left edge next to the spine. The spine itself shows several thick raised bands, and the leather surface exhibits a rich patina with minor scuffing and cracking, consistent with centuries of use.

<summary>This page describes the ornate 16th or 17th-century leather binding of the manuscript, highlighting its intricate blind-tooled Renaissance patterns and protective brass hardware.</summary>

<keywords>bookbinding, leather, blind-tooling, metal furniture, boss, clasps, Renaissance, manuscript preservation</keywords>

# Frontispiece

->**Hermetic Philosophy**<-
<note>original: "PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA"</note>

A rectangular white slip is pasted into the center of the page, featuring a circular color emblem. This bookplate serves as a visual summary of the manuscript’s contents. The pelican stands upon a white **cubic pedestal** or altar <term>cube: in alchemical tradition, the cube represents the salt of the philosophers or the "Philosopher's Stone" in its perfected, stable state</term>, which is decorated with four red **roses**. ->HERMETIC PHILOSOPHY<-
<note>original: "PHILOSOPHIA HERMETICA". This refers to the tradition of knowledge attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, involving a blend of theology, alchemy, and spiritual transformation.</note>

<note>The central image is a hand-colored circular emblem. It depicts a white pelican standing on a square pedestal, pecking its own breast to feed its young with its blood—an iconographic motif known as the "Pelican in its Piety." In a Christian context, this represents Christ’s sacrifice, but in <term>alchemy</term> (the precursor to modern chemistry and a spiritual philosophy), it symbolizes the "Great Work" of purification and the life-giving nature of the philosopher's stone. The pedestal is adorned with four golden roses, a hallmark of <term>Rosicrucianism</term>, a secret mystical society that sought a "universal reformation of mankind" through science and spirituality. Above the scene, a golden sun shines brightly, representing divine light or enlightenment.</note>

<unclear>Faint handwritten cursive is visible behind the pasted emblem, but it is too faded to be read.</unclear>

->**Preface to the Christian Reader.**<-

# Preface to the Christian Reader.

Dearest Christian Reader, it is observed daily that many pious people are found who, instead of idle and lying stories, now much prefer to search the Holy Divine Scripture. And in order to provide for them now in the most pleasant way, we have had the entire Bible (in which everything is contained) printed in a very small format, so that anyone may carry it with them on the road very handily, without great hindrance. In this, we have followed the edition of Nicolaes Biestkens <note>Nicolaes Biestkens (d. 1562) was a famous printer known for producing the first Dutch Bible with verse divisions.</note>, from the year 1572. And for the great help of the good-hearted reader, we have placed the contents of each chapter in the margin, so that whenever the reader desires a certain subject, they do not need to search through the whole chapter, but look only at the margin, where they will immediately find all information regarding it; for you will find the principal distinctions of the subject matter marked in the margin, each one right above the relevant material. Because of the indicators that were previously placed on many signs, to find them distinctly and to learn to recognize them, take note of the following instructions: The number that stands in the margin, beginning thus: 1. 2. 3. and so forth, signifies the verses. The first numeral that stands after the reference signifies the chapter to which it points, and the other number next to it signifies the verse. An example of this: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be satisfied, Mat. 5. a. 6. <note>Matthew 5, verse 6. The "a" refers to a specific section of the page or chapter.</note> in the same verse, as it stands here: Mat. 5. a. 6. And in the open spaces that stand within the chapters, there the verses are separated from one another. And where the whole chapter speaks of one single subject, only that chapter is referred to without anything placed after it; but in the following Index, those same chapters are marked with a small star (which is placed after it). For example: Images and Idols are silver, gold, metal, wood, and stone, made by human hands, Dan. 3. \*. Baruc. 6. \*. By which one shall note and recognize that the same chapters speak entirely of one subject or matter. Also, in various places in that Index, a \* is placed after the verses, and that is when that verse points to it, stating that from then on until the end of the chapter, it treats the same subject. Example: Christ taught and preached. Luke 6. c. 20. \*.

Furthermore, we have added here an explanation of the proper Hebrew, Chaldean <note>Chaldean refers to Aramaic.</note>, and Greek names which are found in the Bible. Moreover, dear reader, since we suspect that there are surely some simple people by whom the numeral <note>referring to Roman numerals</note> is unknown, we have explained that numeral with a common number <note>referring to Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3)</note> in this following small table. Item, where in the Index

<column-break/>

it stands thus: 1. Reg. <note>Latin: *Regum*, meaning Kings.</note> that is the first book of Samuel, or of the Kings. Where it stands thus: 2. Reg. that is the second book of Samuel, or of the Kings. Where it stands thus: 3. Reg. that is the third book of the Kings, which in this edition is called the First Book of the Kings. Where it now stands: 4. Reg. that is the fourth book of the Kings, which in this edition is called the Second Book of the Kings. <note>In older traditions, 1 & 2 Samuel and 1 & 2 Kings were grouped together as 1, 2, 3, and 4 Kings.</note> Item, where it stands: 1. Esd. that is the first book of Esdras, which in this edition is called the book of Ezra. Where it stands: 2. Esd. that is the second book of Esdras, which in this edition is called the book of Nehemiah. Where it stands thus: Eccle. that is Ecclesiastes, the Preacher Solomon. Where it stands: Eccli. that is Ecclesiasticus, or Jesus Sirach. <note>Sirach is a book of the Apocrypha, often included in Bibles of this period.</note> We note all of this together so that the simple reader may not go astray in their searching. Fare well.

# Index.

A.
->Alpha and Omega.<-

I am the Alpha and the Omega <note>original: "a ende O"</note> / the beginning and the end / the first and the last / says the Lord / *Isaiah 41:a, 44:b:4, 48:c:12. Revelation 1:b:8, 2:b:8, 21:a:6, 22:c:13.*

**Aaron**, a son of Amram, the son of Kohath <note>OCR reads "Rahat," a common misreading of "Kahat" or Kohath</note>, the son of Levi / *Exodus 6:c:20.* Was sent with Moses his brother to the Egyptians / *4:c:14, 5:a:1, 6:b:13. Micah 6:a:4.* Was consecrated with his sons as Priests / *Leviticus 8, Numbers 3:b:10, Deuteronomy 18:a:5, Hebrews 5:b:7.* According to the ordinance / *Exodus 28, 29, 40:b:12.* Set up the calf for Israel / *32:a:4, Psalm 106:c:19, Acts 7:e:40.* Murmured against Moses / *Numbers 12:a:1.* His rod blossoms / *17:b:8, Ecclesiasticus 45:d:25, Hebrews 9:a:4.* Enters the most holy place only once a year / *Exodus 30:b:10, Leviticus 16:g:34, 3 Maccabees 1:a:17, Hebrews 9:a:7.* Dies outside the land of Canaan / *Numbers 20:d:28, 33:d:38, Deuteronomy 10:b:6, 32:g:50.* After him, his son Eleazar became High Priest / *Numbers 20:d:26.* Is praised / *Ecclesiasticus 45:b:7.*

**Abaddon** / *Revelation 9:b:11.*

**Abarim**, a mountain range / *Numbers 21:b:11, 27:c:12, 33:f:44, Deuteronomy 32:g:49.*

**Abba Father** / *Mark 14:d:36, Romans 8:c:15, Galatians 4:a:6.*

**Abdias** / see **Obadiah**.

**Abdon**, a Judge in Israel / *Judges 12:c:13.*

**Abednego**, thrown into the glowing furnace / *Daniel 3:d:21.* Was named Azariah / *1:b:6.*

**Abel** or **Habel**, was slain by his brother Cain / *Genesis 4:b:8, 1 John 3:b:12.* Read of Abel / *Matthew 23:e:34, Luke 11:e:51, Hebrews 11:a:4, 12:d:24.*

**Abel-beth-maachah**, was besieged by Joab / *2 Samuel 20:c:14.* Was plundered <note>original: "geklagt," likely "geklaagt" or "geplaagd"</note> by Ben-hadad / *1 Kings 15:c:20.* Then by Tiglath-Pileser the King of Assyria / *2 Kings 15:f:29.*

**Abijah**, Samuel’s son, a Judge over Israel / *1 Samuel 8:a:2.*

**Abijah**, the son of Jeroboam / *1 Kings 14:a:1.*

**Abijah** / *1 Chronicles 24:b:10 <note>original: "1. Par. 25. b. 10."</note>, Luke 1:a:1.*

**Abijam**, a son of Rehoboam, King in Judah / *1 Kings 14:e:31, 15:a:1, 2 Chronicles 13:d:15.* Succeeded by Asa / *1 Kings 15:b:8, Matthew 1. b. 7.*

**Abiathar** the Priest, escaped from the hands of Saul / *1 Samuel 22:d:20.* Fled to David at Keilah / *23:a:6.* Sided with Adonijah / *1 Kings 1:a:7.* Was removed from the Priesthood / *2:d:27.* According to the word / *1 Samuel 2:f:30, g:35.*

**Abidan**, a Captain <term>Hooftman: a leader or commander</term> of the tribe of Benjamin / *Numbers 1:a:11.*

**Abigail**, a brave woman <note>original: "cloeck wijf"</note> of the godless Nabal / *1 Samuel 25:a:3.* After Nabal’s death, became King David’s wife / *25:g:39.*

**Abihu** and **Nadab**, sons of Aaron, were consumed by fire / *Leviticus 10:a:2, Numbers 26:g:61.*

**Abimelech**, the King at Gerar, takes Sarah / *Genesis 20:a:2.* Makes a covenant with Abraham / *21:c:23.*

->Concerning the Ban in the New Testament.<-
<note>The "Ban" refers to excommunication or the formal exclusion of a person from the religious community.</note>

The Evangelical Ban was instituted and commanded by Jesus Christ, Matthew 16:c:19, 18:a:8, b:18, 5:d:29, Mark 9:e:42, John 20:c:23. And was also used and taught by the Apostles, 1 Corinthians 5:a:3, b:10, 2 Thessalonians 3:a:6, b:14, 1 Timothy 1:c:20, Titus 3:b:10. For the maintenance and preservation of his community <note>original: Gemeynten</note>, and also for the improvement (and not for the condemnation) of the one who has sinned, 1 Corinthians 5:a:4, 1 Timothy 1:c:20, 2 Thessalonians 3:b:14. So that the fallen Christian, through the Evangelical Ban, which he well deserves, may be ashamed and in his soul may be won over and improved, 2 Thessalonians 3:b:14. In short, the fallen Christian ought to be regarded after the expulsion (according to the command of Jesus Christ) as a heathen and a tax collector <note>original: Publicaen</note>. Just as Jesus Christ intended, and as Paul, through the Holy Spirit, explained and set it forth in his letters, 1 Corinthians 5:\*, Titus 3:b:10. The believers must and should also exclude and shut out <note>original: Wannen ende wt sluyten</note>, without respect of persons, after sufficient warning, all those among them who

<column-break/>

teach offensively and live offensively, and will not improve themselves, Joshua 22:b:10, 3 Maccabees f:69, Matthew 18:b:17, Romans 16:b:16, 1 Corinthians 5:\*, 2 Corinthians 2:b:8, 2 Thessalonians 3:\*, 1 Timothy 1:c:20, 6:a:5, 2 Timothy 2:b:17, c:21, 3:a:5, Titus 3:b:10, 2 John b:10. And after the expulsion, they shall shun and avoid them until their repentance, so that they may be ashamed and that the congregation may not be defiled by them nor lost through association, 1 Corinthians 5:a:5. ### Of the Ban <note>Excommunication</note> in the New Testament.

The Gospel Ban is instituted and commanded by Christ Jesus / Matthew 16:c:19, 18:a:8, b:18, 5:d:29. Matthew 9:e:42. John 20:c:23. And also used and taught by the Apostles / 1 Corinthians 5:a:3, b:10. 2 Thessalonians 3:a:6, b:14. 1 Timothy 1:c:20. Titus 3:b:10. For the maintenance of purity and the protection of His Church / And also for the improvement (and not the damnation) of the one who has sinned there / 1 Corinthians 5:a:4. 1 Timothy 1:c:20. 2 Thessalonians 3:b:14. So that the fallen Christian / by means of the Gospel Ban / which he well deserves / may be ashamed / and may be won and improved in his soul / 2 Thessalonians 3:b:14. In sum / the fallen Christian / after expulsion, should be regarded (according to the command of Christ Jesus) as a Heathen and a Publican <note>tax collector</note>. Just as Christ Jesus intended that / and as Paul through the Holy Spirit has explained and set forth in his letters / 1 Corinthians 5:\*. Titus 3:b:10. Banning and shunning / the believers should and ought also to do without respect of persons / after sufficient warning / to all those among them who

In the beginning God created Heaven and Earth.
2 And the Earth was waste and empty / and it was dark upon the deep / and the Spirit of God hovered upon the water. 3 And God spoke: Let there be light. 4 And there was Light. Then from evening and morning came the first day. 6 *And God spoke: Let there be a firmament <note>The "firmament" refers to the dome of the sky which ancient peoples believed separated the waters above from the waters below.</note> between the waters / and let it be a distinction between the waters. 7 Then God made the firmament / and divided the water under the firmament / from the water above the firmament. 8 And it happened so. And God called the firmament / Heaven. Then from evening and morning came the second day. 9 And God spoke: *Let the water gather itself under the heaven into particular places / that the dry land may be seen. 10 And it happened so. And God called the dry / earth / And the gathering of the waters he called sea. And the earth brought forth grass and herbs / that yielded seed / each after its kind: And trees that there bore fruit and had their own seed within themselves / each after its kind / and God saw that 13 it was good. Then from evening and morning came the third day. 14 And God spoke: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the Heaven / and divide day and night / and let them be for signs / times / days and Years. 15 And let them be lights in the firmament of the heaven / that they shine upon the earth. And it happened so. 16 And God made two great lights. A great light / to rule the day / and a small light / to rule the night: 17 Thereto also stars. It highlights the transition of the Abrahamic blessing to Jacob and his commitment to God through his vow and tithe.</summary>

<margin>Breeding.</margin>
...distanced them far apart, between himself and Jacob. Thus Jacob tended the remaining flocks of Laban. But Jacob took sticks of green poplar trees, hazel, and chestnut, and peeled white stripes in them, so that the white was exposed on the sticks. And he laid the sticks he had peeled in the watering troughs for the flocks, where they had to come to drink, so that they would conceive when they came to drink. Thus the flocks conceived over the sticks, and brought forth speckled, spotted, and mottled offspring. Then Jacob separated the lambs and put the separated flocks with the spotted and black ones in Laban's flock, and he made himself his own flock, which he did not add to Laban's flock. But whenever the early flocks were in heat, he laid the sticks in the troughs before the eyes of the flock, so that they would conceive over the sticks. But in the late breeding season, he did not lay them in there. Thus the late-born became Laban’s, and the early-born became Jacob’s. From this, the man became exceedingly rich, so that he had many sheep, maidservants, menservants, camels, and donkeys.

Jacob came to Luz in the land of Canaan (which was called Bethel) with all the people who were with him. And he built an altar there, and he called the place *El-Bethel* <note>meaning "The God of the House of God"</note>, because God had revealed Himself to him there when he fled from his brother. Then Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and it was called the Oak of Mourning. *And God appeared to Jacob once again, after he had come from Mesopotamia, and blessed him, and spoke to him: "Your name is Jacob; *but you shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel shall be your name." And so he was named Israel. And God spoke to him: "I am the Almighty God; be fruitful and multiply; nations and a company of nations shall come from you, and kings shall come from your loins. And the land that I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land." Then God went up from him, from the place where He had spoken with him. But Jacob set up a stone pillar there, in the place where He had spoken with him, and poured a drink offering on it, and poured oil over it. And Jacob called the place where God had spoken with him, Bethel. And they journeyed from Bethel; and when there was still a distance to go to Ephrath, Rachel went into labor: and she had a hard time in her giving of birth. But when she was so distressed in the labor, the midwife spoke to her: "Do not fear, for you shall have this son as well." And it happened while Israel lived in that land, that Reuben went and slept with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and that came to Israel’s ears. Now Jacob had twelve sons. The sons of Leah were these: Reuben, the firstborn son of Jacob, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. The sons of Rachel were: Joseph and Benjamin. The sons of Bilhah, Rachel’s maidservant: Dan and Naphtali. The sons of Zilpah, Leah’s maidservant: Gad and Asher: these are Jacob’s sons, who were born to him in Mesopotamia. And he came to his father Isaac at Mamre in the chief city which is called Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac had lived as strangers. And Isaac became one hundred and eighty years old. And he grew weak and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days; and his sons, Esau and Jacob, buried him.

And Jethro said: Blessed be the Lord who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and Pharaoh, who knows how to deliver his people from the hand of Egypt. Then Aaron and all the Elders of Israel came to eat bread with Moses' father-in-law before God.

The next morning, Moses sat to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from morning until evening. But when his father-in-law saw all that he did with the people, he said: What is this that you are doing with the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand around you from morning until evening? Moses answered him: The people come to me to ask God for counsel. For whenever they have a matter to settle, they come to me, so that I may judge between a man and his neighbor, and teach them God’s statutes and his laws. His father-in-law spoke to him: What you are doing is not good. You will weary yourself, and the people who are with you as well. * This work is too heavy for you; you cannot perform it alone. Now hear my voice; I will advise you, and God shall be with you. You represent the people before God, and bring the cases before God. And make for them statutes and laws, and teach them the way in which they should walk, and the works they must do. And look out from among all the people for capable men, who fear God, are truthful, and hate covetousness; set these over them. Some over thousands, over hundreds, over fifties, and over tens, so that they may judge the people at all times. * But whenever there is a great matter, let them bring it to you, and let them judge all small matters themselves; so it will be lighter for you, and they shall bear the burden with you. If you do this, you will be able to endure what God commands you, and all these people can come to their place in peace. Moses listened to his father-in-law’s words * and did all that he said. And he chose capable men out of all Israel and made them heads over the people: some over thousands, over hundreds, over fifties, and over tens, so that they might judge the people at all times. But the hard cases they brought to Moses, and the small matters they judged themselves. Thus Moses let his father-in-law depart back to his own land.

And you shall be to me a priestly kingdom and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall say to the children of Israel. And Moses told the Lord the words of the people. The Lord said to Moses: Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow; let them wash their clothes and be ready for the third day. For on the third day, the Lord will come down in the sight of all the people upon Mount Sinai. And set boundaries <note>original: "teeckenen," marks or signs used here as physical limits.</note> around the people, and say to them: Take heed to yourselves, that you do not go up the mountain, nor touch the edges of it. * For whoever touches the mountain shall surely die. No hand shall touch him, but he shall be stoned or shot through with arrows <note>original: "met gheschut door geschootẽ," likely referring to arrows or darts.</note>; whether it be beast or man, he shall not live. When the sound of the horn is heard, then they shall come to the mountain. Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified them, and they washed their clothes. <margin>20</margin> Whoever strikes his servant or his maidservant with a rod, so that they die under his hands, shall be punished.
<margin>21</margin> *But if they live for one or two days, then he shall not be punished for it, for they are his property <note>Literally "his money," reflecting the legal status of servants as property in ancient Near Eastern law.</note>.
<margin>22</margin> *If men fight together and hurt a pregnant woman, so that her fruit departs <note>This refers to a miscarriage.</note> and no further harm happens to her, then he shall be punished with a fine as much as the woman's husband imposes upon him, and he shall give it according to the judgment of the arbiters <term>segslieden: officials or witnesses chosen to settle a dispute and determine a fair fine</term>.

<margin>31</margin> The same shall be done with him if it gores a son or a daughter.
<margin>32</margin> But if it gores a servant or a maidservant, then he shall give thirty silver shekels <term>sickel: a weight of silver used as currency</term> to their master, and the ox shall be stoned.

<margin>34</margin> The owner of the pit shall pay the other back with money, but the carcass shall be his.

### The 22nd Chapter.

<margin>31. a b. 6 e / 2 a. / ade, z. 30 . 15. 7 or those who...</margin>
<margin>1</margin> When someone steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters or sells it, *he shall give five oxen back for one ox,
<margin>2</margin> and four sheep for one sheep. If a thief is found breaking in and is struck so that he dies, then no blood-judgment <note>A legal process for murder or manslaughter.</note> shall be held over the one who did it.
<margin>3</margin> But if the sun has risen over him, then a blood-judgment shall be held. A thief must make full restitution. If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft <note>The original "dienerie" refers to the act of theft or the stolen goods.</note>.
<margin>4</margin> But if the stolen thing <note>original: "dienerie"</note> is found alive with him, whether it be an ox, donkey, or sheep, then he shall give back double.
<margin>5</margin> If someone damages a field or vineyard by letting his cattle do damage in another's field, he shall make restitution from the best of his own field and vineyard.
<margin>6</margin> *If a fire breaks out and catches in the thorns, and burns the sheaves or the grain that is still standing, or the field, then he who started the fire shall make full restitution.
<margin>7</margin> *If someone gives his neighbor money or household goods to keep, and it is stolen from that person's house, if the thief is found, he shall give back double. If the thief is not found, then the master of the house

<margin>9</margin> If one person accuses another of any kind of wrong, whether it be for an ox, donkey, or sheep, or clothing, or anything that is lost, then both their cases shall come before the judges; and whomever the judges condemn, he shall give back double to his neighbor.
<margin>10</margin> When someone gives his neighbor a donkey or ox or sheep or any livestock to keep, and it dies, or is injured, or is taken away while no one is watching,

<margin>14</margin> If someone borrows anything from his neighbor and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, then he shall make full restitution.
<margin>15</margin> But if its owner is with it, then he shall not pay back, since he has hired it for his money.

### The 1st Chapter.

1 **A**ND the LORD called Moses, and spoke with him from the Tent of Testimony <note>The Tabernacle, the portable dwelling place of God's presence</note>, saying: Speak with the children of Israel, and say to them: whoever among you wishes to make an offering to the Lord, let him do so from the livestock,
2 from the cattle, or from the sheep. If he wishes to make a burnt offering of oxen, let him offer a male that is without blemish <note>original: "sonder smette"; meaning physically perfect, suitable for a holy sacrifice</note>, at the door of the Tent of Testimony, so that it may be acceptable to the Lord
3 on his behalf. And let him lay his hand upon the head of the burnt offering, so it shall be accepted to make atonement for him. And he shall slaughter the young bull
4 before the Lord. And the Priests, Aaron’s sons, shall bring the blood and sprinkle it all around the Altar that is before the door of the Tent of Testimony.
5 And the skin shall be stripped from the burnt offering, and it shall be cut into pieces.
6 And the sons of Aaron the Priest shall prepare a fire upon the altar
7 and lay wood upon it. And they shall lay the pieces—namely, the head and the fat—upon the wood that is on the fire
8 upon the Altar. But the entrails and the legs shall be washed with water, and the Priest shall burn it all on the Altar as a burnt offering. That is a fire
9 of a sweet aroma <note>original: "soeten rueck"; a pleasing fragrance to God</note> to the Lord. But if he wishes to make a burnt offering from the sheep or from the goats, let him offer a male that is without blemish.
10 And he shall slaughter it at the side of the Altar toward the North before the Lord. And the Priests, Aaron’s sons, shall sprinkle its blood all around the Altar.
11 And it shall be cut into pieces, and the Priest shall lay the head and the fat upon the wood and the fire that is on the Altar. But the entrails and the legs shall be washed with water. And the Priest shall offer it all and burn it on the Altar as a burnt offering: That is a fire of a sweet aroma to the Lord. But if he wishes
12 to make a burnt offering of birds to the Lord, let him do so from turtledoves or from
13 young pigeons. And the Priest shall bring it to the Altar and wring off its head, so that it may be burned on the Altar, and
14 let its blood flow out against the wall of the Altar. And its crop with its feathers shall
15 be thrown beside the Altar toward the East upon the
16 ash heap. And he shall cleave its wings, but not break them off. And so the Priest shall burn it on the Altar, upon the wood,
17 upon the fire as a burnt offering. That is a fire of a sweet aroma to the Lord.

### The 2nd Chapter.

1 **W**HEN a soul wishes to make a grain offering <note>original: "spijsoffer"; literally a food or meal offering, consisting of flour rather than meat</note> to the Lord, it shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and
2 put frankincense upon it, and so bring it to the Priests, Aaron’s sons. Then the Priest shall take his handful of the same fine flour and oil, with all the frankincense, and burn it as a memorial on
3 the Altar. That is a fire of a sweet aroma to the Lord. But what remains of the grain offering shall be for Aaron and his
4 sons: That shall be the Most Holy <note>original: "Alderheylichste"</note> of the offerings of the Lord. But if he wishes to make a grain
5 offering of that which is baked in the oven, let him take cakes of fine flour, unleavened, mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers
6 smeared with oil. But if your grain offering is something baked in a pan, it shall be of unleavened fine flour mixed with oil.
7 And you shall divide it into pieces and pour oil upon it; then it is a grain offering. But if your

3 burn it on the Altar. That is a fire of a sweet aroma to the Lord. But what
4 remains shall be for Aaron and his sons: that shall be the most holy of the offerings of the Lord. Every grain offering that you wish to offer to the Lord shall be made without leaven <note>original: "suerdeech"; yeast or sourdough</note>.
<margin>For grain offerings are without leaven.</margin>

## Lawful Worship. Leviticus.

1 AND the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:
2 Speak with the children of Israel, and say: If a soul <note>The word "soul" here refers to an individual person.</note> sins through ignorance against any commandment of the Lord, concerning things which ought not to be done, namely:

<margin>Of the sin offering for the Priests. Leviticus 9:15.</margin>
3 If a priest who is anointed sins, so that he brings guilt upon the people, he shall bring for his sin, which he has committed, a young bull without blemish to the Lord for a <term>sin offering</term> <note>A sacrifice specifically intended to purify a person after a mistake or ritual impurity.</note>.
4 And he shall bring the bull before the door of the Tent of Testimony <note>The Tabernacle, the portable earthly dwelling place of God.</note> before the Lord, and lay his hand upon its head, and slay it before the Lord.
5 And the Priest who is anointed shall take of the bull’s blood and bring it into the Tent of Testimony.

<margin>Leviticus 16:19</margin>
6 And he shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, before the veil of the sanctuary.
7 And he shall put some of the same blood on the horns of the altar of incense, which stands before the Lord in the Tent of Testimony. And all the rest of the blood he shall pour at the bottom of the Altar of burnt offerings, which stands before the door of the Tent of Testimony.
8 And all the fat of the sin offering he shall lift <note>To "lift" or "heave" refers to the ritual removal of specific portions for the sacrifice.</note>, namely, the fat on the entrails,
9 the two kidneys, with the fat that is on them by the loins, and the membrane over the liver which is removed with the kidneys,
10 Just as it is lifted from the bull of the thank offering; and he shall burn it on the Altar of burnt offerings.

<margin>Exodus 29:14. Numbers 19:5.</margin>
11 But the skin of the bull, with all the flesh, with the head and legs, and the entrails and the dung,
12 he shall carry all of it outside the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and shall burn it on wood with fire.

<margin>Leviticus 9:15. Numbers 15:1. Of the sin offering for the congregation.</margin>
13 When a whole multitude in Israel errs, and the deed remains hidden from their eyes, such that they have done something against a commandment of the Lord which they should not have done, and thus make themselves guilty,
14 and afterwards they become aware of their sin which they have committed, then they shall bring a young bull for a sin offering, and place it before the door of the Tent of Testimony.
15 And the elders of the multitude shall lay their hands on its head before the Lord, and slay the bull before the Lord.
16 And the Priest who is anointed shall bring the blood of the bull into the Tent of Testimony,
17 And dip his finger in it, and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, before the veil.
18 And he shall smear some of the blood on the horns of the Altar which stands before the Lord in the Tent of Testimony, and pour all the other blood at the bottom of the Altar of burnt offerings, which stands before the door of the Tent of Testimony.
19 But all its fat he shall lift and burn upon the Altar.
20 And he shall do with the bull as he did with the bull of the [previous] sin offering; and so shall the Priest make atonement for them, and it shall be forgiven them.
21 And he shall bring the bull outside the camp and burn it, as he burned the first one. That shall be the sin offering of the multitude.

<margin>Of the sin offering for a Leader.</margin>
22 But when a leader sins, and does something against the commandment of the Lord his God which he should not do, and commits an error for which he makes himself guilty,
23 And he becomes aware of the sin which he has committed, he shall bring for an offering a male goat without blemish,
24 And lay his hand on the goat’s head, and slay it in the place where the burnt offering is slain before the Lord; that is his sin offering.
25 Then the Priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and smear it on the horns of the Altar of burnt offerings, and pour the rest of the blood at the bottom of the Altar of burnt offerings.

<column-break/>

26 But all its fat he shall burn upon the altar, just like the fat of the thank offering. And so shall the Priest make atonement for his sins, and it shall be forgiven him.

<margin>Numbers 15:28. Of the sin offering of a soul for a common man.</margin>
27 If a soul among the common people errs and sins, such that he does something against one of the commandments of the Lord which he should not do, and thus makes himself guilty,
28 And his sin which he has committed becomes known to him, he shall bring for the offering a female goat without blemish, for the sin which he has committed,
29 And shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slay it at the place of the burnt offering.
30 And the priest shall take of the blood with his finger, and smear it on the horns of the Altar of burnt offerings, and pour all the other blood at the bottom of the Altar.

<margin>Exodus 30.</margin>
31 But all its fat he shall remove, just as he removes the fat of the thank offering, and shall burn it on the Altar for a sweet aroma to the Lord; and so shall the Priest make atonement, and it shall be forgiven her.
32 But if he brings a sheep for a sin offering, he shall bring a female that is without blemish,
33 And lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slay it for a sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slain.
34 And the Priest shall take of the blood with his finger, and smear it on the horns of the Altar of burnt offerings, and pour all the blood at the bottom of the Altar.
35 But all its fat he shall remove, as he removed the fat of the lamb of the thank offering, and shall burn it on the Altar as a fire for the Lord; and so shall the Priest make atonement for his sin that he has committed, and it shall be forgiven him.

<margin>49</margin> and if the mark is pale or reddish in the garment or in the skin, or in the warp or woof, or in any kind of thing made of skins, it is certainly a mark of leprosy. Therefore the Priest shall examine it.
<margin>50</margin> And when he sees the mark, he shall shut it up for seven days.
<margin>51</margin> And if he sees on the seventh day that the mark has spread further in the garment, in the warp, or in the woof, in the skin, or in all that is made of skins, then it is a "devouring" <note>original: "etende" – literally "eating," referring to a spreading or malignant infection</note> mark of leprosy, and it is unclean.
<margin>52</margin> And he shall burn the garment, or the warp, or the woof, whether it be wool or linen, or any leatherwork in which such a mark is found. For it is a mark of leprosy; and he shall burn it with fire.
<margin>53</margin> But if the Priest shall see that the mark has not spread further in the garment, or in the warp, or in the woof, or in any kind of leatherwork,
<margin>54</margin> then he shall command that the thing in which the mark is be washed, and he shall shut it up for another seven days.
<margin>55</margin> And when the Priest sees, after the mark is washed, that the mark has not changed before his eyes, and has also not spread further, it is still unclean and he shall burn it with fire, for it has eaten deep inward and has corrupted it.
<margin>56</margin> But if the Priest sees that the mark has faded after it was washed, then he shall tear it out of the garment, or the skin, or the warp, or the woof.
<margin>57</margin> But if it is still seen in the garment, in the warp, or in the woof, or in any kind of leatherwork, then it is a spreading plague, and he shall burn with fire that in which such a mark is.
<margin>58</margin> But the garment, or warp, or woof, or any kind of leatherwork that has been washed, and from which the mark has departed, shall be washed once more, and then it is clean.
<margin>59</margin> This is the law regarding the marks of leprosy in garments, whether they be wool or linen, in the warp or the woof, and in all kinds of leatherwork, to pronounce them clean or unclean.

# Statutes and Laws. Leviticus.

This refers to the Year of Jubilee, a holy year every 50 years when debts were cancelled and land was returned to its original ancestral owners.</note></term> year shall be holy among you. But you shall eat what the field brings forth. That is the Jubilee year, when every man shall come again to his own property. <margin>On buying and selling land.</margin> When you now sell anything to your neighbor, or buy anything from him, no man shall deceive his brother. But according to the number of years after the Jubilee you shall buy from him, and according to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you. According to the multitude of years you shall increase the price, and according to the fewness of years you shall diminish the price, for he sells to you according to the number of harvests it may bear. So let no one now deceive his neighbor, but fear your God. For I am the Lord your God. Therefore, act according to my statutes and keep my laws, that you do them, so that you may dwell in the land securely. For the land shall give you its fruit, so that you have enough to eat, and dwell securely therein. <margin>Against anxiety.</margin> And if you should say: "What shall we eat in the seventh year? For we do not sow, nor do we gather in any grain." I will command my blessing upon you in the sixth year, so that it shall yield grain for three years. So that you sow in the eighth year, and eat of the old grain until the ninth year; you shall eat of the old until the new grain comes again. <margin>Psal. 24:1</margin> Therefore you shall not sell the land forever, for the land is *mine, and* you are strangers and guests before me. <margin>Num. 35:3. Jere. 32:3. Ruth 4:4. Regarding redemption of the land.</margin> And in all your land, you shall grant the right to redeem the land. If your brother becomes poor and sells you his property, and his nearest kinsman comes to him to redeem it, then he shall redeem what his brother has sold. But if a man has no redeemer, and can manage with his own hand to bring enough together to redeem a portion of it, then let him count the years from the time he sold it, and restore the overplus to the man to whom he sold it, that he may come again to his property. But if his hand cannot find enough to get it back, then that which he sold shall remain in the hand of the buyer until the Jubilee year. In that same year it shall be released, and he shall return to his property. <margin>On the selling of the house.</margin> Whoever sells a dwelling house within a walled city has a whole year's respite to redeem it; that shall be the time in which he may redeem it. But if he does not redeem it before the full year is out, then the buyer shall keep it forever, and his descendants, and it shall not be released in the Jubilee. But if it is a house in a village that has no wall around it, it shall be counted as the fields of the country; it may be redeemed, and it shall be released in the Jubilee. The cities of the Levites, and the houses in the cities that are their property, may be redeemed at any time. <margin>Jere. 32:8</margin> Whoever redeems anything from the Levites, whether it be a house or a city that he possessed, shall leave it in the Jubilee. For the houses in the cities of the Levites are their property among the children of Israel. But the fields before their cities may not be sold, for it is their eternal inheritance. If your brother becomes poor and falls into decay beside you, then you shall take him in, as a stranger or a guest, so that he may live with you. <margin>Exo. 22:25. Deut. 23:19</margin> And you shall take no <term>usury<note>Dutch: "woecker." Taking interest on loans to fellow Israelites was forbidden, as it was seen as profiting from a brother's misfortune.</note></term> from him, nor any profit; but fear your God, so that your brother may live with you. For you shall not give him your money upon usury,

<column-break/>

nor put out your food for profit. For I am the Lord your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God. If your brother becomes poor beside you, and he sells himself to you, you shall not let him serve as a <margin>Exod. 21:2. Deut. 15:12. Jere. 34:14.</margin> <term>bondservant<note>Dutch: "lijfeygen," literally "body-owned." An Israelite who sold himself was to be treated as a hired worker, not a slave.</note></term>. But as a day laborer and a guest he shall be with you, and shall serve with you until the Jubilee. Then he shall go out from you, and his children with him, and shall return to his own family, and to the property of his fathers. For they are my servants, whom I led out of the land of Egypt; therefore they shall not be sold in the manner of bondservants. And you shall not rule over them with rigor, but fear your God. But if you wish to have bondservants and maids, you shall buy them from the heathens that are around you. From the guests who are strangers among you, and from their descendants who are born among you in your land. These you shall have as your own, and you shall possess them, and your children after you, for an eternal possession; these you shall let be bondservants. <margin>3 Re. 9:22</margin> But over your brothers, the children of Israel, no one shall rule over the other with such rigor. If a stranger or guest among you prospers, and your brother beside him becomes poor, and sells himself to the stranger or guest among you, or to someone of his lineage, then after he is sold, he shall have the right to be redeemed again. And someone among his brothers may redeem him, or his father, or also his father’s son, or any other of his near kin of his family. Or if his own hand earns so much, then he shall redeem himself. And he shall reckon with his buyer from the year that he was sold to him until the Jubilee. And the price of his sale shall be according to the number of years; and his time shall be reckoned as that of a day laborer. If there are still many years until the Jubilee, he shall give accordingly more for his redemption, out of the money that he was bought for. But if there are few years remaining until the Jubilee, then he shall also give back accordingly for his redemption. And his time shall be reckoned as a day laborer from year to year; and you shall not let him be ruled over with rigor before your eyes. But if he is not redeemed in this manner, then he shall go out free in the Jubilee, and his children with him. For the children of Israel are my servants, whom I led out of the land of Egypt. <margin>Deut. 5:8. Exo. 20:4</margin> I am the Lord your God. You shall make no idols for yourselves, nor images, nor shall you set up columns for yourselves, nor set up any stone signs in your land to worship before them. For I am the Lord your God. Keep my Sabbaths and stand in awe of my Sanctuary. I am the Lord.

neither exchange nor substitute it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good. But if someone wishes to exchange one beast for another, then both shall be holy to the Lord.
<margin>Livestock valuation.</margin>
11 But if the animal is unclean, so that it may not be offered to the Lord, then he shall set it before the Priest,
12 And the Priest shall value it, whether it be good or bad; and it shall remain as the Priest's valuation.
13 But if someone wishes to redeem it, he shall give a fifth [part] above the valuation.
<margin>House valuation.</margin>
14 When someone consecrates his house, so that it is holy to the Lord, the Priest shall value it whether it be good or bad. And as the Priest values it, so shall it remain.
15 And if he who has consecrated it wishes to redeem it, then he shall give the fifth part of the money above what it is valued at, and so it shall be his.
<margin>Field valuation.</margin>
16 If someone consecrates a piece of a field to the Lord from his inheritance, it shall be valued according to what it produces. If it bears a homer <note>A dry measure of roughly 220 liters.</note> of barley, it shall be worth fifty Shekels of silver.
17 But if he consecrates his field from the Year of Jubilee <note>original: "Luytiaer"; literally the 'sounding year,' referring to the trumpet blast announcing the Jubilee.</note> onwards, it shall be worth its full value.
18 But if he has consecrated it after the Jubilee, then the Priest shall reckon to him the money according to the years that remain until the Jubilee, and the valuation shall be reduced accordingly.
19 But if he who has consecrated it wishes to redeem the field, he shall give the fifth part of the money above what it is valued at, and so it shall be his.
20 But if he does not wish to redeem it, but sells it to another, then he may not redeem it any more.
21 But the same field, when it goes free in the Jubilee, shall be holy to the Lord, like a devoted field <note>A field set apart or 'banned' from common use; see 'cherem'.</note>, and it shall be the Priest's inheritance.
22 But if someone consecrates a field to the Lord which he has bought, and is not part of his inheritance,
23 then the Priest shall reckon to him what it is worth until the Jubilee; and he shall give that valuation on the same day, as a holy thing to the Lord.
24 But in the Jubilee, it shall return to him from whom it was bought, to whom the inheritance of the land belongs.
25 All valuations shall be made according to the Shekel of the Sanctuary. * A Shekel makes twenty Gerahs.

26 The firstborn among the livestock, which otherwise belongs to the Lord, no one shall consecrate to the Lord, whether it be an Ox or a Sheep, for it is the Lord's.
27 But if it is an unclean beast, then he shall redeem it according to its valuation, and give the fifth [part] above it. But if he does not wish to redeem it, then it shall be sold according to its valuation.
28 Nothing devoted <note>original: "verbannens"; referring to the 'herem' or things strictly set apart for God that cannot be reclaimed.</note> shall be sold or redeemed, that someone devotes to the Lord of all that is his, whether it be Man, Livestock, or inherited field. For everything devoted is Most Holy to the Lord.
29 No devoted person shall be redeemed, but he shall surely die.
30 All tithes in the Land, both of the seed of the soil and of the fruit of the trees, are the Lord's, and shall be holy to the Lord.
31 But if someone wishes to redeem his tithe, he shall add a fifth part to it.
<margin>The tithe</margin>

33 One shall not distinguish whether it be good or bad, nor shall one exchange it. But if someone wishes to exchange it, then both shall be holy and not be redeemed.
34 These are the Commandments which the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.

<margin>Leviticus 5:23. Concerning confession of sins</margin>
...if anyone commits a sin against another person, and thereby sins against the Lord, then that soul has a debt upon them: <margin>7</margin> And they shall confess the sin they have done and shall restore their debt in full <note>original: "hooftsomme" — the principal amount</note>, and add the fifth part thereto, and give it to the one against whom they have trespassed. <margin>8</margin> But if there is no kinsman present to whom the debt should be paid, then it shall be given to the Lord, for the Priest, in addition to the Ram of Atonement, <margin>9</margin> by which he is atoned for. Likewise, every Contribution <note>original: "Heffinge" — a portion of an offering set aside for the priests</note> of all that the children of Israel hallow and offer to the Priest, shall be <margin>10</margin> his. And whatever anyone hallows shall also be his. And whatever anyone gives to the Priest shall also be his. <margin>11</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and say <margin>12</margin> to them: <margin>Deuteronomy 22:13. Concerning the law of jealousy.</margin> If any man’s wife goes <margin>13</margin> astray, and commits a sin against him, and another man lies with her carnally, and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband, and stays concealed, so that she is defiled, and there are no witnesses against her, as she was not caught <margin>14</margin> in the act; and a spirit of jealousy <margin>* A jealous spirit.</margin> comes upon him, so that he is jealous of his wife, whether she be defiled or not <margin>15</margin> defiled: then he shall bring her to the Priest, and bring an offering for her, a tenth of an ephah of barley meal; he shall pour no oil upon it, nor put frankincense upon it. For it is a Jealousy offering and a Memorial offering <note>original: "wroechofer" — an offering intended to bring a transgression to remembrance or judgment</note>, <margin>16</margin> that brings the misdeed to light. Thus the Priest shall bring her, and set her before the Lord. <margin>Numbers 19.</margin> <margin>17</margin> And he shall take holy water in an earthen vessel, and take dust <note>original: "stoc sandt" — likely a transcription for 'stof' or 'stuck' sand, referring to dust from the floor</note> from under the Tabernacle and put it into the <margin>18</margin> water. And he shall set the woman before the Lord, and uncover her head, and lay the Memorial offering, which is a Jealousy offering, upon her hand. And the Priest shall have in his hand the bit- <margin>19</margin> ter, cursed water, and shall adjure the woman, and say to her: If no man has slept with you, and you have not gone astray from your husband so that you have not defiled yourself, then these bitter, cursed waters <margin>20</margin> shall not harm you. But if you have gone astray from your husband, so that you are defiled, and someone has <margin>21</margin> slept with you besides your husband: then the Priest shall adjure the woman with such a curse, and shall say to her: The Lord make you a curse and an oath among your people, that the Lord may make your <margin>22</margin> thigh rot and your belly swell. So let this cursed water go into your body, that your belly may swell and your thigh rot. <margin>23</margin> And the woman shall say: Amen, Amen. Thus the Priest shall write this curse on a scroll <margin>Concerning bitter water.</margin> and wash it off with the bitter water, <margin>24</margin> and shall give the woman the bitter, cursed water to drink. And when the cursed, bitter water has entered into her, then <margin>25</margin> the Priest shall take the Jealousy offering from her hand, and wave it as a Grain offering before the Lord, <margin>26</margin> and offer it upon the Altar; namely, he shall take a handful of the Grain offering as her Memorial offering, and burn it upon the Altar, and <margin>27</margin> thereafter give the woman the water to drink. And when she has drunk the water, if she is defiled and has sinned against her husband: then the cursed water shall enter into her and be bitter to her, so that her belly shall swell and her thigh shall rot; and the woman shall be a <margin>28</margin> curse among her people. But if such a woman is not defiled, but is clean, then it shall not harm her, so that she may <margin>29</margin> conceive. This is the Law of Jealousy, when a wife goes astray from her husband and becomes defiled; or <margin>30</margin> when a spirit of jealousy comes upon a man, so that he <margin>31</margin> is jealous of his wife; that he shall set her before the Lord, and the Priest shall do with her all according to this law: and the man shall be guiltless of this misdeed, but the woman shall bear her misdeed.

### The 6th Chapter.

<margin>1</margin> And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: <margin>2</margin> Speak to the children of Israel, <margin>Concerning the law of the Nazirites.</margin> and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow to separate <margin>3</margin> themselves to the Lord, they shall abstain from wine and strong drink. <margin>Judges 13:4; Amos 2:11.</margin> They shall drink neither wine-vinegar nor strong-drink vinegar, nor shall they drink anything made from grapes. They shall not eat fresh or dried <margin>4</margin> grapes, as long as their vow lasts. Nor shall they eat anything that is made from the grapevine, neither the seeds nor the skins. <margin>5</margin> As long as the time of such a vow <margin>Leviticus 21:5.</margin> lasts, no razor shall come upon their head until the time is fulfilled for which they vowed to the Lord: for they are holy. And they shall <margin>6</margin> let the hair on their head grow freely. All the time that they have vowed to the Lord, <margin>7</margin> they shall not go near any dead body. They shall not even defile themselves for the death of their father, their mother, their brother, or their sister. For the vow of <margin>8</margin> their God is upon their head. And all the time of their vow, they shall be holy to the Lord. <margin>9</margin> And if someone dies suddenly and unexpectedly before them, then the head of their vow <margin>Acts 18:18; 21:24.</margin> shall become unclean. || Therefore they shall shave their head on the day of their cleansing, which is <margin>10</margin> on the seventh day. And on the eighth day they shall bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to the Priest, to the <margin>11</margin> door of the Tabernacle of Testimony. And the Priest shall make one a sin offering and the other a burnt offering, and make atonement for them; because they sinned because of the dead body, and thus hallow their head on that same <margin>12</margin> day. That they may continue the time of their vow to the Lord, they shall bring a year-old lamb as a guilt offering; but the previous days shall be lost, because their vow was defiled. This <margin>13</margin> is the law of the Nazirite <note>original: "verloueden" — the one who has made a vow</note>: When the time of their vow is fulfilled, they shall be brought to <margin>14</margin> the door of the Tabernacle of Testimony. And they shall bring their offering to the Lord: a year-old lamb without blemish for a burnt offering, and a year-old sheep without blemish for a sin offering, and a ram without blemish for <margin>15</margin> a peace offering <note>original: "dancoffer" — thank offering</note>, and a basket of unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers <margin>16</margin> smeared with oil, and their grain offering and drink offering. And the Priest shall bring them before the Lord, and <margin>17</margin> shall make their sin offering and their burnt offering. And he shall make the ram a peace offering to the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread. And he shall also make its grain offering and drink <margin>18</margin> offering. And the Nazirite shall shave the head of their vow at the door of the Tabernacle of Testimony. And the hair of the head <margin>19</margin> [shall be put in the fire]. The Priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram and one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall lay them upon the Nazirite's hands, after <margin>20</margin> they have shaved off the hair of their vow: and shall wave them before the Lord. This is holy to the Priest, along with the wave-breast and the heave-shoulder. Thereafter the Nazirite may drink <margin>21</margin> wine. This is the law of the Nazirite who vows their offering to the Lord because of their vow, besides that which they are otherwise able to afford. As they have vowed, so shall they do.

The children of Israel did exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.

Whoever is clean in your house may eat of it. All the best oil and all the best <term>must</term> <note>new wine</note> and grain of their firstfruits which they give to the Lord, I have given to you. The firstfruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to the Lord, shall be yours. Whoever is clean in your house may eat of it. Everything <term>devoted</term> <note>original: "verbannen"; refers to "herem," items or property irrevocably dedicated to God</note> in Israel shall be yours. Everything that opens the womb among all flesh, which they bring to the Lord, whether man or beast, shall be yours. Nevertheless, you shall permit the firstborn of man to be redeemed, and the firstborn of an unclean beast you shall also permit to be redeemed. But they shall redeem them when they are a month old, and you shall give them for redemption for money, for five shekels according to the shekel of the sanctuary, which is worth twenty <term>gerahs</term> <note>a small unit of weight/currency</note>. But the firstborn of an ox, or a lamb, or a goat, you shall not permit to be redeemed, for they are holy. Their blood you shall sprinkle upon the altar, and their fat you shall burn as an offering of a sweet savor to the Lord. Their meat shall be yours, just as the wave-breast and the right shoulder are yours. All the heave offerings which the children of Israel sanctify to the Lord, I have given to you and your sons and your daughters with you as a perpetual right. That shall be an incorruptible covenant to you, forever before the Lord, for you and your offspring with you. And the Lord spoke to Aaron: You shall possess nothing in their land, nor have any portion among them; for I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel. But to the children of Levi I have given all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance for their service which they do for me in the Tabernacle of Testimony. Let the children of Israel from now on not come near the Tabernacle of Testimony, lest they bring sin upon themselves and die. But the Levites shall perform the service in the Tabernacle of Testimony, and they shall bear their own iniquity, as a perpetual right among your descendants. And they shall possess no inheritance among the children of Israel: For the tithes of the children of Israel, which they lift up as a heave offering to the Lord, I have given to the Levites as an inheritance. Therefore I have said to them that they shall possess no inheritance among the children of Israel. And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying: Tell the Levites and speak to them: When you take the tithe from the children of Israel which I have given to you from them as your inheritance, then you shall make a heave offering from it to the Lord, which is a tenth of the tithe. And you shall account such a heave offering as if it were grain from the barn and the fullness from the winepress. Thus you shall also give the heave offering to the Lord from all your tithes which you take from the children of Israel, which you give as such a heave offering of the Lord to Aaron the Priest. From everything that is given to you, you shall give to the Lord all kinds of heave offerings from <margin>Levit. 18. Num. 18. b. 19.</margin> the best that is sanctified from it. And speak to them: When you have thus heave-offered the best of it, it shall be reckoned to the Levites as the income of the barn and as the income of the winepress. And you may eat it in all places, you and your children. For it is your reward for your service in the Tabernacle of Testimony. So you shall bring no sin upon yourselves when you have heave-offered the best of it, and you shall not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, and not die.

1 And the Lord spoke with Moses, saying:

<margin>Exo. 29. g. 38. 1. Esdr. 3. a. 3. Hebr. 9. a. 6.</margin> 3 * These are the offerings which you shall offer to the Lord: Year-old lambs without blemish, two every day for a continual burnt offering,
4 One lamb in the morning, the other in the evening.
<margin>Nu. 15. a. 4.</margin> 5 And a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with pressed oil, of a fourth part of a hin <term>Hin: an ancient unit of liquid measure, roughly 1.5 gallons</term>.

7 And its drink offering, for each lamb, a fourth part of a hin.
8 In the sanctuary shall you pour out the wine of the drink offering to the Lord. The other lamb you shall offer in the evening; as the grain offering of the morning and its drink offering, for an offering of a sweet savor to the Lord.
9 And on the Sabbath day, two year-old lambs without blemish, and two tenths of fine flour for a grain offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering.
10 This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, besides the continual burnt offering with its drink offering.

### The xxx. Chapter.

<margin>
Num. 25:c.

<margin>
Regarding vows that are made by husband and wife.
Num. 23:21.
* Deut. 23:21.
</margin>
**A** 1 And Moses spoke with the heads of the tribes of the children of Israel, and said: This is what the Lord has commanded.
2 If a man makes any vow to the Lord or swears an oath, binding his soul, he shall not break his word; but shall do everything just as it has come out of his mouth.
3 If a woman makes a vow to the Lord and binds herself while she is still in her father's house and in her youth <note>literally: "maechdom" or maidenhood</note>,
4 And her vow and the bond that she makes over her soul comes before her father, and he remains silent, then all her vows shall stand, and every bond with which she has bound her soul shall stand.
5 But if her father forbids her on the day that he hears it, then no vow or bond with which she has bound her soul shall stand. And the Lord shall be gracious to her, because her father forbade her.
6 But if she has a husband, and has a vow upon her, or a bond escaped from her lips over her soul,
7 And the husband hears it and remains silent on that same day, then her vow and bond with which she bound her soul shall stand.
8 But if her husband forbids her on the day that he hears it, then her vow which she had upon her is void, along with the bond she let go from her lips over her soul; and the Lord shall be gracious to her.
9 The vow of a widow and of her that is divorced—everything with which they bind their souls—that shall stand for them.
10 If someone's household <note>referring specifically to a wife or dependent</note> makes a vow or binds themselves with an oath over their soul,
11 And the master of the house <note>the husband</note> hears it and remains silent and does not turn against it, then every vow is of value, and everything with which they bound themselves.
12 But if the master of the house makes it void on the day he hears it, then what went out of the lips is of no value, whether it was a vow or a bond over the soul; for the master of the house has made it void, and the Lord shall be gracious to him.
13 And every vow and oath with which one binds oneself to chastise the body, the master of the house may confirm or break.
14 Thus: when he remains silent from one day to the next...

<margin>Regarding the cities of the Levites. Joshua 21:1, 4.</margin>
1 And the Lord spoke to Moses on the plains of the Moabites by the Jordan across from Jericho, saying: 2 Command the children of Israel that they give the Levites cities from their inheritance so that they may live in them. 3 Additionally, you shall also give the Levites the suburbs <note>original: "voorsteden," referring to the pasture lands surrounding a city</note> around the cities, so that they may live in the cities and have their cattle, goods, and all kinds of animals in the suburbs. 4 And the width of the suburbs which you shall give the Levites shall be one thousand cubits <note>An "el" or cubit is a unit of measure based on the length of the forearm, roughly 18 inches or 45 centimeters.</note> outward from the city walls all around. 5 So you shall now measure outside the city, on the side toward the East, two thousand cubits. And on the side toward the South, two thousand cubits. And on the side toward the West, two thousand cubits. And on the side toward the North, two thousand cubits, so that the city is in the middle. These shall be their suburbs. 6 And among the cities that you shall give the
<margin>Exodus 21:13; Joshua 20:1; Deuteronomy 19:2.</margin>
Levites, you shall give six cities of refuge <note>original: "vrijsteden," sanctuary cities where a person could seek legal protection</note> so that anyone who has committed manslaughter may flee there. Above these same ones, you shall give another forty-two cities. 8 So all the cities that you give the Levites shall be forty-eight in total, with their suburbs. And you shall give more from those who possess much among the children of Israel, and fewer from those who possess little. <margin>Exodus 21:13; Deuteronomy 19:2.</margin>
ing: 11 Speak with the children of Israel and say to them: When you come over the Jordan into the land of Canaan, you shall choose cities to be cities of refuge, so that he who commits manslaughter unawares <note>original: "onuersiens," meaning accidentally or without intent</note> may flee there. And 
<margin>Cities of Refuge.</margin>
such cities of refuge shall be among you for protection from the blood-avenger <note>original: "bloet-wreecker," the victim's relative who had the traditional right to seek retribution</note>, so that he who has committed manslaughter does not have to die until he has stood for trial before the assembly. 13 And the cities that you shall give shall be six cities of refuge. 14 Three you shall give on this side of the Jordan, and three in the land of Canaan. <margin>Cities of Refuge.</margin>
[1] When the Lord your God has rooted out the nations whose land the Lord your God shall give you, and you take it and live in their cities and houses, <margin>4.g.41. 2 34.b.11 18.a.3 2</margin> [2] then you shall set aside three cities for yourself in the land that the Lord your God gives you to possess. [5] As when someone goes into the forest with his neighbor to chop wood, <margin>If killing is not intentional, they may flee.</margin> and as his hand swings the axe to cut down the wood, the iron head slips from the handle and strikes his neighbor so that he dies; he shall flee into one of these cities so that he may stay alive. [6] Otherwise, the <term>avenger of blood: a relative of the deceased who had the legal right to seek justice</term> might pursue the manslayer while his heart is hot with anger and overtake him because the way is so far, and strike him dead, even though he was not deserving of death, since he had no previous hatred for him.

### The 12th Chapter.

1 There was also a man, a kinsman of Naomi's husband, of the family of Elimelech, named Boaz, who was a <term>worthy man<gloss>a person of standing, wealth, and character</gloss></term>.
2 And Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi: "Let me go into the field and glean ears of grain after him in whose sight I find favor." And she said to her: "Go then, my daughter."
3 She went out, came, and gleaned in the field behind the reapers. And it happened by chance that this very field belonged to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.
4 And behold, Boaz came just then from Bethlehem and said to the reapers: "The Lord be with you." They answered: "The Lord bless you."
5 Then Boaz said to his <margin>*Servant</margin> servant who was set over the reapers: "Whose girl is this?"
6 The young man who was set over the reapers answered and said: "This is the Moabitish girl who came back with Naomi from the land of the Moabites;
7 For she said: 'Please let me glean and gather among the sheaves behind the reapers.' And so she came and has stood there from this morning until now, and stayed only a little while in the house."
<margin>Boaz speaks with Ruth.</margin>
8 Then Boaz said to Ruth: "Do you hear me, my daughter? You shall not go to glean in any other field, nor go away from here. But keep close to my young women,
9 And watch where they reap in the field and follow after them. I have commanded my young men that no one shall touch you. And if you are thirsty, go to the vessels and drink from what my young men draw."
10 Then she fell on her face and bowed to the earth, and said to him: "How have I found such favor in your eyes that you should take notice of me, seeing I am a stranger?"
11 Boaz answered and said to her: "I have been fully told all that you have done for your husband’s mother since the death of your husband; how you have left your father and mother and the land of your birth, and have come to a people that you did not know before.
12 The Lord repay your deed, and may your reward be full from the Lord God of Israel, to whom you have come to take refuge under his wings."
13 She said: "Let me find favor in your eyes, my lord, for you have comforted me and spoken kindly to your maidservant, though I am not even like one of your own servants."
14 Boaz said to her: "When it is mealtime, come here and eat of the bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar." And she sat beside the reapers. And he reached out parched grain to her. And she ate and was satisfied, and had some left over.
15 And when she rose up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying: "Let her also glean among the sheaves, and do not shame her.
16 Also let some fall on purpose from the bundles and leave it for her to glean, and do not rebuke her for it."
17 So she gleaned in the field until evening, and beat out what she had gleaned, and it was about an <term>epha<gloss>an ancient Hebrew dry measure, roughly equivalent to 22 liters or a bushel</gloss></term> of barley.
<margin>Ruth returns again from the field.</margin>
18 And she took it up and came into the city; and her husband's mother saw what she had gleaned. Moreover, she brought forth and gave to her what she had kept from her meal after she was satisfied.

<column-break/>

19 Then her husband's mother said to her: "Where have you gleaned today, and where have you worked? Blessed be he who took notice of you." And she told her husband's mother with whom she had worked, and said: "The man's name with whom I worked today is Boaz."
20 And Naomi said to her daughter-in-law: "Blessed be he by the Lord, for he has not withheld his kindness both to the living and to the dead." And Naomi said to her: "This man is a close relative of ours, <margin>Deuteronomy 25a</margin> and is our <term>heir<gloss>original: "Erfgenaem"; refers to the 'Go'el' or kinsman-redeemer who had the right to buy back family land and marry a childless widow</gloss></term>."
21 Ruth the Moabitess said: "He also said to me: 'You shall keep close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.'"
22 Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law: "It is better, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, so that no one meets you in another field."
23 Thus she kept close to the young women of Boaz to glean, until the end of the barley harvest and the wheat harvest; and she lived with her husband's mother.

**B**oaz went up to the gate and waited there. And behold, when the kinsman-redeemer <note>original: "erfgenaem" – in biblical law, the relative responsible for buying back family land and marrying a childless widow</note> passed by, Boaz spoke with him and said: "Come and sit down here, friend." 3 Then he said to the kinsman-redeemer: "Naomi, who has come back from the land of the Moabites, is offering for sale the piece of land that belonged to our 4 brother Elimelech. Therefore I thought to bring it to your attention and say: 'If you wish to inherit this, buy it before the citizens and before the elders of my people. But if you do not wish to inherit it, tell me so that I may know; for there is no kinsman-redeemer but you, and I am after you.'" He said: "I will redeem it." Boaz said: "On the 5 day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you must also take Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the deceased, so that you may raise up a name for the 6 deceased upon his inheritance." Then he said: "I cannot inherit it, lest I perhaps ruin my own inheritance. You inherit what I should inherit, for I 7 cannot inherit it." But there was of old such a custom in Israel: when someone did not wish to inherit or buy a property, so that 8 all matters would be settled, he pulled off his shoe and gave it to the other. That was the testimony in Israel. And the kinsman-redeemer said to Boaz: "You buy it," and he pulled 9 off his shoe. And Boaz said to the elders and to all the people: "You are witnesses today that I have bought all that belonged to Elimelech, and all that belonged to Chilion and 10 Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi. Moreover, I take Ruth the Moabitess, Mahlon's wife, as a wife, so that I may raise up a name for the deceased upon his inheritance, and that his name may not be cut off from among his brothers or from the gates of his place. 11 You are witnesses of this today." When he came to him, he said to him: "There were two men in a city, the one rich, the other poor. 2 The rich man had very many sheep and cattle, 3 But the poor man had nothing more than one single small ewe lamb that he had bought, and he nourished it so that it grew up with him and with his children together. It ate of his morsel and drank from his cup and slept in his 4 lap, and he held it like a daughter. But when a guest came to the rich man, he spared taking from his own sheep and cattle to prepare something for the guest who had come to him, and took the poor man's lamb and prepared it for the man who 5 had come to him." Then David burned with great anger against that man and said to Nathan: "As surely as the Lord lives, the man who has done this is a child of 6 death <note>original: "kint des doots," meaning he deserves to die</note>. Moreover, he shall pay for the lamb fourfold because he has done such a thing and has not spared." <margin>1 Samuel 16:13</margin> 7 Then Nathan said to David: "You are the man." Thus says the Lord the God of Israel: "I anointed you as king over Israel and I delivered you out of the hand 8 of Saul, and I gave you your master's house, moreover his wives into your lap, and I gave you the house of Israel and Judah. And if that were too little, I would have done 9 this and that more for you. Why have you despised the word of the Lord, that you did such evil in His eyes? You have struck down Uriah the Hittite with the <margin>2 Samuel 10, 17</margin> 10 sword; you have taken his wife to be your wife. But him you have killed with the sword of the children of Ammon. Now therefore, the sword

shall never depart from your house because you have despised Me and have taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite so 11 that she might be your wife." Thus says the Lord: "Behold, I will raise up misfortune over you from your own house, and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, so that he shall sleep with your wives 12 in the light of the sun. And David saw that his servants were whispering, and perceived that the child was dead, and said to his servants: "Is the child 20 dead?" They said: "Yes." He said: "For the child's sake I fasted and wept while he lived, for I thought: 'Who knows whether the Lord will be gracious to me, so that the child may remain alive?' But 23 now that he is dead, why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I shall indeed go to him, but he shall not return to me." 24 And when David had comforted his wife Bathsheba, he went in to her and slept with her. And he took the crown of their king from his head, which weighed a talent <note>original: "Centner," a unit of weight</note> of gold and had precious stones, and it was 31 placed on David's head, and he carried away much spoil from the city. But the people who were within he brought out and put them under iron <margin>1 Chronicles 21:3-4</margin> saws and harrows and iron axes, and burned them in brick kilns. Thus he did to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

1 <margin>2 Samuel 15:34</margin> <margin>Ahithophel gives counsel.</margin> And Ahithophel said to Absalom: "I will choose twelve thousand men, and set out, and pursue David tonight, 2 and I will overtake him while he is weary and weak. Furthermore, your father is a man of war, and will not rest with the people. 9 See, he is perhaps hidden now in some pit or elsewhere. If it should happen that the first attack goes poorly, and a rumor and report should come: 'A slaughter has occurred among the people following Absalom,' 10 then every man's heart would melt, even those who are otherwise warriors and have hearts like lions. For all Israel knows that your father is strong, and the warriors who are with him. 11 But this I advise: that you gather all Israel to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as many as the sand by the sea, and that you in person go with them. 12 Then we will fall upon him in whatever place we find him, and we will come over him as the dew falls upon the earth, so that we leave not even one of him or all his men.
