### The xxiii. Chapter.

<margin>The last words of David.</margin>
1 These are the last words of David. David the son of Jesse spoke: The man who is assured of the Messiah <note>original: "Messia"; referring here to the "Anointed One" of God</note> of the God of Jacob, lovely with the Psalms of Israel, spoke:
2 The spirit of the Lord has spoken through me, and his word was spoken through my mouth.
3 The God of Jacob has spoken to me. The Strong One of Israel has spoken, the righteous Ruler among men, the Ruler in the fear of God.
4 And like the light of the morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, so that from the shining after the rain the grass grows out of the earth.
<margin>2 Samuel 7:c, 11.</margin>
5 For my house is not so with God, for he has made a covenant with me that is eternal, and altogether well-ordered and kept. For all my salvation and all my desire is that which does not grow. <note>David reflects on the stability of God's promise compared to the fleeting nature of earthly growth.</note>
6 But the sons of Belial <note>original: "Belial"; a term used in the Bible to describe the wicked, worthless, or lawless</note> are all like discarded thistles, which one cannot take up with the hands.
7 But whoever shall touch them must have iron and spear-shafts in hand. And they shall be burned with fire in their dwelling.
<margin>David’s Heroes. 1 Chronicles 12:b, 10. Jashobeam.</margin>
8 These are the names of David’s heroes: Jashobeam <note>original: "Jasabeam"</note>, the son of Hachmoni, the chief among the three. He lifted up his spear and slew eight hundred at one time.
<margin>Eleazar.</margin>
9 After him was Eleazar, the son of Dodo, the son of Ahohi, among the three heroes with David when they defied the Philistines and were gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel went up.
10 Then he stood and struck the Philistines until his hand was weary and grew stiff to the sword. And the Lord gave a great victory at that time, so that the people turned back after him only to plunder.
<margin>Victory.</margin>
<margin>Shammah.</margin>
11 After him was Shammah, the son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines gathered in a village where there was a piece of field full of lentils <note>original: "wicken"; referring to vetch or lentils</note>, and the people fled from the Philistines.
12 Then he stepped into the middle of that field and delivered it, and struck the Philistines. And God gave a great victory.
<margin>1 Chronicles 12:b, 15</margin>
13 And these three chiefs among the thirty went down in the harvest to David in the cave of Adullam, and the army of the Philistines lay in the valley of Rephaim.
14 And David was at that time in the stronghold. But the Philistines' garrison was at Bethlehem.
15 And David felt a longing and said: "Who will fetch me a drink of the water from the well at Bethlehem, by the gate?"
<margin>The heroes draw water at Bethlehem by the gate.</margin>

17 and said: "May the Lord keep me from doing this. Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives and went there?" And he would not drink it. These things did those three heroes.

19 and the most glorious among the three, and was their captain; but he did not attain to the first three.

### The 7th Chapter.

<margin>Of the building of Solomon's house.</margin>
1. But Solomon was building his own house for thirteen years until he had completely finished it.
2. Specifically, he built a house of the Forest of Lebanon, a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. Upon this four-sided structure, he laid the ceiling of cedar boards upon rows of cedar columns.
3. And above that, a roof of cedar upon the same columns, of which there were forty-five, being fifteen in each row.
4. And there were windows in three rows, facing one another, three against three; and the doorframes were four-sided.
5. He also made a porch of columns, fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. And another porch stood before it with columns and thick beams.
6. He also built a porch for a Judgment Seat <note>original: "Richtstoel" — Solomon's throne room where he dispensed justice.</note>, where he held court, and paneled both the ceilings with cedar.
7. Furthermore, his own house where he lived, in the rear court behind the porch, was made in the same manner.
<margin>1 Kings 3:1</margin>
8. And he also made a house like that porch for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Solomon had taken as his wife.

10. The foundations were also of costly and large stones, ten and eight cubits in size.
11. And above them were costly stones hewn to measure, and cedar beams.

# Abijam. Asa. The First Book <note>The First Book of Kings.</note>

<margin>2 Sam. 11:4</margin>
...pleased the Lord well, and had not turned away from all that He commanded him throughout his life, except only in the matter concerning Uriah <note>original: "Ozia," a common early variant for Uriah</note> the Hittite. But there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all his life.

<margin>Abijam dies.</margin>
But as for what more there is to say of Abijam, and all that he did, behold, is that not written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah? There was also war between Abijam and Jeroboam. And Abijam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And Asa his son became King in his place.

<margin>Asa becomes King.</margin>
In the twentieth year of King Jeroboam over Israel, Asa became King in Judah, and reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Maacah, a daughter of Abishalom.

<margin>2 Chron. 14:1</margin>
And Asa did that which well pleased the Lord, just like his father David.

<margin>1 Kings 22:47</margin>
And he drove the male cult prostitutes <note>original: "Hoereerders," referring to ritual prostitutes or sodomites</note> out of the land, and took away all the idols that his fathers had made.

<margin>2 Chron. 15:16</margin>
Furthermore, he also removed his mother Maacah from her office, because she had made an abominable idol <term>Niphezeth: an old Dutch rendering of the Hebrew word for a "horrific" or "shameful" idol, likely an Asherah pole</term> in a grove. And Asa rooted out her idol and burned it by the brook Kidron. But the high places were not taken away; nevertheless, Asa’s heart was upright before the Lord all his life. And the silver and gold, and the vessels that his father had sanctified, and all that was sanctified for the house of the Lord, he brought back into it. And there was strife between Asa and Baasha the King of Israel all their lives.

<margin>2 Chron. 16:1</margin>
<margin>Baasha marches against Judah.</margin>
Baasha the King of Israel marched up against Judah and built up Ramah, so that no one could go out or come in on the side of Asa the King of Judah. Then Asa took all the silver and gold that was left in the treasury of the house of the Lord and in the treasury of the King’s house, and gave it into the hands of his servants, and sent it to Ben-hadad the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, the King of Syria, who dwelt at Damascus, saying:

<margin>Asa sends gifts to Ben-hadad.</margin>
<margin>1 Kings 20:1</margin>
"There is a covenant between me and you, and between my father and your father. Therefore, I send you a gift of silver and gold, so that you might break the covenant that you have with Baasha the King of Israel, so that he may withdraw from me."

Ben-hadad gave ear to King Asa and sent his captains against the cities of Israel, and struck Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maacah, and all of Chinnereth, along with the entire land of Naphtali.

When Baasha heard this, he stopped building Ramah and withdrew back to Tirzah.

But King Asa issued a proclamation throughout all Judah: "No one shall remain unpunished <note>meaning no one was exempt from service</note>." And they took away the stones and the wood of Ramah with which Baasha had been building. And King Asa used them to build Geba of Benjamin and Mizpah.

But as for what more there is to say of Asa, and all his power, and all that he did, and the cities that he built, behold, that is written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah. Except that in his old age, he was diseased in his feet.

<margin>Asa dies.</margin>

But Nadab the son of Jeroboam became King over Israel in the second year of Asa, King of Judah, and reigned over Israel for two years.

<column-break/>

had caused Israel to sin. But Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines. For Nadab and all Israel were besieging Gibbethon.

Thus Baasha killed him in the third year of Asa, King of Judah, and became King in his place.

<margin>1 Kings 14:14</margin>
Now as soon as he was King, he struck the entire house of Jeroboam, and left nothing remaining that had breath <note>original: "pet dat Adem had," literally 'that which had breath'</note> of Jeroboam's line, until he had destroyed them according to the word of the Lord, which He had spoken through His servant Ahijah of Shiloh; because of the sins of Jeroboam which he committed, and with which he caused Israel to sin, and by the provocation with which he angered the Lord God of Israel.

But as for what more there is to say of Nadab, and all that he did, behold, is that not written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel? And there was war between Asa and Baasha, the King of Israel, all their lives.

In the third year of Asa, King of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah became King over all Israel at Tirzah for twenty-four years. And he did what displeased the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam and in his sins, with which he caused Israel to sin.

Then the word of the Lord came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying:

<margin>God foretells evil against the house of Baasha.</margin>
"Because I raised you up out of the dust and made you a Prince over my people Israel, yet you walk in the way of Jeroboam and make my people Israel sin, to provoke me with their sins; behold, I will take away the descendants of Baasha and the descendants of his house, and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

<margin>1 Kings 14:11</margin>
Whoever of Baasha's line dies in the city, the dogs shall eat; and whoever of his dies in the field, the birds of the heaven shall eat."

But as for what more there is to say of Baasha, and what he did, and his power, behold, is that not written in the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel?

And Baasha slept with his fathers and was buried at Tirzah.

<margin>Baasha dies.</margin>
And his son Elah became King in his place. The word of the Lord also came through the Prophet Jehu, the son of Hanani, against Baasha and against his house, because of all the evil that he did before the Lord to provoke Him through the works of his hands, so that it should become like the house of Jeroboam, and because he had struck it down.

### The XVI. Chapter.

<margin>Elah becomes King.</margin>
**In** the twenty-sixth year of Asa, King of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha became King over Israel at Tirzah for two years. But his servant Zimri, the commander over half of the chariots, conspired against him. While he was at Tirzah, drinking and getting drunk in the house of Arza, the steward at Tirzah,

Zimri came in and struck him dead, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa, King of Judah, and became King in his place.

And when he was King and sat upon his throne, he struck the entire house of Baasha and left no one remaining—not even one who pisses against a wall <note>A literal Biblical idiom for any male person</note>—including his heirs and his friends.

10 He spoke: I have been very zealous for the Lord God of Sabaoth <note>Lord of Hosts</note>. For the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, broken your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword; and I alone am left, and they seek to take my life.
11 He spoke: Go out, and stand upon the mountain before the Lord. And behold, the Lord went by, and a great, strong wind that tore the mountains and broke the rocks before the Lord. But the Lord was not in the wind. After the wind came an earthquake. But the Lord was not in that earthquake.
12 And after the earthquake came a fire: but the Lord was not in the fire. And after that fire came a still, soft whistling <note>The "still small voice"</note>.
13 When Elijah heard that, he covered his face with his mantle, and went out and stood in the entrance of the cave. And behold, then came a voice to him and spoke: What do you have to do here, Elijah?

And he took the same mantle of Elijah that had fallen from him and struck the water and spoke: "Where is now the Lord, the God of Elijah?" And he struck the water. Then it divided to both sides, and Elisha went through.
15 And when the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him from the opposite side, they said: "The spirit of Elijah rests upon Elisha," and they went to meet him and bowed 16 to the earth, and spoke to him: "Behold, there are among your servants fifty strong men; let them go and seek your master, perhaps the spirit of the Lord has taken him and cast him upon some mountain or into a valley." But he spoke: 17 "Do not let them go." But they urged him until he was weary <note>original: "ommoedich schelde," meaning he was embarrassed or worn down by their persistence</note> and spoke: "Let them go." And they sent fifty men and they sought him for three days, but they did not find him. And 18 they came back to Elisha. And he remained in Jericho and spoke to them: "Did I not say to you that 19 you should not go?" And the men of the city spoke to Elisha: "Behold, it is good to dwell in this city, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land is barren."
20 He spoke: "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." And they brought it to him. 21 Then he went out to the spring of the waters and threw the salt into it and spoke: "Thus says the Lord: I have made this water healthy. From now on, neither death nor barrenness shall come from it." 22 Thus the water became healthy to this day, according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.
23 And he went up from there to Bethel. And as he was going up the road, little boys <note>original: "cleyne knechtkens," can refer to children or young men</note> came out of the city and mocked him and spoke to him: "Baldhead, come up! Baldhead, 24 come up!" And he turned around. And when he saw them, he cursed them in the name of the Lord. Then two bears came out of the woods and tore forty-two of the children. 25 From there he went to Mount Carmel and returned from there to Samaria.

Heathens <note>Referring to the foreign peoples resettled in Samaria by the Assyrians.</note> served the Lord, and yet also served their idols. Their children and grandchildren did the same, just as their fathers had done, even unto this day.

1 In the third year of Hoshea, the son of Elah, King of Israel, Hezekiah, the son of Ahaz, King of Judah, became King.

# Solomon. The Second Book.

<margin>Wisdom 9:7</margin>
9 Now, O Lord God, let your word to my father David be proven true, for you have made me King over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.
<margin>1 Kings 3:9 <note>original: "3.Reg.3.b.9." - Older Bibles often labeled the books of Samuel and Kings as 1-4 Kings.</note></margin>
10 Therefore, give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people. For who can judge this, your great people?
<margin>1 Kings 3:11. God hears Solomon's prayer and gives him more than he asks.</margin>
11 Then God spoke to Solomon: "Because you had this in your mind, and have not asked for riches, nor for wealth, nor for honor, nor for the lives of your enemies, nor have you asked for a long life; but have asked for wisdom and knowledge, so that you might judge my people over whom I have made you King:
<margin>1 Kings 4:29. Wisdom 7:11.</margin>
12 I will grant you wisdom and knowledge. And I will also give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings before you have had, nor shall any after you possess the like."
13 So Solomon came from the high place that was at Gibeon to Jerusalem, from the tent of testimony, and reigned over Israel.
<margin>1 Kings 4:26. Regarding Solomon's riches.</margin>
14 And Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen, so that he brought together one thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, and stationed them in the chariot cities and with the King at Jerusalem.
15 And the King made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars as plentiful as the sycamore-fig trees in the lowlands.
16 And horses were brought to Solomon from Egypt and all kinds of wares. The King’s merchants bought these same wares and brought them from Egypt,
17 each chariot for six hundred silverlings <note>likely shekels of silver</note>, and a stallion for one hundred and fifty. In this way, they also brought them for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Syria.

### The 2nd Chapter.

<margin>Regarding Solomon's workmen.</margin>
1 And Solomon began to build a house for the Name of the Lord, and a house for his kingdom.
2 And he counted out seventy thousand men for the burdens, and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred officers over them.
<margin>1 Kings 5:2-3.</margin>
3 And Solomon sent word to Huram <note>Also known as Hiram</note>, the King of Tyre, saying: "As you dealt with my father David, and sent him cedars to build him a house to dwell in, [so do also with me.]
<margin>2 Samuel 5:11. Solomon sends to Huram.</margin>
4 Behold, I wish to build a house to the Name of the Lord my God, that it may be sanctified to him, to burn sweet incense before him, and to continually prepare the showbread, and burnt offerings in the morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, and New Moons, and on the feasts of the Lord our God, forever for Israel.
5 And the house that I wish to build shall be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
<margin>1 Kings 8:27. Isaiah 66:1.</margin>
6 But who is able to build him a house? || For the heaven, and the heaven of all heavens, cannot contain him. Who would I then be, that I should build him a house, except only that one might burn incense before him?
7 Therefore, send me now a wise man to work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, scarlet, rose-red, and yellow silk, and who knows how to engrave with the wise men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
8 Also send me cedars, firs, and ebony wood from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the wood on Lebanon. And behold, my servants shall be with your servants,
9 so that much wood may be prepared for me. For the house that I wish to build shall be great and wonderful.
10 And behold, I will give to the craftsmen, your servants who cut the wood, twenty

11 Then Huram the King of Tyre spoke through writings and sent them to Solomon: "Because the Lord loves his people, he has made you King over them."
12 And Huram spoke further: "Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, who made Heaven and Earth, that he has given King David a wise, clever, and understanding son, who would build a house for the Lord and a house for his kingdom.

He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, scarlet, yellow silk, linen, and rose-red, and to engrave all sorts of things, and to skillfully make whatever is set before him, with your wise men and with the wise men of my lord King David, your father.

### Chapter 4.

1 <margin>1 Chronicles 29:1. The metal altar.</margin> He also made a metal altar, twenty cubits long and wide, and ten cubits high.
2 <margin>1 Kings 7:23</margin> And he made a molten sea <note>A massive bronze basin used for ritual washing.</note>, ten cubits wide from one rim to the other, perfectly round, and five cubits high. And a line of thirty cubits could encompass it round about.
3 And figures of oxen were under it all around. For every ten cubits, there were two rows of buds around the sea (which was ten cubits wide) that were cast with it.
4 <margin>on twelve oxen.</margin> But it stood upon those twelve oxen. Three were turned toward the North, three toward the West, three toward the South, and three toward the East; and the sea was set on top of them, and all their hindquarters were turned inward.
5 Its thickness was a handbreadth, and its rim was like the rim of a cup, like an open rose; it held three thousand baths <note>A "bath" was a liquid measure of approximately 22 liters.</note>.
6 <margin>1 Kings 7:38. Then ten basins.</margin> And he made ten basins; he set five on the right side and five on the left, to wash in them everything that belonged to the burnt offering, so they might rinse them there. But the sea was for the priests to wash in.
7 <margin>Then ten lampstands.</margin> He also made ten golden lampstands, as they were required to be, and he placed them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left side.
8 <margin>Then ten tables, and also a court for the priests.</margin> And he made ten tables and set them in the temple, five on the right and five on the left side. And he made a hundred golden bowls.
9 He also made a court for the priests and a large outer court, and the doors for that court, and overlaid the doors with metal.
10 And he set the sea on the right corner, toward the Southeast.
11 And Huram made the pots, shovels, and bowls. So Huram finished the work that he did for King Solomon on the house of God:
12 <margin>1 Kings 7:15.</margin> Namely, the two columns, with the bowls and the capitals on top of both columns, and the two braided wreaths to cover both bowls of the capitals on top of the columns;
13 <margin>A summary of the metal works.</margin> And the four hundred pomegranates on both braided wreaths, two rows of pomegranates on each wreath, to cover both bowls of the capitals that were on top of the columns.
14 <margin>A Sea.</margin> He also made the stands, and the basins on the stands;
15 and one sea, and twelve oxen under it.
16 Additionally, the pots, shovels, meat-hooks, and all their vessels, Huram-Abiff <note>The master craftsman sent by the King of Tyre.</note> made for King Solomon for the house of the Lord, out of polished metal.
17 In the plain of the Jordan, the King had them cast in clay ground, between Succoth and Zeredah.
18 And Solomon made a great many of all these vessels, so that

<column-break/>

the weight of the metal could not be known.
19 And Solomon made all the furniture for the house of God, namely, the <margin>Exodus 25:30.</margin> golden altar, the tables, and the showbread <note>The "bread of the presence" kept on the table in the sanctuary.</note> upon them,
20 the lampstands with their lamps <margin>Leviticus 24:5.</margin> of pure gold, that they should burn before the sanctuary, as was required.
21 And the flowers on the lamps, and the snuffs were of gold; that was all of solid gold.
22 Moreover, the knives, bowls, spoons, and basins were of pure gold. And the entrance and its inner doors to the Most Holy Place, and the doors to the house of the temple, were golden. Thus all the work that Solomon did for the house of the Lord was finished.

### Chapter 5.

1 <margin>1 Kings 7:51</margin> Then Solomon brought in everything that his father David had dedicated, namely, the silver and the gold, and all kinds of furniture, and placed them in the treasures of the house of God.
2 <margin>1 Kings 8:1</margin> Then Solomon gathered all the elders in Israel, all the heads of the tribes, and the princes of the fathers among the children of Israel in Jerusalem, that they might bring up the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, which is Zion.
3 And all the men of Israel gathered themselves to the King at the feast <note>to bring the temple [into use]</note>, which is in the seventh month.
4 And all the elders of Israel came. And the Levites took up the Ark,
5 and they brought it up with the Tabernacle of the Testimony, and all the holy furniture that was in the Tabernacle.
6 And the priests and the Levites brought them up. But King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel gathered to him before the Ark, sacrificed sheep and oxen, so many that no one could count or reckon them.
7 Thus the priests brought the Ark of the Covenant of the Lord to its place in the sanctuary of the house, the most glorious part in the Most Holy Place, under the wings of the Cherubim.
8 For the Cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the Ark, and the Cherubim covered the Ark and its poles from above.
9 The poles were so long that their ends were seen far from the Ark, before the sanctuary, but they were not seen from outside.
10 <margin>1 Kings 8:9</margin> And it has been there to this day. And there was nothing in the Ark except the two tablets <margin>Deuteronomy 10:5</margin> which Moses had put therein at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the children of Israel when they came out of Egypt.
11 And it happened, when the priests came out of the holy place (for all the priests who were present had sanctified themselves, so that their divisions were not observed),
12 and the Levites, with all those under Asaph, Heman, Jedithun, and their sons and brothers who were singers, dressed in fine linen, sang with lutes, cymbals, psalteries, and harps. And they stood toward the East of the altar, and with them a hundred and twenty priests who blew with trumpets.
13 And it was as if it were only one who trumpeted and sang, as if one voice were heard, to praise and thank the Lord. And when the voice was lifted up with the trumpets, cymbals, and other musical instruments, and with strings, in that praise of the Lord: "that He is good and that His mercy endures forever."
14 <margin>Exodus 40:34. Ezekiel 9:3.</margin> Then the house of the Lord was filled with a cloud, so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud. For the glory of the Lord filled the house of God.

<header>Release from Captivity. Ezra.</header>

<margin>Cyrus releases the captives of Judah to return to Jerusalem and to build the Temple. Isaiah 45:1.</margin>
2 Cyrus the King of Persia says: The Lord the God of Heaven has given me all the kingdoms in the land, and he has commanded me to build him a house at Jerusalem in Judah. Whoever now among you is of his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem in Judah, and build that house of the Lord the God of Israel. He is the God who is in Jerusalem.

4 And whoever remains, in every place where he is a stranger, let the people of his place help him with silver and gold, goods and cattle, out of free will, for the house of God in Jerusalem.

<margin>The people set out to build the Temple.</margin>
5 Then the chief fathers of Judah and Benjamin arose, and the Priests and the Levites, all whose spirit God stirred to go up and build the house of the Lord in Jerusalem. 

6 And all those who were around them strengthened their hands with silver and golden vessels, with goods and cattle, and precious things, besides all that they gave voluntarily.

8 But Cyrus the King of Persia brought them out by Mithredath the treasurer, and numbered them to <term>Sheshbazzar <note>original: Sefbazar. A name used for the prince of Judah, often identified with Zerubbabel or a high official.</note></term> the Prince of Judah.

# The Book

## The first Chapter.

<margin>1</margin> These are the chronicles of Nehemiah, the son of Hachaliah: It happened in the month of Chisleu <note>Chisleu corresponds to parts of November and December</note>, in the twentieth year, that I was in the castle at Shushan <note>Also known as Susa, a capital of the Persian Empire</note>. <margin>2</margin> Then Hanani, one of my brothers, came with some men from Judah. And I asked them how it went with the Jews who had escaped and remained from the captivity, and how things stood in Jerusalem.

<margin>3</margin><margin>Isaiah 25:10, Psalm 36:19</margin> And they said to me: Those remaining from the captivity there in the land are in great misfortune and reproach. The walls of Jerusalem are broken down, and its gates burned with fire. <margin>4</margin> When I heard such words, I sat and wept, and mourned for two days long, and fasted, and prayed before <margin>Nehemiah prays with fasting. 2 Esdras 9:32, Daniel 9:4, Exodus 20:5, Deuteronomy 7:9.</margin> the God of Heaven, and said: <margin>5</margin> Oh Lord God of Heaven, you great and terrible God, who keeps the covenant and mercy for those who love him and keep his commandments. <margin>6</margin> Let your eyes now notice, and your eyes be open, that you may hear the prayer of your servant, which I now pray before you day and night, for the children of Israel your servants, and confess the sins of the children of Israel which we have committed against you. Both I and my <margin>7</margin> father’s house have also sinned. We have become corrupt, in that we have not kept the commandments, decrees, and laws which you commanded your servant <margin>8</margin> Moses. But remember the word that you commanded your servant Moses, saying: <margin>Deuteronomy 30:1, 2; Psalm 6:37.</margin> If you transgress, I will scatter you among the <margin>9</margin> nations. But if it be that you turn back to me, and keep my commandments and do them—even if you were cast out to the ends of the heavens—I will yet gather you from there and will bring you to the place that I have chosen, so that <margin>10</margin> my name might dwell there. They are <margin>Exodus 14:30.</margin> surely your servants and your people, whom you have redeemed by your great power and mighty hand. <margin>11</margin> Oh Lord, let your ears notice the prayer of your servant, and the prayer of your servants who desire to fear your name. And let your servant succeed today, and give him mercy before this man. For I was the King’s Cupbearer.

And when I came to Jerusalem, and had been there for three days, I <margin>12</margin> arose in the night, and a few men with me. And they said: So let us rise up and we shall build; and their hands became courageous for the good. <margin>19</margin> But when Sanballat the Horonite, and Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab heard it, they mocked us and despised us, and said: What is this thing that you do? Will you rebel against the King again? <margin>20</margin> Then I answered them and said: The God of Heaven shall let us prosper, for we, his servants, have risen up and are building. But you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial in Jerusalem.

### The 5th Chapter.

<margin>The second complaint of the difficult time.</margin>
1 And there arose a great outcry of the people and of their wives against their brothers the Jews.

2 For there were some who said, "Our sons and our daughters are many; let us receive grain for them, so that we may eat and live."

3 But some said, "Let us mortgage <note>original: "verzetten"</note> our fields, vineyards, and houses, and receive grain for them during the famine."

4 And some said, "Let us borrow money for the King’s tribute <note>tax or land tax</note> upon our fields and vineyards.

5 For our brothers' flesh is as our flesh, and their children as our children. Otherwise, we would have to subject our sons and daughters to slavery <note>original: "dienst," meaning service or bondage</note>; and indeed, some of our daughters are already subjected, and there is no power in our hands to stop it. Also, our fields and vineyards now belong to others."

<margin>Usury forbidden.</margin>
6 But when I heard their outcry and such words, I became very angry.

7 And my heart took counsel within me, and I rebuked the Councilors and the leaders, and spoke to them: "Will you practice usury <note>charging excessive interest on loans</note> against one another?" And I gathered a great assembly against them.

<margin>Leviticus 22:25; Deuteronomy 23:19</margin>
8 And I said to them: "We have redeemed our brothers the Jews, who were sold to the heathens, according to our ability. And will you now even sell your brothers, whom we have bought back for ourselves?" Then they were silent and found nothing to answer.

9 And I said: "It is not good what you do. Should you not walk in the fear of God, because of the reproach of the heathens our enemies?

10 I and my brothers and my servants have also lent them money and grain, but let us leave off this usury.

11 Give back to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, and the hundredth part of the money, of the grain, of the wine, and of the oil that you have exacted from them as usury."

12 Then they said: "We will give it back, and will require nothing of them, and will do exactly as you have said." And I called the Priests and took an oath from them that they would do so.

13 I also shook out the fold of my garment <note>original: "boesem," referring to the pocket-like fold of a robe</note> and said: "So may God shake out every man from his house and from his labor who does not keep this word; let him be thus shaken out and emptied." And the whole assembly said, "Amen,"

<column-break/>

14 and praised the Lord. And the people did so. <margin>2 Esdras 2:1</margin> Also, from the time that I was appointed to be a Governor in the land of Judah—that is, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes <note>original: "Arthahsastha"</note>, which is twelve years—neither I nor my brothers ate the food provided for the Governor <note>the official food allowance or tax for the governor's table</note>.

15 For the former Governors who were before me had burdened the people, and had taken from them bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants behaved with violence toward the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.

16 I also labored on the work of the wall, and we bought no field. And all my servants were gathered there for the work.

17 Moreover, there were at my table one hundred and fifty of the Jews and rulers, besides those who came to us from the heathens who are around us.

18 And there was prepared for me daily one ox and six choice sheep, and birds. And every ten days, an abundance of all kinds of wine. Yet for all this, I did not demand the Governor's allowance, because the service was heavy upon this people.

### The 6th Chapter.

<margin>Sanballat against Nehemiah.</margin>
1 Now when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arabian, and our other enemies heard that I had built the wall and that there was no breach left in it (though at that time I had not yet hung the doors in the gates),

2 Sanballat and Geshem sent to me, saying, "Come, let us meet together in the villages on the plain of Ono." But they thought to do me harm.

3 But I sent messengers to them, saying: "I am doing a great work; I cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it and come down to you?"

4 They sent to me four times in this manner, and I answered them in the same way.

<margin>Sanballat writes to Nehemiah.</margin>
5 Then Sanballat sent his servant to me a fifth time with an open letter in his hand,

6 In which it was written: "It is reported among the heathens—and Geshem <note>original: "Gosem"</note> has said it—that you and the Jews intend to rebel. That is why you are building the wall, and you wish to be their King in these matters.

7 And you have appointed prophets to proclaim concerning you at Jerusalem, saying: 'He is the King of Judah.' And now this report will reach the King. So come now, and let us take counsel together."

8 But I sent to him, saying: "No such things as you say have happened; you have invented them out of your own heart."

# Esther.
### The first Chapter.

<margin>Esther 1:1.</margin>
**I**n the time of Ahasuerus, * who was King from India even unto Ethiopia <note>original: "Moren lant"; literally "land of the Moors," used historically for Ethiopia or Cush</note>, over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces. 2 And when he sat on his royal throne in the Citadel of Susa, 3 in the third year of his reign, he made a feast for all his princes and servants; namely, the powerful men of Persia and Media, the governors and nobles of his 4 provinces, so that he might show the glorious riches of his kingdom and the costly honor of his majesty for many days, namely, one hundred and eighty 5 days long. And when the days were completed, <margin>Regarding the great feast of Ahasuerus.</margin> the King made a feast for all the people who were in the Citadel of Susa, both great and small, for seven days, in the <margin>Courtyard.</margin> 6 garden of the court of the King’s house. There hung white, red, and yellow cloths, fastened with linen and purple cords in silver rings upon marble columns. The couches were of gold and silver upon a pavement of green, white, yellow, and black 7 marble stones. And the drink was served in vessels of gold, and always in different vessels: and royal wine in abundance, 8 as the King was able to provide. And no one was forced to drink more than they wished. For the King had ordered all the officials of his house that each should do as 9 it pleased him. And Queen Vashti <margin>feast.</margin> made a feast for the women in the royal house of King Ahasuerus. 10 And on the seventh day, when the King was in good spirits from the wine, he commanded Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas, the seven chamberlains <note>original: "Camerlinge"; court eunuchs or officials</note> who served 11 before King Ahasuerus, that they <margin>Vashti is summoned and refuses to come.</margin> should bring Queen Vashti before the King, wearing the royal crown, to show the people and the princes her beauty. For she was very 12 beautiful. But Queen Vashti refused to come at the King's word brought by his chamberlains. Then the King became very angry, and his wrath 13 burned within him. ### The 2nd Chapter.

<margin>How beautiful maidens were sought for the king.</margin>
1 After these events, when the wrath of King Ahasuerus had cooled, he thought of Vashti, of what she had done, and what had been decreed 2 against her. Then the King’s servants who served him said: "Let there be sought for the King 3 young, beautiful virgins. And let the King appoint overseers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather all kinds of young, beautiful virgins together at the citadel of Susa, in the women’s quarters <note>original: "vrouwen getimmer"; refers to the harem or the building designated for women</note>, under the hand of Hegai, the King’s chamberlain, who 4 keeps the women, and let him give them their ointments. And let the maiden who pleases the King be Queen in Vashti’s place." This pleased the King well, and he did so.

### The xxviii. Chapter.

1 Surely there are mines for silver, and a place for gold where they refine it. 2 Iron is taken out of the earth, and metal is smelted from stones. 3 An end is made to darkness, and man searches out to the furthest limit the stones <note>original: "Scheuerkeen", likely referring to ore in crevices</note> hidden deep in the dark. 4 A stream breaks out where they dwell, forgotten by the foot: it dries up and wanders away from men. 5 As for the earth, out of it comes bread, yet underneath it is turned up as if by fire. 6 The sapphire is found in certain places, and the dust of the earth contains gold. 7 No bird of prey knows the path, nor has the falcon's eye seen it. 8 The proud beasts have not trodden it. 9 Nor has the lion passed over it. 10 Man puts his hand upon the flinty rock, and overturns the mountains. 11 He cuts out rivers from the rocks, and his eye sees every precious thing. 12 He binds the floods from overflowing, and the thing that is hidden he brings to light. 13 But where shall wisdom be found? 1 Can you hunt the prey for the lionesses, and satisfy the young lions?
2 When they lie down in their places, and rest in the dens where they lurk?

9 To whom I have given the field for a house, and the wilderness for a dwelling.

11 It looks toward the mountains where its pasture is, and seeks out every green thing.
12 <margin>Matthew 23:23</margin> <margin>Psalm 22:21</margin> Do you think that a Unicorn <note>The "Unicorn" likely refers to a wild ox (aurochs) or perhaps a rhinoceros in historical context.</note> will serve you, and stay at your manger?

16 Are the feathers of the peacocks more beautiful than the wings and feathers of the ostrich?
17 Which leaves its eggs on the earth, and lets them be warmed in the dust.
18 It forgets that they might be trampled, and that a wild beast might break them.

1 <margin>Job 38:1.</margin> <margin>The Lord answers Job out of a storm.</margin> And the Lord answered Job out of a storm <note>Original: "onweder," meaning a storm or tempest.</note> and said:

3 Will you bring my judgment to nothing, and condemn me, so that you may be righteous?

8 Bury them together in the earth, and bind their pride in the hidden place:
9 Then I will also acknowledge to you that your own right hand can help you.
10 <margin>Isaiah 27:1</margin> <margin>Elephant</margin> Behold, the Behemoth, <note>Behemoth is often identified as a hippopotamus, though the margin here suggests an elephant.</note> which I made along with you; he eats grass like an ox.

12 <margin>The sneezing of the Behemoth.</margin> His tail stretches out like a cedar; the sinews of his thighs are knit together like a branch.
13 His bones are like solid metal. His limbs are like bars of iron.
14 He is the beginning of the ways of God; He who made him reaches him with His sword.
15 The mountains bring him herbs, and all the wild beasts play there.
16 He gladly lies in the shadow, hidden in the reeds and the mire.
17 The woods cover him with their shadow, and the willows of the brook cover him.
18 See, he swallows up the stream and does not think it great; he imagines that he can drink up the Jordan with his mouth.
19 Yet one catches him with his own eyes, and pierces his nose with snares.

### The XLII. Chapter.

<margin>Isaiah 29:15, Ecclesiasticus 43:4, Hebrews 4:14. Job accuses himself before God and does penance.</margin>
1 And Job answered the Lord and spoke:
2 I acknowledge that you can do all things, and no thought is hidden from you.
3 It is an undiscerning man who intends to hide his counsel. Therefore I acknowledge that I have spoken unwisely of what is too high for me, and which I do not understand.
4 So hear now, let me speak. I will ask you; teach me.
5 I have heard you with my ears, and my eye sees you now also.
6 Therefore I accuse myself, and do penance in dust and ashes.
7 <margin>Job 27:7. God rebukes Job's friends. Matthew 5.</margin> When the Lord had spoken these words with Job, he spoke to Eliphaz of Teman: My wrath is kindled against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken rightly of me, as my servant Job has.

8 So take now seven oxen and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. And let my servant Job pray for you, for I will look upon him, so that I do not deal with you according to your folly <note>Original: "sotheyt," meaning foolishness or lack of wisdom.</note>, for you have not spoken rightly of me, as my servant Job has.
9 <margin>Job 2:11.</margin> Then Eliphaz of Teman, Bildad of Shuah, and Zophar of Naamah went and did as the Lord had commanded them. <margin>Genesis 4:4.</margin> And the Lord looked upon Job.
10 And the Lord turned the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friend. And the Lord gave Job twice as much <margin>Daniel 4:35, Matthew 19:29</margin> as he had before.
11 Then all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all who had known him before, came to him and ate with him in his house, and they turned to him and comforted him over all the misfortune that the Lord had let come upon him. And every one gave him a fine coin <note>Original: "penninck," referring to a piece of money, likely the Hebrew *kesitah*.</note> and a golden forehead band.
12 <margin>Job 1:3, Ecclesiasticus 11:5.</margin> And the Lord blessed Job afterward more than before, so that he obtained fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand donkeys.
13 And he had seven sons and three daughters,
14 and he called the first Jemima, the second Kezia, and the third Keren-happuch.
15 And there were no women found so beautiful in all the land as the daughters of Job. And their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
16 And Job lived after that a hundred and forty years, so that he saw children and children's children, even to the fourth generation. <margin>Genesis 50:22, Psalm 128:6. Job dies.</margin>
17 And Job died, old and satisfied with life.

### The 61st Psalm.

->A Psalm of David / to be sung upon a stringed instrument.<-

1 Hear, O God, my crying / and attend to my prayer.
2 From here below on earth I cry to you / when my heart is in anguish : Lead me surely upon a high rock <note>original: "steenrootse", meaning a rocky crag or cliff.</note>.
3 <margin>Isaiah 13:15, Ecclesiasticus 34:16</margin> *For you are my refuge / a strong tower against my enemies.
4 I will dwell in your Tent <note>original: "Hutte", referring to the Tabernacle.</note> forever / and trust under your wings. Selah.
5 For you, O God, hear my vows / you reward those well / who fear your name.
6 You give a King a long life so that his years continue ever and ever.
7 That he always sits and remains before God : Endow him with kindness and faithfulness / that they may preserve him.
8 So I will sing praise to your name forever / that I may pay my vows daily.

### The 62nd Psalm.

->A Psalm of David / to be sung for Jeduthun <note>Jeduthun was one of the three directors of music in the Davidic sanctuary.</note>.<-

1 My soul is silent toward God / who helps me.
2 For he is my comfort / my help / my protection / so that no fall shall strike me / however great it may be.
3 <margin>A man.</margin> How long do you all lie in wait / *for one lowly man <note>original: "Eenen lagen", referring to someone of low status or being brought low.</note> that you may destroy him / like a leaning wall and broken fences?
4 They only think of how to suppress him / they delight in lies : They give good words / but in their hearts they curse. Selah.
5 But my soul waits only upon God / for he is my hope.
6 He is my comfort / my help / and my protection / so that I shall not fall.
7 <margin>1 Samuel 1:15</margin> In God is my salvation / my honor / the rock of my strength / my refuge is in God.
8 Hope in him always / dear people / *Pour out your heart before him / God is our refuge. Selah.
9 But men are truly nothing at all. Great men also fail : They weigh less than nothing / all of them together.
10 <margin>Ecclesiastes 5:1, 1 Timothy 6:17</margin> *Do not rely on injustice and presumption / and do not cling to such things / which are nothing. If wealth falls to you / do not set your heart upon it.
11 God has spoken one word / that I have sometimes heard / that God alone is mighty.
12 <margin>Jeremiah 17:10, Job 34:11, Romans 2:6, Proverbs 20:23</margin> And you, Lord, are merciful / *and you reward every person / as he has deserved.

### An instruction of Asaph.

1 <margin>Psalm 49:4; Matthew 13:35; *Exodus 12:25. The duty of parents toward their children.</margin> Hear my law, O my people: incline your ears to the words of my mouth.

7 That they might set their hope in God / and not forget the deeds of God / and keep his commandments.

10 They did not keep the covenant of God / and would not walk in his law.
11 And forgot his deeds / and his wonders / which he had shown them.
12 <margin>Then the wonderful deeds of God toward Israel were demonstrated. *Exodus 7, 8, 9. *Exodus 14:21. Psalm 136:13. *Exodus 13:21. 2 Corinthians 10:1. *Numbers 20:11. Exodus 17:6.</margin> Before their fathers he did wonders in the land of Egypt / in the field of Zoan.
13 He divided the Sea / and let them pass through it / and made the water stand like a wall.
14 * He led them by day with a cloud / and all the night with a bright fire.
15 * He split the rocks in the wilderness / and gave them drink in great abundance.
16 And let streams flow out of the rocks / so that they flowed down like rivers of water.
17 <margin>Ingratitude and unbelief of Israel. Exodus 16, 18.</margin> Yet they sinned even more against him / and provoked the Most High in the wilderness.
18 And they tempted God in their hearts / by demanding food for their souls.
19 And they spoke against God / and said: "Yes, could God prepare a table in the wilderness?"
20 Behold, he indeed struck the rock / so that the waters flowed / and the streams poured out.
But how can he give bread / and provide meat for his people?
21 <margin>Numbers 11:1.</margin> When the Lord heard this, he was kindled. And fire broke out in Jacob / and wrath came upon Israel.
22 Because they did not believe in God / and did not hope in his help.
23 And he commanded the clouds above / and opened the doors of heaven.
24 <margin>Exodus 16:5; Deuteronomy 8:3.</margin> * And let Manna rain upon them to eat: And gave them the bread of Heaven.
25 They ate the bread of Angels <note>original: "Enghels broot," a traditional term for Manna</note> / he sent them food in abundance.
26 He let the East wind blow under the heaven / and by his power he stirred up the South wind.
27 <margin>Numbers 11:31; Wisdom 16:2.</margin> And he let meat rain upon them like dust / and birds like the sand of the sea.
28 And let them fall in the midst of their camps everywhere / where they lived.
29 Then they ate / and were well filled: He let them have their fill of their desire.
30 When they had satisfied their desire / and while they were still eating of it:

<column-break/>

31 Then the wrath of God came upon them / and God's hand slew the most prominent among them / and the unperceivable punishment <margin>unperceivable punishment</margin> struck down the best in Israel.
32 * But despite all that / they sinned even more / <margin>Numbers 14:2.</margin> and did not believe in his wonders.
33 Therefore he let them die away / so that they did not God immediately delay / and had to be plagued <margin>God delays for the sake of improvement.</margin> all their days.
34 Whenever he slew them / then they sought him / and they turned early to God.
35 And remembered that God is their comfort / and the Most High God is their redeemer.
36 And they flattered him with their mouths / and lied to him with their tongues: <margin>Then gave hypocrisy.</margin>

39 For he remembered that they are flesh / a <margin>Psalm 103:14.</margin> wind that passes away and does not return.

41 They tempted God again and again / and limited the Holy One of Israel.
42 They did not think of his hand / on the day when he delivered them from the enemy.

44 * When he changed their waters into blood / <margin>Exodus 7:20; Psalm 105:29.</margin> so that they could not drink from their streams.
45 When he sent evil * swarms <note>original: "Wormē," likely referring to the plague of flies or lice</note> among them / <margin>Exodus 8:24; Exodus 8:6.</margin> which devoured them / and frogs which destroyed them.

50 When he let his wrath have its way / and did not spare their souls from death / and <margin>Exodus 9:2.</margin> let their cattle die of the pestilence.

61 And gave their power into captivity / and <margin>1 Samuel 4:6.</margin> their glory into the hands of the enemy.
62 And gave his people over to the sword / and was kindled against his inheritance.
63 The fire devoured their young men / and their maidens had to remain unmarried.

<summary>This page contains the majority of Psalm 78, a historical psalm recounting God's wonders during the Exodus and the repeated rebellion and unfaithfulness of the Israelites. It details the plagues of Egypt, the provision of manna, and the eventual entry into the Promised Land, serving as a moral lesson on the necessity of teaching God's law to future generations.</summary>

33 So will I visit their sins with the rod / and their misdeeds with plagues.
34 But my mercy I will not turn from him / and my truth I will not let fail.
35 I will not profane my covenant / and not change what has gone out of my mouth.
36 I have sworn once by my holiness: I will not lie to David.
<margin>Psalm 72:5, 17</margin>
37 His seed <note>The lineage or descendants of David.</note> shall be eternal / * and his throne before me like the Sun.
38 Like the Moon he shall be preserved forever / and just as the witness in the clouds is certain. Selah.
39 But now you reject and cast off / and are angry with your anointed.
40 You have broken the covenant of your servant / and trodden his crown into the earth.
<margin>Psalm 80:13</margin>
41 You break all his walls into pieces / and let his fortresses be torn down.
42 All who pass by rob him / he has become a mockery to his neighbors.
43 You exalt the right hand of his adversaries / and gladden all his enemies.
44 Also, you have taken away the strength of his sword / and do not let him prevail in the battle.
45 You have ended his splendor / and cast his throne to the earth.
46 You shorten the time of his youth / and cover him with shame. Selah.
<margin>Psalm 44:24</margin>
47 Lord / how long will you hide yourself so completely / and let your wrath burn like fire?
48 Remember how short my life is / why should you have created all men for nothing?
<margin>Genesis 3:19; Hebrews 9:27.</margin>
49 Where is anyone who lives / and does not see death? Who could deliver his soul from the hand of Hell? <note>original: "Hellen hant," referring to the grave or the underworld, Sheol.</note> Selah.
50 Lord, where is your former mercy: Which you swore to David in your truth.
<margin>Psalm 79:10; Colossians 1:15.</margin>
51 Remember, Lord, the contempt shown to your servants / which I carry in my bosom / from so many nations.
52 With which, Lord, your enemies revile / with which they revile the footsteps of your Anointed.
53 Blessed be the Lord forever. Amen. Amen.

### The 90th Psalm.

->A prayer of Moses, the man of God.<-

1 Lord God / you are our refuge from generation to generation.
<margin>Proverbs 8:23; John 17:5; Colossians 1:15.</margin>
2 Before the mountains were / and the earth / and the world were created / you are God from eternity to eternity.
3 You who let man die / and say: Return, you children of men.
<margin>2 Peter 3:8</margin>
4 For a thousand years are before you / like the day that passed yesterday: And like a watch in the night.
<margin>On the shortness of man's life. Psalm 73:20</margin>
5 You let them pass away like a stream / and they are like a sleep / just like grass / which quickly withers.
<margin>Psalm 103:15; Isaiah 40:6; James 1:10.</margin>
6 Which flourishes early / and quickly withers / and in the evening is cut down and dries up.
7 That is what your anger does / that we so perish / and your wrath / that we must die so unexpectedly.
8 For you set our misdeeds before you / our unknown sins / in the light before your face.
9 Therefore all our days pass away through your anger / we spend our years like a useless tale. <note>original: "onnutte reden," suggesting life passes as quickly as a spoken word or an idle story.</note>
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 18:13.</margin>
10 Our life lasts seventy years / and if it comes to a great age / it is eighty years:

<column-break/>

11 And when it has been precious / it has been trouble and labor / * for it passes quickly away / as if we flew from it. <margin>Job 7:6.</margin>
12 But who believes that you are so very angry? And who fears such indignation of yours?
<margin>Psalm 39:5.</margin>
13 Teach us to consider / that we must die / so that we may become wise.
14 Lord / turn back to us / and be merciful to your servants.
15 Fill us early with your mercy / so we will boast and be joyful all our days.
16 Gladden us again now / after you have plagued us so long / after we have suffered misfortune for so long.
17 Show your servants your works / and your glory to their children.
18 And may the Lord our God be friendly to us / and further the work of our hands among us: Yes, may he further the work of our hands.

### The 91st Psalm.

1 He who sits under the protection of the Most High / and remains under the shadow of the Almighty.
<margin>Psalm 18:3.</margin>
2 He speaks to the Lord: My refuge and my fortress / my God / in whom I hope.
3 For he delivers me from the snare of the hunter / and from the harmful pestilence.
<margin>Psalm 121:4.</margin>
4 He shall cover you with his feathers / and your refuge shall be under his wings. His truth is shield and buckler.
<margin>Job 5:21; Ephesians 6:16</margin>
5 So that you must not be terrified by the horror of the night / by the arrows that fly by day.
6 By the pestilence / that creeps in the darkness / by the sickness / that destroys at noon.
7 Though a thousand fall at your side / and ten thousand at your right hand / yet it shall not strike you.
8 Indeed, you shall see with your eyes your desire: and behold how the godless are repaid.
<margin>Psalm 18:19; Ecclesiasticus 34:16.</margin>
9 For the Lord is your refuge / the Most High is your shelter.
<margin>Exodus 23:20</margin>
10 No evil shall meet you / and no plague shall come near your hut.
<margin>Matthew 4:6.</margin>
11 For he has commanded his angels concerning you / that they should protect you in all your ways.
12 That they shall carry you on their hands / so you do not strike your foot against a stone.
<margin>Luke 10:19</margin>
13 Upon the lions and adders shall you go / and tread upon the young lions and dragons.
14 He desires me / so I will help him out: He knows my name / therefore I will protect him.
<margin>Psalm 4:1.</margin>
15 He calls upon me / so I will hear him / I am with him in trouble / I will pull him out / and bring him to honor.
16 I will satisfy him with long life / and will show him my salvation.

### The 92nd Psalm.

-> A Psalm-song for the Sabbath day. <-

<margin>Hebrews 13:15.</margin>
1 It is a precious thing to thank the Lord / and to sing praise to your name / you Most High.
2 In the morning to proclaim your mercy / and in the night your truth.
4 On the ten strings and the psaltery / with playing on the harps.
<margin>Wisdom 13:1; Romans 1:19.</margin>
5 For Lord / you let me sing joyfully of your works / and I boast of the deeds of your hands.
<margin>Psalm 111:3.</margin>
6 Lord, how great are your works: your thoughts are so very deep.
7 A foolish person does not believe that / and a fool does not regard such things.

<summary>This section of the Psalter contains hymns of praise and appeals for divine justice, emphasizing God's role as the creator and righteous judge of all nations. It contrasts the fleeting success of the wicked with the eternal stability of God's kingdom and the flourishing of the faithful.</summary>

### The 101st Psalm.
#### A Psalm of David.

1 **O**f mercy and justice I will sing, and give praise to you, Lord.
2 I deal prudently and reasonably with those who belong to me, and walk faithfully in my house.
3 I set no wicked thing before my eyes: I hate the transgressor and do not let him remain with me.
4 A perverse heart must depart from me: I will not tolerate the wicked.
5 Whoever secretly slanders his neighbor, him will I destroy: I cannot endure those who have a haughty look and a proud heart.
6 My eyes look toward the faithful in the land, <margin>Psalm 15:a:1</margin> so that they may dwell with me; and I gladly have upright servants.
7 Deceitful people I will not keep in my house: <margin>Psalm 5:a:7</margin> liars shall not prosper near me.
<margin>Job 18:d:17 / Psalm 37:b:9 / Proverbs 2:b:22 8</margin>
8 Speedily I will destroy all the godless in the land, that I may root out all evildoers from the city of the Lord.

### The 102nd Psalm.
#### A prayer of the afflicted, when he is overwhelmed and pours out his complaint before the Lord.

<margin>Psalm 143:a:1 1</margin>
1 **L**ord, hear my prayer, and let my cry come to you.
<margin>Psalm 86:a:1 / Lamentations 3:e:57 2</margin>
2 Hide not your face from me in my distress; incline your ears to me: whenever I call upon you, answer me speedily.
<margin>Psalm 68:a:3 / Wisdom 5:c:15 3</margin>
3 For my days are consumed like smoke: and my bones are burned like a hearth.
4 My heart is stricken and withered like grass, so that I even forget to eat my bread.
<margin>Lamentations 4:b:8 5</margin>
5 My bones cling to my flesh from groaning and sighing.
6 I am like a bittern in the wilderness of the pelican <note>These birds are used as symbols of extreme loneliness and desolation.</note>: I am like a little owl in the ruined cities.
7 I lie awake and am like a solitary bird upon the roof.
8 Daily my enemies taunt me, and those who mock me swear by me.
9 For I eat ashes like bread, and mix my drink with weeping.
10 Because of your threats and wrath, for you have lifted me up and cast me down.
<margin>Job 8:a:9 / Psalm 109:c:23 11</margin>
11 My days are gone like a shadow, and I wither like grass.
<margin>Wisdom 2:b:9 12</margin>
12 But you, Lord, remain forever, and your remembrance from generation to generation.
13 You will surely arise and have mercy upon Zion, for it is time that you are gracious to her; the hour has come.
<margin>Jeremiah 25:b:12 / 1 Ezra 1:a:1 14</margin>
14 For your servants would gladly see her built, and would gladly see her stones and mortar made ready.
15 That the heathens may fear your name, and all kings on earth your glory.
16 When the Lord builds up Zion, he appears in his glory.

### The 104th Psalm.

### The CVIII. Psalm.
#### A Psalm-Song of David.
<margin>Psa. 57:b:8.</margin>
1 O God, I am truly earnest / * I will sing and compose, my glory also. <note>original: "mijn eere oock" refers to the soul or the tongue as the source of one's honor and praise.</note>
2 Awake, Psaltery and Harp / I will be up early.
3 I will thank you, Lord, among the nations, I will sing your praise among the people.
<margin>Psa. 57:b:11.</margin>
4 * For your mercy reaches as wide as the Heaven is / and your truth as wide as the clouds go.
5 Exalt yourself, O God, above the Heaven / and your glory over all Lands.
6 In order that your dear friends may be delivered / help with your right hand / and hear me.
<margin>Psal. 60:b:8.</margin>
7 * God spoke in his sanctuary / therefore I am joyful / and will divide Shechem and measure out the valley of Succoth. <note>Shechem and Succoth represent the regions on both sides of the Jordan River.</note>
<margin>Gen. 49:b:10.</margin>

10 Who will lead me into a fortified city? who shall lead me into Edom?
11 Will you not do so, O God, you who cast us out? And do you not go out, O God, with our army?
<margin>Psa. 60:b:15.</margin>
12 || Do us assistance in need / for human help is of no use.

### The CIX. Psalm.
#### A Psalm of David to be sung.
<margin>1 This psalm treats the obstinacy against Christ.</margin>
1 O God, my praise / be not silent.
2 For they have opened their godless and false mouths against me / and speak against me with false tongues.
3 And they speak poisonously against me everywhere / and fight against me without cause.
<margin>Psa. 35:b:12.</margin>
4 In return for my love / they are against me / but I pray.
5 They show me evil for good / And hatred for love.
<margin>Lev. 26:c:17. 6 * Zach. 3:a:1.</margin>
6 * Set the godless over him / * and the Satan <note>original: "Satan" here often implies an "Accuser" or legal adversary.</note> must stand at his right hand.
7 Whoever allows himself to be taught by the same / his life must be godless / and his prayer must be sin.
<margin>John 17:d:12. This is spoken of the traitor Judas; Matthias received his office Acts 1:d:20.</margin>
8 His days must be few / and another must receive his office.
9 His children must become orphans / and his wife a widow.
10 His children must go wandering and bewildered / and beg / and seek / as those who are wasted away.
11 The usurers must suck out all that he has / and strangers must plunder his goods.
12 And no one must show him kindness / and no one have mercy on his orphans.
13 His descendants must be rooted out; Their name must be extinguished in the next generation.
14 His fathers' misdeed must be remembered before the Lord / and his mother's sin must not be blotted out.
15 The Lord must never let them out of his sight / and their memory must be rooted out from the earth.
16 Because he had absolutely no com-

<column-break/>

<margin>Exod. 23:a:7. Psa. 10:b:3. Isaiah 3:c:14.</margin>
16 passion: * But persecuted the wretched and Poor / and the sorrowful / that he might kill him.
17 And he wanted the curse / so it shall also come to him: He did not want the blessing / so it shall also remain far from him.

30 I have chosen the way of truth; your statutes I have set before me.
<margin>Ps. 25:2 31 32</margin>

<margin>Mat. 10:22 33 34 35 36 37 38 39 40 41</margin>

36 Incline my heart to your testimonies, and not to greed.
37 Turn away my eyes, that they do not look upon useless teaching <note>original: "onnutte leeringe" — vanity or worthless instruction.</note>, but revive me in your way.

40 Behold, I desire your precepts; revive me with your righteousness.
41 Lord, let your mercy come to me, and your help according to your word.

<margin>

A fatherly exhortation to wisdom and its profit.

1 Hear, my children, the instruction of your father; pay attention, so that you may learn and become wise. 2 For I give you a good teaching; do not forsake my law. 3 For I too was my father’s son, a tender one, and the only beloved before my mother. 4 And he taught me, and said: "Let your heart receive my words; keep my commandments, so you shall 5 live." 5 Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding; do not forget, and do not depart from 6 the speech of my mouth. 6 Do not forsake her, and she shall preserve you; love her, and she shall 7 protect you. 7 The beginning of wisdom is when one gladly hears it, and prizes 8 discernment more than all goods. 8 Hold her high, and she shall exalt you; she shall bring you to honor, 9 if you embrace her. 9 She shall add to your [beauty], and shall adorn you with a beautiful 10 crown. 10 So hear, my child, and receive my words, so that the years of your life 11 may be many. 11 I want to lead you on the way of wisdom. I want to lead you on the right path, 12 so that when you walk, your pace shall not be difficult, and when you run, 13 you shall not stumble. 13 Hold fast to instruction and do not let go; preserve it, for it is 14 your life. 14 Do not come upon the path of the godless, and do not step on the way of the wicked. 15 Let it go, and do not enter it. 16 Depart from it, and pass by; for they do not sleep unless they have 17 done harm. 17 For they feed themselves on the bread of ungodliness, and drink of the wine of 18 presumption. 18 But the path of the righteous shines like a light that goes forth and 19 shines until the full day. 19 But the way of the godless is like darkness, and they do not 20 know where they shall fall. 20 My son, attend to my words, and incline your ear to my 21 speech. 21 Do not let them depart from your eyes; keep them in your heart. 22 For they are life to those who find them, and health 23 to their whole body. 23 Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flows life.

### The 5th Chapter.

<margin>
A warning against the fickleness of harlots.

1 My child, attend to my wisdom, and incline your eyes to my teaching, 2 so that you may maintain good counsel, and the lips of your mouth may know how to have discernment. 3 For the lips of the harlot are sweet as honeycomb, and her throat is smoother than oil. 4 But afterwards she is bitter as wormwood <note>original: "Alsene"</note>, and sharp as a two-edged sword. 5 Her feet run downwards to death; her steps reach into hell. 6 She does not 6 go straight on the path of life; her steps are unstable, so that she does not know where she goes. 7 So listen to me now, my children, and do not depart from the speech of my mouth. 8 Let your ways be far from her, and do not come near the door of her house, 9 lest you give your honor to strangers and your years to the cruel. 10 Lest strangers satisfy themselves with your wealth, and your labor be in another's house; 11 and you must groan afterwards, when you have consumed your physical goods, 12 and say: "Oh, how I hated instruction, and my heart despised correction! 13 And I did not hear the voice of my teachers, and did not incline my ear to those 14 who taught me. 14 I have come into almost every misfortune, before all people and all nations." 15 Drink water from your own cistern, and flowing water from your own fountain. 16 Let your fountains flow out, and the streams of water 17 into the streets. 17 But have them for yourself alone, and no stranger with you. 18 Let your fountain be blessed, and rejoice in the wife 19 of your youth. 19 She is lovely as a hind, and as gracious as a roe deer <note>original: "Rhee"</note>. Let her love always satisfy you, and always delight 20 in her love. 20 My child, why would you delight yourself with a stranger, and embrace 21 another woman? 21 For every man's ways are before the Lord, and he measures 22 all their paths. 22 The iniquity of the godless shall catch him, and he shall be held with the snare 23 of his sins. 23 He shall die because he would not let himself be instructed, and because of his great foolishness, it shall not go well for him.

The Proverbs

### The 30th Chapter.

1 **T**hese are the words of Agur, the son of Jakeh; the teaching and discourse of the man to Ithiel, even to Ithiel and Ucal.
2 For I am the most foolish of all, and human understanding is not within me.
3 I have not learned wisdom, and what is holy, I do not know.
4 Who has ascended into heaven and come down again? Who has gathered the wind in his hands? Who has bound the waters in a garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name? And what is his son's name? Do you know?
<margin>Psalm 7:a. 12; 18:c. 31. Deuteronomy 4:a. 2, 6.</margin>
5 All the words of God are pure <note>Original: "doorgeloutert," meaning refined like precious metal in a furnace.</note> and are a shield to those who trust in them.
6 Do not add to his words, so that he does not punish you and you be found a liar.
7 Two things I request of you; do not deny them to me before I die:
<margin>Proverbs 20:c. 21. Jeremiah 17:b. 11. Ecclesiasticus 27:a. 4. 1 Timothy 6:b. 9. Deuteronomy 8:c. 12.</margin>
8 Keep idolatry and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches. But let me take my allotted portion of food.
9 Otherwise, if I were too full, I might deny you and say: "Who is the Lord?" Or if I became too poor, I might steal and dishonor the name of my God.
10 Do not slander a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you must bear the guilt.
<margin>Exodus 21:b. 17. Deuteronomy 27:c. 16. Matthew 15:a. 4.</margin>
11 There is a generation <note>Original: "eenen aert," meaning a type of people or a lineage.</note> that curses their father and does not bless their mother.
12 A generation that considers itself pure, and yet is not washed from its own filth.
<margin>Psalm 18:c. 28. Proverbs 6:b. 17.</margin>
13 A generation that carries its eyes high and lifts up its eyelids.
<margin>Psalm 10:b. 8. Isaiah 3:c. 14.</margin>
14 A generation whose teeth are swords, *which devours and consumes with its molars* the miserable in the land and the poor among the people.
15 The leech <note>Original: "Egel," here referring to the horse-leech or bloodsucker.</note> has two daughters: "Bring here, bring here." Three things are never satisfied, and the fourth does not say:
<margin>Proverbs 27:c. 20.</margin>
16 "It is enough": the grave; the closed womb of a woman; the earth that is never saturated with water; and the fire that never says, "It is enough."
17 An eye that mocks the father and despises giving ear to the mother—that the ravens by the brooks should pick out, and the young eagles devour.
18 Three things are too wonderful for me, and the
<margin>Wisdom 5:b. 11.</margin>
19 fourth I do not know: the way of an eagle in the sky; the way of a serpent on a rock; the way of a ship in the middle of the sea; and the way of a man with a young woman.
20 Such is also the way of an adulteress; she devours and wipes her mouth and says: "I have done nothing evil."
21 A land is made restless by three things, and
22 the fourth it cannot endure:
<margin>3 Kings 11:f. 29. <note>In older Bibles, 1 Kings is often cited as 3 Kings.</note></margin>
23 A servant, if he becomes king; a fool, when he is full of bread; a wicked woman, when she is married; and a maidservant, when she becomes the heir to her mistress.
24 These things are small on earth, yet they are wiser
<margin>Proverbs 6:a. 6. Ecclesiasticus 10:e. 18.</margin>
25 than the wise: The ants, a weak people, yet they prepare their food in the summer.
26 The rock badgers <note>Original: "Conijnen," literally rabbits, but referring to the hyrax or rock badger.</note>, a weak people, yet they make their house in the rocky cliffs.
27 The locusts have no king, yet they march out in great swarms.
28 The spider works with her hands and is found in the palaces of kings.
29 Three things have a fine stride, and the fourth walks quite well:
30 The lion, mighty among the animals, who does not turn back for anyone.
31 A greyhound <note>Original: "Haelwint," a hunting dog known for its speed.</note> with good loins; a ram; and the king, against whom no one dares to stand.
32 If you have been foolish and exalted yourself, or if you have intended something evil, then lay your hand upon your mouth.
33 When one churns milk, butter is made from it. And whoever blows the nose hard, forces blood out of it. And whoever stirs up anger, forces strife from it.

### The 31st Chapter.

1 **T**hese are the words of King Lemuel: the teaching that his mother taught him.
2 Oh my chosen one, oh you son of my body, oh my longed-for son.
3 Do not give your strength to women, and do not walk in the ways where kings perish.
<margin>Ecclesiasticus 19:a. 1.</margin>
4 Oh not for kings, Lemuel, do not give kings wine to drink, nor princes strong drink.
5 They might otherwise drink and forget the laws, and change the causes of the miserable people.
6 Give strong drink to those who shall perish,
<margin>Psalm 104:b. 15. Ecclesiasticus 32:a. 7.</margin>
7 and wine to the sorrowful souls, so that they may drink and forget their misery, and remember their misfortune no more.
8 Open your mouth for the dumb, and for the cause of all who are forsaken.
9 Open your mouth, and judge righteously, and avenge the miserable and the poor.
<margin>Proverbs 18:f. 22. Ecclesiasticus 26:a. 1. For praise and honor of the virtuous woman.</margin>
10 *To whom a virtuous wife is granted, she is much more noble than precious pearls.*
11 Her husband's heart dares to rely on her, and nourishment <note>Original: "neringe," meaning livelihood or trade.</note> shall not be lacking to him.
12 She does him good and not evil all the days of her life.
13 She deals with wool and flax, and works willingly with her hands.
14 She is like a merchant ship that brings its goods from afar.
15 She rises in the night and gives food to her household, and a portion to her maidservants.
16 She considers a field and buys it, and plants a vineyard from the fruits of her hands.
17 She girds her loins tightly and strengthens her arms.
18 She notices how her dealings bring a profitable advantage; her candle does not go out at night.
19 She stretches out her hand to the distaff, and her fingers grasp the spindle.
<margin>Deuteronomy 15:a. 1. Proverbs 11:c. 24. 2 Corinthians 9:b. 1.</margin>
20 She spreads out her hands to the poor and reaches her hand to the needy.
21 She does not fear for her household because of the snow, for her whole house has double clothing.
22 She makes her own coverings; white silk and purple are her clothing.
23 Her husband is well-known in the gates when he sits with the elders of the land.
24 She makes a garment and sells it; she gives a girdle to the merchant.
<margin>Luke 6:f. 21. Proverbs 11:c. 24.</margin>
25 Her adornment is that which is pure and glorious, and she shall laugh in the time to come.
<margin>Psalm 37:d. 30.</margin>
26 She opens her mouth with wisdom, and on her tongue is wholesome teaching.
27 She watches how things go in her house and does not eat her bread in idleness.
28 Her sons rise up and call her blessed; her husband praises her.
29 "Many daughters gather riches together, but you surpass them all."
<margin>The fear of the Lord.</margin>
30 Charm and beauty are nothing; a woman who fears the Lord shall be praised.
31 She shall be praised for the fruits of her hands, and her works shall praise her in all the gates.
