### The XXVI. Chapter.

Agrippa said to Paul: You are permitted / to speak for yourself. Then Paul stretched out his hand / and answered for himself:

2 I am very glad / dear King Agrippa / that I shall answer for myself before you today / concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews.

3 Especially / because you know all the customs and questions of the Jews / therefore I beseech you / to hear me patiently.

4 It is true / my life from my youth up / how I lived from the beginning among my own people at Jerusalem / all the Jews know well /

5 Who knew me from the beginning / if they would testify. For I was a Pharisee / which is the strictest sect of our religion.

6 And now I stand / and am accused for the hope of the promise / which was made by God to our Fathers:

7 To which promise our twelve tribes hope to come / serving God day and night with all diligence. For the sake of this hope / dear King Agrippa / I am accused by the Jews.

8 Why should it be judged an incredible thing by you / that God should raise the dead?

9 I truly / thought within myself / that I ought to do many things contrary to the Name of Jesus of Nazareth /

10 Which I also did in Jerusalem / where I shut up many of the saints in prison / having received authority from the High Priests; And when they were put to death / I helped to give my voice against them.

11 And I punished them often in every synagogue / and compelled them to blaspheme / and being exceedingly mad against them / I persecuted them even into foreign cities.

# The Epistle of St. Paul
## to the Romans.

### The First Chapter.

<margin>Acts 13:2. Galatians 1:15. Genesis 3:15. Jeremiah 23:5. Acts 28:23. Matthew 1:1. Isaiah 9:5.</margin>
1 **P**aul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an Apostle, set apart to preach the Gospel of God (which he promised beforehand through his Prophets, in the holy scriptures),
<margin>Acts 2:31. Acts 9:17. Acts 24:21. Paul speaks with the Elders of the Jews in Rome. Acts 28:14.</margin>
2 Concerning his Son, who was born of the seed of David according to the flesh.
3 And powerfully proven to be a Son of God according to the Spirit, who sanctifies. Since the time that he arose from the dead, namely, Jesus Christ our Lord,
4 Through whom we have received grace and the Apostleship among all Heathens <note>original: "Heydenē"; refers to non-Jewish nations/Gentiles</note>, to establish the obedience of faith under his Name,
5 Of which you also are a part, who are called by Jesus Christ.
6 To all who are in Rome, the beloved of God, and called Saints.
<margin>1 Corinthians 1:2.</margin>
7 Grace be with you and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
8 First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ on behalf of you all, that your faith is spoken of in the whole world,
<margin>John 4:23. 2 Timothy 1:3. Philippians 1:4. Acts 23:6.</margin>
9 For God is my witness (whom I serve in my spirit in the Gospel of his Son) that I remember you without ceasing,
10 and always in my prayer I plead: if it might once please him to arrange that I might come to you, by God’s will.
<margin>Jeremiah 10:23. 1 Thessalonians 3:10. Romans 15:29.</margin>
11 For I long to see you, so that I may share with you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,
12 (That is) that I may be comforted with you through your and my faith, which we have among one another.
<margin>1 Thessalonians 2:18. Luke 2:34.</margin>
13 I do not want to hide from you, dear brothers, that I have often intended to come to you, but have been hindered until now, so that I might also produce fruit among you, just as among other Heathens.
<margin>Genesis 3:15. Deuteronomy 18:15. 2 Samuel 7:12. Acts 17:4.</margin>
14 I am a debtor both to the Greeks and to the non-Greeks: both to the Wise and to the unwise:
15 Therefore, as much as is in me, I am inclined also to preach the Gospel to you in Rome.
<margin>Psalm 40:11. 2 Timothy 1:8. 1 Corinthians 1:18.</margin>
16 For I am not ashamed of the Gospel of Christ: for it is a power of God that saves all those who believe in it, the Jews especially, and also the Greeks:
<margin>Romans 3:21. Habakkuk 2:4. Hebrews 10:38. Wisdom 13:1.</margin>
17 Since therein is revealed the righteousness that counts before God, which comes from believing into faith. As it stands written: The Righteous shall live by his faith.
18 For God’s wrath from Heaven is revealed over all godless being and unrighteousness of Men, who hold back the truth in unrighteousness.
<margin>Acts 14:10. Psalm 19:1.</margin>
19 For what may be known, that there is a God, that is manifest to them.
20 For God has revealed it to them, in that God’s invisible being—that is, his eternal power and Divinity—is seen, when one perceives it in his works, namely, in the creation of the world: So that they have no excuse,
<margin>Through creation one learns to know the creator. Deuteronomy 28:28. Jeremiah 5:21. Psalm 106:20. God punishes with blindness. Bel and the Dragon 22. 2 Samuel 24:1.</margin>
21 Because they knew that there is a God, and did not praise him as a God, nor thanked him, but have become vain in their thinking, and their foolish heart is darkened.
22 While they held themselves for wise, they became fools,
23 And have changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image like corruptible man, and birds, and four-footed animals, and creeping creatures.
24 Therefore has

<column-break/>

God also given them up, in the lusts of their hearts, to uncleanness, to dishonor their own bodies among themselves:
25 who have changed God's truth into a lie, and have honored and served that which is created more than the Creator, who is blessed in eternity, Amen.
<margin>Leviticus 18:22.</margin>
26 Therefore God has also given them up to shameful lusts. For their women have changed the natural use into the unnatural:
27 Likewise also the Men have left the natural use of women and were inflamed toward one another in their lusts, and have wrought shame, men with men, and received the reward of their wandering (as was proper) in themselves.
<margin>Proverbs 1:26. Acts 7:42.</margin>
28 And just as they did not regard knowing God, so God gave them over to a perverted mind, to do that which is not proper:
29 Full of all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, malignity; whisperers, backbiters,
30 Haters of God, insolent, haughty, boasters, harmful, disobedient to Parents,
<margin>Wisdom 15:6. Hosea 7:3.</margin>
31 Without understanding, faithless, hard-hearted, irreconcilable, unmerciful: Who, although they know God’s righteousness—that those who do such things are worthy of death—not only do it, but also have a delight in those who do it.

->The Second Chapter.<-

<margin>One must <unclear>self-seek</unclear> one's own guilt. Do not excuse yourself, whoever you are, who judge therein:</margin>
1 **T**herefore, O man, you cannot excuse yourself, whoever you are, who judge therein: For wherein you judge another, there you condemn <gloss>has.</gloss> yourself, since you <gloss>likewise</gloss> do the same thing that you judge.
<margin>Matthew 7:1. 2 Samuel 12:5. 1 Corinthians 4:5.</margin>
2 For we know that God's judgment is right over those who do such things.
3 But do you think, O man, you who judge those who do such things and also do the same yourself, that you shall escape the judgment of God?
<margin>Isaiah 30:18. 2 Peter 3:15.</margin>
4 Or do you despise the <gloss>especially without</gloss> goodness, <gloss>consumption.</gloss> patience, and long-suffering? And do you not know that God’s goodness leads to repentance?
<margin>James 5:3.</margin>
5 But you, according to your hardened and impenitent heart, heap up for yourself wrath for the day of wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God.
<margin>Psalm 62:13. Matthew 16:27. 2 Corinthians 5:10.</margin>
6 Who shall give to each one according to his works.
7 Namely, praise and honor and an incorruptible being to those who, with patience in good works, strive for eternal life:
<margin>2 Thessalonians 1:8.</margin>
8 But to those who are contentious and are not obedient to the truth, but are obedient to unrighteousness, indignation and wrath.
<margin>Joel 3:23.</margin>
9 Tribulation and anguish upon every soul of man who does evil, especially of the Jew, and also of the Greek:
10 But praise and honor and peace to everyone who does good, especially to the Jew and also to the Greek.
<margin>Deuteronomy 10:17. Galatians 2:6.</margin>
11 For there is no respect of persons before God.
12 Those who have sinned without the Law shall also perish without the Law. And those who have sinned under the Law shall be judged by the Law.
<margin>Matthew 7:24. Luke 6:47. James 1:22.</margin>
13 Since those who hear the Law are not righteous before God: But those who do the Law shall be righteous.
14 For if the Heathens who do not have the law nonetheless do the works of the Law by nature, they themselves—while they do not have the Law—are a law unto themselves,
15 Whereby they prove that the work of the Law is written in their hearts: Since their conscience bears witness to them, as do also the thoughts that accuse or excuse one another,
<margin>Matthew 25:31.</margin>
16 On that day when God shall judge the secrets of men through Jesus Christ,

28 For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly; neither is that circumcision which happens outwardly in the flesh.

### The 3rd Chapter.

<margin>In which the Jews have more advantage than the Gentiles.</margin>
1 What advantage then do the Jews have? Or what is the benefit of circumcision?
2 Truly, a great deal. First: they were entrusted with what God has spoken.
<margin>Romans 3:4. 2 Timothy 1:13. Numbers 23:19. John 3:33.</margin>
3 But if some do not believe in that same thing, what of it? Should God’s faithfulness be brought to nothing because of their unbelief? Far be it.
<margin>Psalms 51:6.</margin>
4 Let it much rather be that God is true and all men are false, as it is written: That you may be justified in your words, and overcome when you are judged.
5 But if it is so, that our unrighteousness praises God’s righteousness, what shall we say? Is God then unrighteous because He becomes angry over it? (I speak here in a human way.)
6 Far be it. How else could God judge the world?
7 For if the truth of God becomes more glorious through my lie, to His praise, why should I then still be judged as a sinner?
8 And why not rather do (as we are slandered, and as some say that we should say): Let us do evil so that good may come of it? Their condemnation is entirely just.
<margin>How the Jews again have no advantage.</margin>
9 What do we say then now? Do we have an advantage? In no way. For we have proven before that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin.
<margin>Psalms 14:2. Psalms 10:7. Psalms 5:10. Psalms 140:4. Psalms 10:7. Proverbs 1:16. Isaiah 59:7. Psalms 36:1.</margin>

11 There is no one who is understanding, there is no one who seeks after God.
12 They have all turned away and have altogether become useless. There is no one who does any good, not even one.
13 Their throat is an open grave; with their tongues they act deceitfully; the venom of asps is under their lips.
14 Their mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
15 Their feet are swift to shed blood.
16 In their ways is nothing but calamity and heartache.
17 And the way of peace they do not know.
18 There is no fear of God before

19 their eyes. But we know that whatever the law says, it says to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be stopped and the whole world may be held accountable to God.
20 Therefore, no flesh can be justified before Him through the works of the law, for through the law comes only the knowledge of sin.
21 But now, without the aid of the law, the righteousness that counts before God has been revealed, and witnessed to by the Law and the Prophets.
22 But I speak of such righteousness before God, which comes through faith in Jesus Christ, to all and upon all those who believe.
23 For there is no distinction here; they are all sinners, and they lack the glory they should have in God,
24 and they are justified without merit, by His grace, through the redemption that has occurred through Christ Jesus.
25 Whom God has set forth as a mercy seat <note>original: "genadēstoel"; refers to the cover of the Ark of the Covenant where atonement was made</note>, through faith in His blood, so that He might offer the righteousness that counts before Him, in that He forgives the sins that remained until now,
26 under divine forbearance; so that He might at this time offer the righteousness that counts before Him: so that He alone might be righteous and make him righteous who is of the faith in Jesus.
27 Where is your boasting now? It is excluded. By which law? By the law of works? Not so: but by the law of faith.
28 So we now hold: that man is made righteous without the works of the law, through faith alone <note>original: "alleen door den gelooue"; the inclusion of "alone" was a hallmark of Reformation-era Bibles</note>.
29 Or is God the God of the Jews only? Is He not also the God of the Gentiles?
30 Yes, surely, also the God of the Gentiles: since there is but one God who makes the circumcised righteous out of faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
31 How? Do we then abolish the Law through faith? Far be it; rather, we uphold the Law.

### The 4th Chapter.

1 What then shall we say of our father Abraham, what he found according to the flesh?
2 For if Abraham were justified by works, he would indeed have something to boast of, but not before God.
3 For what does the scripture say? Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.
4 But to one who works, the reward is not reckoned out of grace, but as a debt.
5 But to one who does not work, but believes in Him who makes the ungodly righteous, his faith is reckoned as righteousness.
6 In which manner David also says: that the blessedness belongs only to the man to whom God reckons righteousness without the addition of works, where he speaks:
7 Blessed are those whose unrighteousness is forgiven and whose sins are covered.
8 Blessed is the man to whom God reckons no sin.
9 Does this blessedness apply to the circumcision or to the uncircumcision? We must indeed say that Abraham’s faith was reckoned for righteousness.
10 How then was it reckoned to him? While in circumcision? Or in uncircumcision? Without doubt, not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.
11 But he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of faith, which he already had while uncircumcised: so that he might become a father to all those who believe while uncircumcised, so that the same might also be reckoned to them for righteousness.
12 And that he might also be a father of circumcision, not only to those who are of the circumcision, but also to those who walk in the foot-

<vocab>Abraham, circumcision, righteousness, faith, Jews, Gentiles, law, sinner, mercy seat, Spirit</vocab>

<summary>This page covers Romans 2:17 through 4:12, where Paul argues that religious rituals like circumcision are secondary to internal faith and that both Jews and Gentiles are justified by faith alone rather than the Law. He uses the example of Abraham to demonstrate that righteousness was credited through faith before the ritual of circumcision was established.</summary>
<keywords>justification by faith, circumcision of the heart, universal sin, mercy seat, Abraham's faith, righteousness, grace, Law vs. Faith</keywords>

1 <margin>A</margin> Do you not know, dear brothers (for I speak to those who know the Law), that the Law rules over a person as long as he lives?

For I did not know of lust <note>original: "lust"; used here in the sense of covetousness or forbidden desire</note> if the Law had not said: || Do not lust.

10 But I died; and it was found that the commandment which was given to me for life, resulted in death for me.

->The Eighth Chapter.<-

1 <margin>A</margin> So there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.
2 For the law of the spirit, which makes alive in Christ Jesus, has made me *free from the Law of sin and death.
3 For what was impossible for the Law (since it was weakened by the flesh), God did, and sent his Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and condemned sin in the flesh, through sin.
4 So that the righteousness required by the Law might be fulfilled in us, who now walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit.
5 <margin>B</margin> *For those who are fleshly minded are concerned with fleshly things. And those who are spiritual are concerned with spiritual things.
6 But to be fleshly minded is death, and to be spiritually minded is life and peace.
7 Because to be fleshly minded is enmity against God, since it is not subject to the Law of God, nor can it be.
8 But those who are fleshly cannot please God.
9 But you are not fleshly, but spiritual, if indeed the Spirit of God lives in you. But whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ is not his.
10 But if Christ is in you, then the body is dead because of sin: But the spirit is life because of righteousness.
11 If now the spirit of him who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you, then he *who raised Christ from the dead shall also *make your mortal bodies alive because his spirit lives in you.
12 <margin>C</margin> So then, dear brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh,
13 For if you live according to the flesh, you must die. But if you through the spirit kill the works of the flesh, you shall live.
14 For those whom the Spirit of God leads *are children of God.
15 For you have not received a servant-like spirit <note>original: "knechtlycken geest"; a spirit of bondage or slavery</note> that you should fear again, *but you have received a child-like spirit <note>original: "kindelijcken gheest"; a spirit of adoption</note> through which we cry: Abba, dear Father.

### Chapter 10

<margin>Romans 9:31. Galatians 4:17. The Jews' own righteousness.</margin>
1 **D**ear brothers, my heart's desire and my prayer to God for Israel is that they might be saved. 2 For I bear them witness that they are zealous for God, but without understanding. 3 For they do not recognize the righteousness that counts before God, and they seek to establish their own righteousness; therefore, they have not submitted themselves to the righteousness that counts before God. 4 <margin>*Matthew 5:17. Galatians 2:20.</margin> *For Christ is the end of the Law; whoever believes in him is justified. 5 <margin>Leviticus 18:5. Galatians 3:12.</margin> Moses indeed writes of the righteousness that comes from the Law: the person who does these things shall live by them. 6 <margin>*Deuteronomy 30:12. Concerning the righteousness of faith.</margin> But the righteousness that comes from faith speaks thus: *Do not say in your heart, "Who will ascend into Heaven?" (That is nothing else than to bring Christ down). 7 Or, "Who will descend into the depths?" (That is nothing else than to bring Christ up from the dead). 8 But what does it say? The word is near you; namely, in your mouth and in your heart. 9 This is the word of faith that we preach. 10 For if you confess Jesus with your mouth—that he is the Lord—and believe in your heart that God has raised him from the dead, then you shall be saved. 11 For if one believes from the heart, one is justified; and if one confesses with the mouth, one is saved.

<margin>Isaiah 28:16.</margin>
11 *For the Scripture says: Whoever believes in him shall not be put to shame. 12 Here there is no distinction between a Jew and a Greek <note>In the New Testament, "Greek" is often used as a general term for all non-Jewish peoples, or Gentiles</note>. There is one Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him. 13 <margin>Joel 2:32. Acts 2:21.</margin> For whoever shall call upon the Name of the Lord shall be saved. 14 But how shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a preacher? 15 <margin>The sending of preachers. Isaiah 52:7.</margin> And how shall they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: *How lovely are the feet of those who proclaim peace, who proclaim good things.

16 But they have not all been obedient to the Gospel. For Isaiah says: Lord, 17 <margin>Isaiah 53:1. John 12:38.</margin> *who believes our preaching? So faith comes from preaching, and preaching comes through the word of God. 18 But I say: Have they not heard? <margin>Psalm 19:4. No one can make an excuse.</margin> *Yes, truly, their sound has gone out into all lands, and their words to the ends of the world. 19 But I say: Did Israel not know? First, Moses says: <margin>*Deuteronomy 32:21.</margin> *I will make you jealous by those who are not my people, and by a foolish nation I will anger you. 20 <margin>Isaiah 65:1.</margin> And Isaiah is so bold as to say: I was found by those who did not seek me, and I appeared to those who did not ask for me. 21 <margin>Isaiah 65:2.</margin> But to Israel he says: "All day long I have stretched out my hands to a people that will not be told, and who speak against me."

1 **I** say then: *Has God then cast away his people? God forbid! For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. 2 God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew. But if you do boast against them, know that you do not support the root, but the root supports you. 19 Then you will say: The branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in. 20 That is well spoken; they were broken off because of their unbelief, but you stand by faith. 21 Do not be arrogant, but fear. If God did not spare the natural branches, take care that he might not spare you either. 22 Therefore, behold the goodness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, and goodness toward you, provided you remain in that goodness; otherwise, you also shall be cut off. 23 *And they, if they do not remain in unbelief, shall be grafted in; God is well able to graft them in again. 24 For if you were cut out of the olive tree which was wild by nature, and were grafted contrary to nature into the good olive tree, how much more shall the natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree? 25 I would not have you ignorant, dear brothers, of this mystery <note>original: "verholē hept" (verholentheyt); a secret or divine truth now revealed</note>, so that you are not arrogant. Blindness in part has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, 26 and so all Israel shall be saved. As it is written: *Out of Zion shall come the Deliverer, who shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob. 27 *And this is my covenant with them, when I shall take away their sins. 28 Concerning the Gospel, I consider them enemies for your sake; 29 but concerning the election, I love them for the fathers' sake. God's gifts and callings can never be repented of by him. 30 For just as you in times past did not believe God, but now have obtained mercy...

**P**aul, called to be an Apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and brother Sosthenes, to the Church of God at Corinth, the sanctified in Christ Jesus, the called saints, with all those who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, theirs and ours. ### Chapter 12.

<margin>Concerning spiritual gifts</margin>
1 Now concerning spiritual gifts, dear brothers, I do not want to keep you in ignorance.
2 You know that you were heathens, led away to mute idols, however you were moved.
3 Therefore, I make known to you that no one speaking by the Spirit of God calls Jesus accursed; and no one can call Jesus "Lord" except by the Holy Spirit.
<margin>Rom. 12:6</margin>
4 There are various gifts, but there is one Spirit.
<margin>1 Pet. 4:10</margin>
5 And there are various offices, but there is one Lord.
<margin>John 5:17</margin>
6 And there are various powers, but there is one God, who works all things in all.
7 To each one, the manifestation of the gifts of the Spirit is given for the common profit.
8 To one is given through the Spirit the word of wisdom; to another the word of knowledge, according to the same Spirit;
9 To another, faith in the same Spirit; to another, gifts of healing in the

<column-break/>

same Spirit;
10 To another, the working of miracles; to another, prophecy; to another, the discerning of spirits; to another, various kinds of tongues; to another, the interpretation of tongues.
11 But all these things are worked by the same one Spirit, distributing to each one individually as he wills.
12 For as the body is one and yet has many members, and all the members of one body, though they are many, are yet one body: so also is Christ.
13 For by one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, slaves or free—and have all been made to drink into one Spirit.
14 For the body is not one member, but many.
15 If the foot should say, "I am not a hand, therefore I am not a member of the body," would it for that reason not be a member of the body?
16 And if the ear should say, "I am not an eye, therefore I am not a member of the body," would it for that reason not be a member of the body?
17 If the whole body were an eye, where would the hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
18 But now God has placed the members, each one of them in the body, just as he desired.
19 If they were all one member, where would the body be?
20 But now there are many members, yet one body.
21 The eye cannot say to the hand, "I have no need of you," nor again the head to the feet, "I have no need of you."
22 On the contrary, those members of the body which seem to be the weakest are the most necessary.
23 And those members which we think to be less honorable, on these we bestow more abundant honor; and our unpresentable parts have more abundant beauty.
24 For our presentable parts have no need. But God has so composed the body, giving more abundant honor to the member that lacked,
25 So that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
26 And if one member suffers, all members suffer with it; and if one member is honored, all members rejoice with it.
27 Now you are the body of Christ, and members individually.
28 And God has appointed in the congregation: first, apostles; second, prophets; third, teachers; after that, miracles; then gifts of healings, helpers, administrators, various kinds of tongues.
29 Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Are all workers of miracles?
30 Do all have the gifts of healing? Do all speak with various tongues?
31 Do all interpret? Earnestly desire the best gifts. And yet I will show you a more excellent way.

### Chapter 13.

1 Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not love, I would be like a sounding brass or a tinkling bell.
2 And though I could prophesy, and understood all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I had all faith so that I could move mountains, and have not love, I would be nothing.
3 And though I gave all my goods to the poor, and let my body be burned, and have not love, it would profit me nothing.
4 Love is long-suffering and kind; love is not envious; love does not act deceitfully; it is not puffed up;
5 It does not behave rudely <note>original: "onaerdelijck"</note>, it does not seek its own, it is not easily embittered, it thinks no evil;
6 It does not rejoice in iniquity, but it rejoices in the truth;
7 It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

# The second Epistle of St. Paul to the Corinthians.

->The 4th Chapter<-

1 Therefore, since we have such a ministry, according to the mercy shown to us,

<column-break/>

2 we do not become weary. But we also renounce hidden shame, and do not walk in craftiness, nor do we corrupt God's word, but by open truth we commend ourselves to every man's conscience before God.
3 If our Gospel is now hidden, it is hidden to those who are lost,
4 In whom the God of this world has blinded the minds of the unbelievers, so that they do not see the clear light of the Gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
5 For we do not preach ourselves, but Jesus Christ, that he is the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake.
6 For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, has given a clear shine in our hearts, so that the enlightenment of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ might arise in us.
7 But we have such treasure in earthen vessels <note>The "earthen vessels" refer to human bodies, which are fragile and humble like clay jars.</note>, so that the extraordinary power may be of God and not from us.
8 We have anxiety and knowledge everywhere, but we are not troubled. We are anxious, but we do not despair.
9 We suffer persecution, but we are not forsaken. We are oppressed, but we do not perish.
10 And we always carry about in our body the dying of the Lord Jesus, so that also the life of the Lord Jesus may be made manifest in our body.
11 For we who live are always delivered unto death for Jesus' sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our mortal flesh.
12 Therefore, death is now powerful in us, but life in you.
13 But since we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written: "I believe, therefore I speak," so we also believe, and therefore we also speak,
14 And we know that he who raised up the Lord Jesus shall also raise us up through Jesus, and shall set us there with you.
15 For it all happens for your sake, so that the abundant grace, through the many thanksgivings, may praise God more richly.
16 Therefore we do not become weary; but though our outward man decays, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
17 For our affliction, which is temporal and light, brings an eternal and beyond all measure weighty glory,
18 To us, who look not at the visible, but at the invisible. For what is visible is temporal, but what is invisible is eternal.

### The 7th Chapter.

**S**ince we now have such promises, my beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and the spirit, and proceed with holiness in the fear of God. *2* Receive us; we have harmed no one, we have deceived no one, we have damaged no one. *3* I do not say this to condemn you. For you were troubled in a godly manner, so that you suffered no damage from us in any way. <margin>1 Peter 2:19.</margin> *10* For godly sorrow works for salvation a repentance that no one regrets. But the sorrow of the world works death. *11* See what this same godly sorrow has wrought in you: what diligence it has sought in you, what defense, indignation, fear, longing, zeal, and revenge. You have shown yourselves in all things to be pure in the matter. <margin>Ecclesiasticus 30:21.</margin> *12* Therefore, although I wrote to you, it was not for his sake who did the wrong, nor for his sake who suffered the wrong, but so that your diligence toward us might be made manifest among you before God. *13* Therefore we were comforted, because you were comforted. But we rejoiced even more abundantly for the joy of Titus. *14* For his spirit was refreshed by you all. -># Chapter 9.<-

<margin>Acts 11:29, 1 Corinthians 16:2. Further regarding alms and good deeds to the poor.</margin> *1* For regarding such ministry as is done for the saints, it is not necessary for me to write to you. *2* For I know your good will, of which I boast to those from Macedonia, saying: Achaia has been ready since last year; and your example has stirred up many. *3* But I have sent these brothers so that our boasting of you should not be in vain in this matter, and that you may be ready, just as I have said of you, *4* lest if those from Macedonia came with me and found you unprepared,

<column-break/>

we (not to say you) should be put to shame with such boasting. *5* Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort the brothers to go to you beforehand to prepare this previously promised blessing, so that it may be ready as a blessing and not as a matter of greed.
*6* But I mean this: He who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly; and he who sows in blessing will also reap in blessing. *7* Every man according to his will, not with reluctance or out of compulsion: for God loves a cheerful giver. *8* And God is able to make all grace abound among you, so that you, having all sufficiency in all things, may be rich in every good work,
*9* As it is written: He has dispersed and given to the poor; his righteousness remains forever. *10* (And he who gives seed to the sower will surely also give bread for food, and will multiply your seed, and increase the fruit of your righteousness.) *11* So that you are rich in all things with all simplicity, which works through us thanksgiving to God. *12* For the administration of this help not only fulfills the needs of the saints, but is also abundant in that many thank God. *13* Through this proven service, they praise God for your submissive acknowledgment of the Gospel of Christ, and for your simple ministry toward them and toward all, *14* and for their prayer for you, who long for you because of the exceeding grace of God in you.

-># Chapter 10.<-

*1* I, Paul, exhort you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, I who am lowly when present among you, but bold toward you when absent. *2* I pray that it may not be necessary for me to act boldly when present, and to use the boldness that is attributed to me against some who consider us as if we walked according to the flesh. *3* For although we walk in the flesh, yet we do not war according to the flesh. *4* For the weapons of our <term>warfare</term> <note>original: "Ridderschap," meaning knighthood or military service</note> are not fleshly, but mighty before God to pull down strongholds, with which we pull down imaginations, *5* and every high thing that exalts itself against the knowledge of God, and bring into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ, *6* and are ready to punish all disobedience when your obedience is fulfilled. *7* Do you judge by appearances? If someone trusts in himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this with himself, that just as he belongs to Christ, so we also belong to Christ. *8* And even if I boasted somewhat more of our power, which the Lord has given us to improve you and not to destroy you, I would not be ashamed. *9* (I say this so that you do not think I wanted to terrify you with letters. *10* For the letters, they say, are weighty and strong, but the presence of the body is weak, and the speech is contemptible.) *11* Let such a person think this: that just as we are in word in our letters when absent, so we will also be in deed when present. *12* For we do not dare to count or compare ourselves with those who praise themselves. ### The 5th Chapter.

1 SO stand fast now in the *freedom with which Christ has made us free, and do not let yourselves be caught again in that bondage. Behold, I Paul tell you: If you let yourselves be circumcised, then Christ is of no use to you.
3 I testify again to every man who lets himself be circumcised, that he is still obligated to do the whole Law. You have lost Christ, you who want to be made righteous through the Law, and have fallen from grace.
5 But we expect in the Spirit through faith the righteousness for which one must hope. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision nor uncircumcision counts for anything, but faith which is active through love.

12 O, I wish that they were even cut off, those who disturb you.

14 *For all Laws are fulfilled in one word, in this: You shall love your neighbor as yourself.
15 *But if you bite and devour one another, see to it that you are not consumed by one another.
16 But I say: *Walk in the Spirit, then you shall not fulfill the lusts of the flesh.
17 For the flesh lusts against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh. These same are against one another, so that you do not do what you want.
18 But if the Spirit governs you, then you are not under the Law.
19 Now the works of the flesh are manifest, which are: Adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, <note>original: "Oertelhept." Refers to wantonness or lack of restraint.</note>

21 Hatred, murder, drunkenness, gluttony, and such like, of which I have told you before, and say even now: That those who do such things shall not possess the Kingdom of God.
22 But the fruit of the Spirit is: Love, joy, peace, patience, friendliness, goodness, faith,
23 Gentleness, chastity, *against such there is no Law.
24 And those who belong to Christ crucify their flesh with its lusts and desires.

### Chapter 6.

1 <margin>Colossians 3:20.</margin> **Y**ou children, be obedient to your parents in the Lord, for that is right.
2 <margin>The duty of children, parents, and servants.</margin> Honor Father and Mother, that is the first commandment that has a promise. <margin>Exodus 20:12 / Deuteronomy 5:16. / Sirach 3:12. / Matthew 15:4.</margin>

13 <margin>Isaiah 59:17. / 1 Thessalonians 5:8. / Romans 10:15 / *Psalm 132:16.</margin> For this cause, take up the armor of God, so that you may withstand in the evil day, and having performed all things well, you may keep the field.

<meta>This page transitions from the end of the Epistle to the Ephesians to the beginning of the Epistle to the Philippians. It includes the standard apostolic greeting, Paul’s reflections on his imprisonment, and the famous exhortation to humility and the "Christ Hymn" in Chapter 2.</meta>

# The Epistle of St. Paul
## to the Philippians.

### The First Chapter.

<margin>Eph. 1:1–2</margin>
<margin>a</margin>
Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the bishops and deacons. 2 Grace be with you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

<margin>2 Thess. 1:3</margin>
<margin>Paul’s prayer for the congregation. 4</margin>
3 I thank my God every time I remember you, 4 (Which I always do in all my prayers for you all, making that prayer with joy) 5 For your fellowship in the Gospel from the first day until now. 6 <margin>John 6:29</margin> And I am confident of this very thing: that he who has begun that good work in you will also complete it until the day of Jesus Christ.

<margin>Paul imprisoned.</margin>
7 Just as it is right for me to think this of you all: because I have you in my heart, in these my bonds <note>original: "gheuanchenisse," referring to his imprisonment</note>, in which I defend and confirm the Gospel, as you are all partakers with me of grace.

<margin>Rom. 1:9</margin>
<margin>* Col. 1:3</margin>
8 For God is my witness, how I long for you all with the heart’s depth <note>original: "gront des herten," literally the ground or bottom of the heart</note> in Jesus Christ. 9 And for this I pray: * that your love may become richer and richer in all kinds of knowledge and in all kinds of discernment. 10 That you may test what is best: so that you may be pure and without offense until the day of Christ, 11 Filled with the fruits of righteousness, which happen through Jesus Christ (in you) to the honor and praise of God. 12 But I want you to know, dear Brothers, that how things stand with me has only come to the greater advancement of the Gospel. 13 So that my bonds in Christ have become well-known in the whole Palace <note>original: "Rechthuyse," referring to the Praetorium or imperial guard's headquarters</note> and to <margin>Eph. 3:13</margin> 14 all others: * And many Brothers in the Lord, having gained confidence from my bonds, have become all the bolder to speak the word without fear.

<margin>Christ is preached in all kinds of ways. 15 16</margin>
15 Some, it is true, preach Christ out of envy and strife: 16 But some out of good intention. The former proclaim Christ out of contention, and not purely, for they think they want to add affliction to my bonds. 17 But these out of love, for they know that I lie here for the defense of the Gospel. 18 But what of it? Provided that in every way Christ is proclaimed, whether by chance or in the right way, I nonetheless rejoice in that, and will also rejoice.

<margin>2 Cor. 1:11</margin>
19 For I know that this same thing shall turn to my salvation, through your prayer and the assistance of the Spirit of Jesus Christ: 20 According to my expectation and hope, that I shall be put to shame in no thing, but that with all boldness, as always before, so now also Christ shall be highly praised in my body, whether through life or through death. 21 For Christ is my life, and dying is my gain. 22 But since living in the flesh serves more to bear fruit, I do not know which I shall choose.

<margin>2 Pet. 2:14</margin>
<margin>* 2 Cor. 5:8</margin>
23 * For I am troubled in my heart by both: I have a desire to depart and to be with Christ, which would also be much better; 24 But it is more necessary to remain in the flesh for your sake. 25 And in good confidence I know that I shall remain and be with you all, for your advancement and for the joy of faith, 26 That you may boast greatly in Christ Jesus regarding me,

<column-break/>

27 through my coming to you again. * Only walk worthily of the Gospel of Christ: so that whether I come and see you, or being absent, I may hear that you stand in one spirit, in one soul, and strive with us in the faith of the Gospel. 28 And let yourselves be in no way terrified by the adversaries, which is a proof of their destruction, but to you of salvation, and that from God. 29 For it is given to you for Christ's sake to act, that you not only believe in him, but also suffer for his sake, 30 and have the same struggle which you have seen in me and now hear of me.

### The Second Chapter.

<margin>a</margin>
1 If there is now any exhortation in Christ, if there is any comfort of love, if there is any fellowship of the spirit, if there is any heartfelt love and mercy, then fulfill my joy, so that you * are of one mind, having the same love, being in harmony and of one accord: 2 and do [nothing] through strife or vain glory, but through humility, let each count the other higher than himself. 4 * And let no one look to his own [interests], but to that which belongs to another. 5 Let everyone be minded as Jesus Christ also was. 6 Who (although he * was in divine form) did not consider it a robbery <note>original: "roof," referring to the Greek *harpagmos*, something to be grasped or held onto selfishly</note> to be equal to God, 7 * But emptied himself and took on the form of a servant, * became like another man, and was found in appearance as a man, 8 and humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even to death on the Cross. 9 Therefore God has also exalted him and given him a Name which is above all names. 10 That in the Name of Jesus * every knee shall bow, of those in Heaven and on Earth and under the Earth, 11 And all tongues shall confess * that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. 12 Therefore my beloved, as you have been obedient, not only in my presence, but now much more in my absence, work so that you become saved with fear and trembling. 13 For it is God who works in you, both the will and the doing, according to his good pleasure. 14 * Do all things without murmuring and without doubting. 15 so that you are without fault and pure, children of God, blameless * in the midst of the degenerate and perverse generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world. 16 In this, that you hold fast to the word of life, as a * boast in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, nor labored in vain. 17 And even if I am offered as a sacrifice over the offering and service of God for your faith, I rejoice, and I rejoice with you all: 18 For this same reason you shall also rejoice, and you shall rejoice with me.

<margin>b</margin>

For as a child serves a father, he has served with me in the Gospel: 23 I hope to send him immediately, as soon as I have learned how things stand with me. 24 And I trust in the Lord that I myself shall also come shortly. 25 But I have considered it necessary to send the brother Epaphroditus to you, who is my helper and fellow soldier and your Apostle <note>original: "Apostel," here meaning messenger or envoy</note>, and the minister to my needs: 26 Since he had a longing for you all...

### The 3rd Chapter.

<margin>Isa. 56:11, 2 / Rom. 2:29, 3 / Col. 2:11</margin>
1 **F**urthermore, dear brothers, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you always does not weary me, and it makes you the more certain.
2 Watch out for the dogs, watch out for the evil workers, watch out for the circumcision <note>original: "besnijdinge"; here Paul uses the term mockingly to refer to those who insist on ritual legalism</note>.
3 For we are the circumcision, we who serve God in the spirit and boast in Christ Jesus, and do not rely on the flesh,
<margin>2 Cor. 12:9</margin>
4 Although I also might have reason to boast in the flesh. If anyone else thinks he may boast in the flesh, I even more:
5 I who was circumcised on the eighth day, one of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews, and according to the Law, a Pharisee,
<margin>Acts 8:3, 6 / Gal. 1:13 / Phil. 1:26 / Isa. 53:14 / John 17:3</margin>
6 According to zeal, a persecutor of the Church; according to the righteousness which is in the Law, I was blameless.
7 But what was gain to me, that I have counted as loss for Christ's sake.
8 For I count all things as loss against the exceeding knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whose sake I have counted all things as loss, and hold them to be dung <note>original: "drec," referring to refuse or waste</note>, so that I may win Christ,
<margin>Rom. 1:17</margin>
9 And be found in him, that I may not have my own righteousness, which is from the Law, but that which comes through faith in Christ, namely, the righteousness which is credited by God to faith,
10 To know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his suffering, that I may become like him in his death,
<margin>Rom. 6:4 / Resurrection of the dead.</margin>
11 So that I may attain to the resurrection of the dead.
12 Not that I have already grasped it, or am already perfect: but I press on after it, if I might also grasp it, since I am grasped by Christ Jesus.
<margin>The Apostle's diligence in God's commandments.</margin>
13 My brothers, I do not yet count myself as having grasped it: but one thing I say: I forget what is behind, and I reach out to that which is ahead,
14 And I press toward the set mark for the prize <note>original: "Cleynodie," meaning a jewel or precious prize</note>, which is held out by the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus.
15 As many of us as are perfect, let us be thus minded. And if you think otherwise in anything, God shall reveal that to you.
<margin>Rom. 12:16 / 1 Cor. 1:9 / 1 Cor. 4:16 / 1 Thess. 1:6, 18</margin>
16 Nevertheless, as far as we have come, let us walk by the same rule and be of the same mind.
17 Follow me, dear brothers, and look to those who walk according to the example you have in us.
18 For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ,
<margin>Rom. 16:17</margin>
19 Whose end is damnation, whose God is their belly, and whose glory becomes their shame, who are earthly minded.
<margin>1 Cor. 15:51 / Titus 2:13 / Matt. 13:43 / 1 John 3:2</margin>
20 But our citizenship is in heaven, from whence we also look for the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ:
21 Who shall transform our lowly body, that it may become like his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is also able to subdue all things to himself.

### The 4th Chapter.

<margin>Luke 10:20 / Rev. 17:8 / 1 Thess. 5:16</margin>
1 **T**herefore, my dear and longed-for brothers, my joy and my crown, stand fast thus in the Lord, you beloved.
2 I exhort Euodia, and I exhort Syntyche, that they be of one mind in the Lord.
3 And I also ask you, my faithful companion <note>original: "gheselle," referring to a close associate or yokefellow</note>, help those women who have struggled with me in the Gospel, with Clement and my other helpers, whose names are in the Book of Life.
4 Rejoice in the Lord always, and again I say: Rejoice.
<margin>Matt. 6:25 / 1 Pet. 5:7 / Psa. 54:22</margin>
5 Let your friendliness be known to all men.
6 The Lord is at hand. Be anxious for nothing, but in all things let your requests be made known before God in prayer and supplication with thanksgiving.
<margin>Eph. 2:13</margin>
7 And the peace of God, which is higher than all understanding, guard your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
8 Furthermore, dear brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honest, whatever is right, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is of good report; if there be any virtue, if there be any praise, think on these things,
<margin>Isa. 9:5</margin>
9 Which you have also learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me; do that, and the God of peace shall be with you.
10 But I am greatly rejoiced in the Lord that you have become active again in caring for me, though you always cared; but the time did not permit it.
<margin>1 Tim. 6:8</margin>
11 I do not say this because of want, for I have learned to be content with whatever state I am in.
12 I know how to be low, and I know how to be high. In all things and among you all I am prepared both to be full and to be hungry, both to have plenty and to suffer want.
13 I can do all things through Christ who makes me powerful.
14 Nevertheless, you have done well that you took part in my distress.
15 But you Philippians know that from the beginning of the Gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no congregation shared with me in the account of giving and receiving, but you alone.
16 For even in Thessalonica you sent once and then again to my necessity.
17 Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that it may be abundant in your account.
18 For I have all things and have abundance; I am fully supplied since I received from Epaphroditus what came from you, a sweet-smelling savor, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God.
19 My God shall fulfill all your need according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
20 Now to God and our Father be glory forever, Amen.
21 Greet all the saints in Christ Jesus. The brothers who are with me greet you.
22 All the saints greet you, and especially those of Caesar's household <note>original: "Keysers huyse," referring to members of the Roman Imperial civil service or family</note>.
23 The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all, Amen.

->Written from Rome, by Epaphroditus.<-

# The First Epistle of St. Paul to Timothy.

### The First Chapter.

1 Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the command of God our Savior, and of the Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope.
2 To Timothy, my true son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ.
3 As I exhorted you to remain at Ephesus when I went into Macedonia, so that you might command some that they teach no other doctrine,
4 nor *give heed to fables and genealogies which have no end, and bring about more questions than edification for God in the faith.
5 For the sum of the commandment is: Love from a pure heart, and from a good conscience, and from unfeigned faith.
6 From which some have missed the mark and have turned aside to idle <term>chatter<note>original: "clappen" — empty or foolish talk</note></term>;
7 wanting to be masters of the Scripture, yet they do not understand what they say or what they affirm.
8 *But we know that the Law is good, if a man uses it rightly:
9 knowing this, namely, that the Law is not given for the righteous, but for the unrighteous and disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the unholy and profane, for those who kill fathers and mothers, for manslayers,
10 for whoremongers, for <term>perverts<note>original: "Jongenschenders" — an archaic term for those who engage in pederasty or male-male sexual acts</note></term>, for kidnappers, for liars, for the perjured, and if there be anything else that is against sound doctrine,
11 according to the glorious Gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.
12 And I thank our Lord Christ Jesus, who has made me strong and accounted me faithful, and put me into the Ministry,
13 I who was previously a blasphemer, *and a persecutor, and an insulter. But mercy was shown to me, because I did it *ignorantly in unbelief.
14 But the grace of our Lord was all the more abundant, together with the faith and the love which is in Christ Jesus.
15 This is a certainly true and precious, worthy word: *That Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, among whom I am the foremost.
16 But for this reason mercy was shown to me, so that in me especially Jesus Christ might show all patience, as an example to those who should believe in him for eternal life.
17 Now to God the eternal *King, the immortal and *invisible, and only wise God, be honor and praise forever and ever, Amen.
18 This commandment I commit to you, my son Timothy, according to the previous prophecies over you, so that in them you might wage a good warfare,
19 and have faith and a good conscience, which some have cast away from them and have suffered shipwreck of their faith.
20 Among whom are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I have delivered to Satan, so that they may be taught not to blaspheme anymore.

2 for all people, for Kings, and for all in authority, so that we may lead a quiet and still life in all godliness and honesty.

Now to God the eternal * King, the immortal and invisible, the only Wise [God], be honor and praise forever and ever, Amen.

# The Second Epistle
## Of St. Paul to Timothy.

### The First Chapter.

<margin>1</margin> Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, according to the promise of life, which is in Christ Jesus. To my dearly beloved son Timo- <margin>2</margin> thy. Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father, and <margin>3</margin> Christ Jesus our Lord. I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with a pure conscience, that without ceasing I have remembrance of you in my prayers night and day; <margin>4</margin> Greatly desiring to see you (being mindful of your tears), that I may be filled with <margin>5</margin> joy; When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois, and in your mother Eunice; and I am persuaded <margin>6</margin> that it is in you also. For which cause I remind you to stir up the gift of God, which is in you by the putting on of my <margin>7</margin> hands. For God has not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of <margin>8</margin> love, and of a sound mind. Therefore be not ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me His prisoner; but be a partaker of the afflictions of the Gospel according to the power <margin>9</margin> of God. Who has saved us, and called us with a holy calling. Not according to our works, but according to His own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before <margin>10</margin> the world began. But is now made manifest by the appearing of our Savior Jesus Christ, who has abolished the power of Death, and has brought life and an immortal being to light through the <margin>11</margin> Gospel. Whereunto I am appointed a Preacher, and an Apostle, and a Teacher of the Gen- <margin>12</margin> tiles: For which cause I also suffer these things.

17 And their word eats <margin>1 Tim. 1:20; 1 Cor. 15:12</margin> about it like a cancer <note>original: "Kancker" — often translated as gangrene in modern bibles, implying a spreading rot</note>: among whom are Hymenaeus and Philetus,
18 Who have missed the truth, saying: The resurrection has already happened, and they have subverted the <margin>John 10:14; Rom. 9:21. The gold, silver, and earthen vessels.</margin> faith of some.
19 But the firm foundation of God stands and has this Seal: "The Lord knows his own: and let everyone who names the Name of Christ depart from iniquity.
20 But in a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and earth. And some to honor, but some to dishonor.
21 If anyone cleanses himself from <margin>1 Tim. 6:11</margin> such people, he shall be a sanctified vessel, for honor, useful to the Master of the house, and prepared for every good work.

## Chapter 3.

1 But you shall know this: * That in the <margin>1 Tim. 4:1. 2 Pet. 3:3.</margin> last days, terrible times shall come.
2 For there shall be people in the last times who love themselves much, greedy, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy,
3 Harsh, stubborn, irreconcilable, slanderers, unchaste, wild, without goodness,
4 Traitors, reckless, puffed up, who love pleasure more than God,
5 Who have the appearance of a godly being, but they deny its power. And such <margin>Matt. 18:18</margin> avoid.
6 Of this sort are those who creep here and there <margin>* Tit. 1:11.</margin> into houses and lead captive weak women <note>original: "Wijfkes" — a diminutive and often disparaging term for women in this context</note> who are burdened with sins and led astray by various lusts,
7 Always learning, and yet never able to come to the knowledge of the truth.
8 <margin>Exod. 7:11.</margin> But just as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also withstand the truth. These are people of corrupt minds, unfit for the faith,
9 But they shall not proceed further. For their folly shall be manifest to all people, just as theirs also was.
10 But you have followed my teaching, my manner, my intent, my faith, my longsuffering, my love, my patience,
11 My persecutions, my sufferings, <margin>The cross * Acts 13:50.</margin> which happened to me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I suffered there, and the Lord delivered me from them all.
12 <margin>2 Cor. 1:10 *Psa. 34:20; Luke 24:25.</margin> "And all who desire to live godlily in Christ Jesus must suffer persecution.
13 But with wicked people and deceivers, it will grow worse and worse; they deceive and are deceived.
14 <margin>2 Tim. 1:13</margin> But you, remain in that which you have learned and has been entrusted to you. For you know from whom you have learned it.
15 And because you have known the holy Scripture from childhood, it can instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
16 <margin>2 Pet. 1:21</margin> "All scripture given by God is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness,
17 That a person of God may be perfect, equipped for every good work.

## Chapter 4.

2 Preach the word, persist, whether it be at the right time or the wrong time; reprove, threaten, exhort with all patience and teaching.
3 For there shall be a time when they will not endure sound teaching, but according to their own lusts, they shall heap up teachers for themselves,
4 According to which their ears itch; and they shall turn their ears away from the truth and turn themselves to fables.
5 But you, be sober in all things, endure, do the work of an Evangelical Preacher, fulfill your office reasonably.
6 For I am <margin>2 Pet. 1:14</margin> already being offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.
7 I have fought a good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith.

Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God's elect, and the knowledge of the truth leading to godliness in the hope of eternal life.
2 Which God, who does not lie, promised before the times of the world,
3 but has revealed his word in due time through the preaching which is entrusted to me, according to the command of God our Savior.
4 To Titus, my true son according to our common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, our 
5 Savior. For this reason I left you in Crete, that you should set in order the things I left behind and appoint elders in every city, 
6 as I commanded you. * If anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children who are not accused of being gluttons <note>original: "Swelgers" — those given to excess or riotous living</note> or disobedient.
7 For a Bishop must be blameless, as a steward of God; not stubborn, not quick-tempered, not a wine-drinker, not violent, 
8 not pursuing dishonest gain. But hospitable, kind, disciplined, righteous, holy, chaste,
9 and holding fast to the word that is certain and can teach: so that he may be able to exhort through sound doctrine and to convict the gainsayers.
10 For there are many rebellious and empty talkers and deceivers, especially 

<column-break/>

11 those who must have their mouths stopped. Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses and teach what is not proper for the sake of shameful gain.

16 They say they know God, but in works they deny him, seeing as they are those whom God finds abominable, and they do not listen, and are useless for every good work.

### The second Chapter.

1 But you, speak what is fitting for sound doctrine. 
2 That the older men be sober, honest, disciplined, sound in faith, in love, in patience.
3 The older women likewise, that they behave as becomes the holy, not being slanderers, not being wine-drinkers, 
4 but teachers of good things: That they may teach the young women to be disciplined, to love their husbands, to love their children, 
5 to be discreet, chaste, homemakers, kind, obedient to their husbands, so that the word of God be not blasphemed.
6 Likewise, exhort the young men to be disciplined.
7 But above all, set yourself as an example of good works, with uncorrupted teaching, with honesty, with sound and blameless words,
8 so that the opponent may be ashamed and have nothing evil to say of us.
9 Exhort servants <note>original: "knechten" — slaves or servants</note> to be obedient to their masters, to please them in all things, not talking back,
10 not being unfaithful, but showing all good fidelity, so that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Savior 
11 in all things. For the saving grace of God has appeared to all men,
12 and instructs us that we should renounce ungodliness and worldly lusts, and live soberly, righteously, and godly in this world,
13 looking for that blessed hope and the appearing of the glory of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ,
14 who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people for a possession, who are zealous for good works.
15 Say these things and exhort and rebuke with all seriousness. Let no one despise you.

5 not for the sake of works of righteousness which we had done, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the bath of regeneration <note>original: "Badt der wedergheboozten" — the washing or baptism of rebirth</note> and renewal of the Holy Spirit.

Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother. To Philemon the beloved and our helper, and to Apphia the beloved, and to Archippus our fellow-soldier, and to the Church in your house. Grace be with you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. I thank my God, always remembering you in my prayers, since I hear of the love and the faith which you have toward the Lord Jesus and toward all saints; that the sharing of your faith may become powerful in you through the knowledge of every good thing that you have in Christ Jesus. For we have great joy and comfort in your love, because the hearts of the saints are refreshed by you, dear brother.

Therefore, although I have great boldness in Christ to command you what is fitting, yet for love's sake I would rather appeal to you—I, being such a one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. I appeal to you for my son Onesimus, whom I have *begotten in my bonds; who in times past was useless to you, but now is very useful to both you and me. I have sent him back to you. And you, receive him (that is, my own heart). For I wanted to keep him with me, that he might serve me in your stead in the bonds of the Gospel. But without your consent I would do nothing, so that your good deed might not be by compulsion, but voluntary. For perhaps he departed from you for a while for this reason: that you might receive him back forever; no longer as a servant <note>original: "knecht" - meaning a bondservant or slave</note>, but more than a servant, a beloved brother, especially to me, and how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord? # The Second Epistle of St. Peter.

<margin>What virtues one shall show toward faith.</margin>
5 For this reason, apply all your diligence to this: demonstrate virtue in your faith, and in virtue, discretion; and in discretion, temperance; and in temperance, patience; and in patience, godliness;
7 and in godliness, brotherly love; and in brotherly love, common love for all. <note>The Dutch "gemepne liefde" refers to universal charity or love for all people, distinct from specific "brotherly love" for fellow believers.</note>
8 For if such things are in you in abundance, they will not let you be idle or unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
9 But he who does not have these things is blind, groping with his hand for the way, and forgets the purification of his former sins.
<margin>That one shall be diligent to confirm our calling.</margin>
10 Therefore, dear brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure. For if you do this, you shall not stumble.
11 And in this way, the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ shall be richly given to you.
<margin>That it is necessary to exhort each other daily.</margin>
12 Therefore, I will not neglect to remind you always of such things, even though you know them and are established in the present truth.
13 For I consider it right, as long as I am in this Tabernacle, <note>Original: "Hutte" (hut/tent), a metaphor for the physical body.</note> to stir you up and to exhort you.
<margin>2 Tim. 4:26</margin>
14 For I know that I must soon lay aside my tabernacle, as our Lord Jesus has also revealed to me.
15 But I will be diligent so that after my departure, you may have these things in your memory.
<margin>1 Cor. 1:15–16; 2 Thess. 1:5</margin>
16 For we have not followed clever fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; rather, we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
<margin>Matt. 17:2; 1 John 1:1. A testimony of the Father regarding Christ! Mark 9:7; Luke 9:35</margin>
17 When he received honor and praise from God the Father, through a voice that came to him from the Great Glory in this manner: !! "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
18 And we heard this voice brought from Heaven when we were with him on the holy Mountain.
19 We have a firm Prophetic word, and you do well to pay attention to it, as to a Light that shines in a dark place, until the day breaks and the morning Star rises in your hearts.
<margin>2 Cor. 4:6</margin>
20 and you should know this first: that no Prophecy in the scripture comes from one's own interpretation.
<margin>Prophecy from Prophets. Dan. 9:10; Zech. 7:12; 2 Tim. 3:16</margin>

### The 2nd Chapter.

<margin>Matt. 24:11; Acts 20:29; 1 Tim. 4:1. Warning against false teachers.</margin>
1 But there were also false Prophets among the people, just as there shall be false Teachers among you, who will secretly introduce harmful Sects and deny the Lord who bought them, and shall bring upon themselves a swift damnation.
2 And many shall follow their destruction, by whom the way of truth shall be blasphemed.
<margin>Matt. 7:13</margin>
3 And through greed, with fabricated words, they shall exploit you; for whom the judgment from long ago is not lingering, and their damnation does not sleep.
<margin>Job 4:9; Jude 6</margin>
4 For if God did not spare the Angels who sinned, but cast them down to Hell with chains of darkness and delivered them to be kept for judgment.
<margin>Gen. 7:21. The punishment of the godless is an example to us.</margin>
5 And if he did not spare the world of old, but preserved Noah, the Preacher of righteousness, being the eighth person, and brought the flood over the world of the godless.
<margin>Gen. 19:24; Isa. 13:19</margin>
6 And turned the Cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes, overthrew and condemned them, thereby setting an Example

<column-break/>

for the godless who should come hereafter.
7 And he rescued Righteous Lot, who was greatly distressed by the shameful people and their immoral conduct.
8 For while he was righteous and lived among them, as he had to see and hear them, they tormented his righteous soul from day to day with their unrighteous works.
9 *The Lord knows how to deliver the Godly out of temptation, but to keep the unrighteous to be punished on the day of judgment.*
10 But most of all those who walk after the flesh in unclean lust and despise authority—daring, headstrong, they are not afraid to blaspheme Majesties. <note>Original: "Maiestepten," referring to high-ranking authorities or celestial beings.</note>
11 Whereas the Angels, who have greater power and strength, do not bring a blasphemous judgment against them before the Lord.
12 But these are like irrational animals, born by nature to be caught and slaughtered. They blaspheme what they do not understand, and shall perish in their own corruption and receive the reward of unrighteousness.
13 They consider it a pleasure to live in luxury for a time. They are spots and blemishes, carousing on your Alms and living off of yours.
14 They have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin, and they entice unstable souls; they have hearts trained in greed—cursed children!
15 They have forsaken the right way and gone astray, !! following the way of Balaam, the son of Beor, <note>Original: "Bosoz," a variant spelling of Beor.</note> who loved the reward of unrighteousness.
16 But he received a punishment for his transgression, for the dumb beast of burden spoke with a human voice and restrained the Prophet's madness.
17 These are fountains without water and clouds driven by a storm wind, for whom dark darkness is reserved for eternity. For they speak boastful words that amount to nothing, and they entice through the debauchery of fleshly lusts those people who had just escaped and now walk in folly. They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption. For by whatever someone is overcome, to that he has become a slave.
20 !! For if they have escaped the uncleanness of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, and are again entangled and overcome in the same, the last state has become worse for them than the first.
21 For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it *and turn away from the holy commandment that was given to them.*
22 The true Proverb has happened to them: *The dog returns to what he has vomited.* And: The sow that was washed wallows again in the mire.

### The 3rd Chapter.

1 This is the second Epistle that I write to you, beloved, in which I stir up and exhort your pure mind,
2 that you remember the words which were spoken before by the holy Prophets, and our commandment, we who are the Apostles of the Lord and Savior.
3 *And know this first: that in the last days scoffers shall come, walking after their own lusts, and saying:*
4 "Where is the promise of his coming? For since the Fathers fell asleep, all things remain as they have been from the beginning of Creation."
5 But they are willfully ignorant of this: that the Heavens were of old, and also the Earth standing out of the water and in the water, by the word of God.

### The 4th Chapter.

1 Beloved, *do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are of God. For many false prophets have gone out into the world. 2 By this you shall know the Spirit of God: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God. 3 And every spirit that does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God. And this is the spirit of the Antichrist, of which you have heard that it should come, and it is now already in the world. 4 Little children, you are of God and have overcome them. For he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world. 5 They are of the world; therefore they speak of the world, and the world hears them. 6 We are of God, *and whoever knows God hears us. Whoever is not of God does not hear us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error. 7 Beloved, let us love one another. For love is of God; and everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. 8 He who does not love does not know God, for God is love. 9 *By this the love of God was manifested toward us: that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, so that we might live through him. 10 In this is love: not that we loved God, but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the reconciliation <note>Original: "versoeninge," referring to the atonement or propitiation for sins.</note> for our sins. 11 Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another. 12 *No one has ever seen God. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love is perfected in us. 13 *By this we know that we remain in him and he in us: because he has given us of his Spirit. 14 And we have seen and do testify that the Father has sent the Son to be a Savior of the world. 15 Whoever now confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God remains in him and he in God. 16 And we have known and believed the love that God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God in him. 17 In this, love is perfected with us, so that we may have boldness on the day of judgment; because as he is, so are we also in this world. 18 There is no fear in love; but perfect love drives out fear, because fear involves pain <note>Original: "pijn," usually translated in this context as "torment" or "punishment."</note>. And he who fears is not perfected in love. 19 Let us love him, for he has first loved us. 20 *If someone says, "I love God," and hates his brother, he is a liar. For he who does not love his brother, whom he sees, how can he love God, whom he does not see? 21 *And this commandment we have from him: that whoever loves God should also love his brother.

Therefore we will now leave behind the teaching of the beginning of the Christian life, and reach for perfection: not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith in God, of Baptism, of Doctrine, of the laying on of hands, of the resurrection of the dead, and of the eternal judgment. For when God promised Abraham, since he had no greater to swear by, * he swore by himself, and 14 spoke: * "Truly I will * bless you and multiply you." And so he remained patient, and obtained the promise. Men indeed swear by a greater than they are, and the oath makes an end of all strife, as it remains firm among them. But God, when he wanted to prove abundantly to the heirs of the promise that his counsel is unchangeable, added an oath to it, so that we through two things that are unchangeable (because it is impossible for God to lie) might have a strong comfort, we who have taken refuge and hold fast to the offered hope, which we have as a sure and firm Anchor of our soul, which also enters into the interior of the veil, 20 where the Forerunner has entered for us, Jesus, having become a high Priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
