<meta>This page continues the Epistle to the Hebrews, moving from the general call to spiritual maturity into a detailed theological argument comparing the priesthood of Melchizedek to that of Aaron, and establishing Jesus as the mediator of a New Covenant. It covers the entirety of Chapter 7, Chapter 8, and the beginning of Chapter 9.</meta>

<header>The Epistle.</header>

<margin>Genesis 14:18.
Thus Melchizedek's priesthood, looking toward Jesus Christ, who is greater than Aaron’s priesthood.</margin>

### The 7th Chapter.

<margin>1</margin> **T**his Melchizedek was a King of Salem, a Priest of the Most High God, who met Abraham as he returned from the slaughter of the kings, <margin>2</margin> and blessed him: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth of all his goods. First, his name is interpreted <note>original: "verdupt," literally "dubbed" or "named"</note> as a King of Righteousness: And after that, he is also a King of Salem, which is a <margin>3</margin> King of Peace. Without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but he is made like unto the Son of God, and remains a Priest <margin>4</margin> forever. But consider how great this man is, to whom even Abraham the Patriarch gave the tenth <margin>5</margin> of the captured spoils. It is true, the <margin>Numbers 18:21. Joshua 14:4.</margin> children of Levi, who receive the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes from the people according to the Law—that is, from their brothers—even though they also <margin>6</margin> came out of the loins of Abraham. But he, whose genealogy is not counted among them, took tithes from Abraham and blessed him who had the <margin>7</margin> promises. Now it is beyond all contradiction that the lesser is <margin>8</margin> blessed by the better. And here, mortal men receive tithes; but there, he receives them of whom it is witnessed that <margin>9</margin> he lives. And so to speak: Levi, who receives tithes, also paid tithes through Abraham: <margin>10</margin> For he was still in the loins of his father when Melchizedek met him.

<margin>Romans 3:20. Galatians 2:22.</margin> <margin>11</margin> Now if perfection had been achieved through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people received the Law), what further need was there to say that another Priest should arise according to the order of Melchizedek, <margin>12</margin> and not according to the order of Aaron? For where the priesthood is changed, there must also <margin>13</margin> be a change of the Law. For he of whom these things are spoken belongs to another tribe, from which no one has ever served at the Altar.

<margin>Isaiah 11:2. Matthew 1:3.</margin> <margin>14</margin> For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Judah, regarding which tribe <margin>15</margin> Moses spoke nothing concerning the priesthood. And it is yet far more clear, if another Priest arises after the likeness of Melchizedek, who is made not according to the law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of <margin>16</margin> an endless life. For he testifies: You <margin>Hebrews 5:4.</margin> are a Priest forever, according to the order of <margin>17</margin> Melchizedek. For thereby the preceding law is set aside (because it was too weak <margin>18</margin> and of no use. For the Law could make nothing perfect) and a <margin>Romans 8:3. Office of the Law.</margin> better hope is introduced, through which we draw near to God.

<margin>19</margin> And furthermore, which is much, this was not without an Oath. For those others became priests without an Oath, <margin>20</margin> but this one with an Oath, through him who <margin>Psalm 110:4.</margin> says to him: The Lord has sworn, and will not repent: You are a Priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.

<margin>21</margin> By so much more has Jesus become the guarantor <note>original: "wtrichteer," meaning executor or one who carries out</note> of a better Testament. And there were many <margin>22</margin> who became priests there, because <margin>23</margin> death did not allow them to remain. But this man, because he remains forever, has an unchangeable priesthood: Therefore he can also <margin>24</margin> save forever those who come to God through him, as he lives always to pray for them in their misery.

<margin>1 Timothy 2:6. 1 John 2:1.</margin> <margin>25</margin> For such a High Priest was fitting for us: one who is holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, <margin>26</margin> and made higher than the heavens: who <margin>Leviticus 16:6.</margin> does not need, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifice daily, first for his own sins and then for the people's sins. For he did this once and for all, when <margin>Hebrews 9:13.</margin> <margin>27</margin> he offered himself. For the Law appoints men

<column-break/>

as high priests who have weakness: but the word of the Oath, which came after the Law, appoints the Son, who is eternal and perfect.

### The 8th Chapter.

<margin>1</margin> **T**his is now the sum of what we are speaking. We have such a High Priest, who sits at the right hand of the throne of Majesty in Heaven, <margin>2</margin> and is a minister of holy things, and of the true Tabernacle <note>original: "hutten," literally "huts" or "tents"</note> which God set up, and not man. For every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices. Therefore this one must also have something <margin>3</margin> to offer. If he were now on earth, he would not be a priest, seeing that there are priests who offer gifts according to the law, who serve the copy and <margin>4</margin> shadow of heavenly things, just as God answered and spoke to Moses when he was about to finish the Tabernacle: See to it, he said, that you make all things according to the pattern <margin>5</margin> shown to you on the Mountain. But now he has <margin>6</margin> obtained a better Office, as he is the mediator of a better Testament <note>The early Dutch translations often use "Testament" for "Covenant"</note>: which is established upon better promises. For if that <margin>7</margin> first one had been blameless, then no place would have been sought for a second.

<margin>8</margin> For he finds fault with them and says: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, that I will make a new Testament with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah: Not according to the Testament that <margin>9</margin> I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. For they did not remain in my Testament, so I did not regard them, says the Lord.

<margin>10</margin> For this is the Testament that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law in their minds, and in their hearts I will write them. And I will <margin>11</margin> be their God, and they shall be my people. And no one shall teach his neighbor, nor anyone his brother, saying: Know the Lord. For they shall all know me, from the least <margin>12</margin> to the greatest. For I will be merciful toward their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquity I will remember no more. In that he says: A New one, he makes <margin>13</margin> the first one old. But what is old and obsolete is near to its end.

But behind the second curtain was the Tabernacle, which is called the <margin>3</margin> Most Holy Place, which had the golden <margin>4</margin> censer and the Ark of the Testament, overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was the golden jar <note>original: "Emer," an omer or vessel</note> that held the heavenly bread, and Aaron’s rod that had budded, and the tables of the Testament; and above it <margin>5</margin> were the Cherubim of glory, overshadowing the Mercy Seat—of which things we cannot now speak in detail. When <margin>6</margin> these things were thus prepared, the priests went always into the first Tabernacle, performing the divine service. But into the second, only the high priest went once <margin>7</margin> a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the people's ignorance. By this the Holy Spirit <margin>8</margin> signified that the way to salvation was not yet made manifest, as long as the first Tabernacle was still standing. # The viij. Chapter.

And when he opened the seventh Seal, there was a silence in Heaven for about half an hour. And I saw seven Angels who stood before God, and to them were given seven Trumpets. And another Angel came and stood by the Altar, and had a golden censer: And much incense was given to him, that he should give it to the prayers of all the Saints, upon the golden Altar before the throne.

<margin>Psa. 141:a.2; Rev. 5:b.8.</margin>
And the smoke of the incense from the prayers of the Saints went up from the hand of the Angel before God. And the Angel took the censer, and filled it with fire from the Altar, and cast it upon the Earth. And then there were voices, and thunders, and lightnings, and earthquakes. And the seven Angels with the seven Trumpets prepared themselves to sound the trumpets. And the first Angel sounded, and there was hail and fire mixed with blood, and it fell upon the Earth: And the third part of the trees was burned, and all the green grass was burned. And the second Angel sounded: And something like a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the Sea: And the third part of the Sea became blood: And the third part of the living Creatures in the Sea died: And the third part of the ships were destroyed. And the third Angel sounded, and there fell a great star from Heaven, burning like a torch: And it fell upon the third part of the water-streams, and over the fountains of water: And the name of the Star is called Wormwood <note>original: "Alsem"</note>. And the third part became Wormwood. And many people died from the waters, because they had become so bitter. And the fourth Angel sounded, and the third part of the Sun was struck, and the third part of the Moon, and the third part of the Stars, so that their third part was darkened. And the night likewise. And I saw, and heard an Angel flying through the midst of Heaven, and saying with a loud voice: Woe, woe, woe to those who live on Earth, because of the other voices of the Trumpets of the three Angels who are yet to sound.

2 And the first went his way, and poured out his bowl upon the Earth. And there became a foul and evil sore upon the men who had the mark of the beast, and those who worshipped his image.

3 And the second Angel poured out his bowl into the sea. And it became blood as of a dead man, and every living soul died in the sea.

4 And the third Angel poured out his bowl into the rivers and the water fountains, and they became blood.

5 And I heard an Angel say: Lord, you are righteous, who is, and who was, and holy, that you have judged such things.

<margin>Matt. 23:e.</margin>

7 And I heard another Angel out of the Altar say: Even so, Lord Almighty God, your judgments are true and righteous.

8 And the fourth Angel poured out his bowl into the sun, and it was given to him to scorch men with fire.

9 And men were scorched with great heat, and blasphemed the Name of God who has power over these plagues, and did not repent to give him the glory.

10 And the fifth Angel poured out his bowl upon the seat of the beast, and his kingdom was darkened, and they bit their tongues for pain,

11 And blasphemed the God in Heaven because of their pains and because of their sores, and did not repent of their works.

<margin>2 Thess. 2:b.</margin>
12 And the sixth Angel poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, and the water thereof dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the Kings from the rising of the Sun.

<margin>Rev. 13:c.14</margin>
13 And I saw out of the mouth of the Dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false Prophet, three unclean spirits go, like frogs.

<margin>2 Pet. 3:b.10 Matt. 24:d.43 2 Cor. 5:a.3</margin>
14 For they are spirits of devils, who do signs, and go out to the Kings on Earth, and upon the whole compass of the world, to gather them together to the battle, on that great day of God the Almighty.

15 Behold, I come as a thief: Blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments, so that he does not walk naked and that they do not see his shame.

<meta>This page serves as the beginning of an alphabetical index or glossary of Biblical names, following the conclusion of the New Testament. It provides etymological explanations for Hebrew, Aramaic (referred to as Syriac/Chaldean), and Greek proper names found in the scriptures.</meta>

# An explanation of the proper Hebrew,
## Chaldean, and Greek Names which
### are found in the Bible.

**Aaron**: a mountain, or a man of the mountain.
**Abba**: father; it is a Syriac word <note>Syriac in this period often referred to Aramaic</note>.
**Abbarim**: a passage, a passing through, or passersby.
**Abdemelech**: a servant of the King.
**Abed-Nego**: a servant of light.
**Abdia**: a servant of the Lord.
**Abdon**: a servant.
**Abel**: with an *aleph* at the beginning <note>original: "met een aleph inden beginne"</note>, is the name of a city called Abel, and is translated as "mourning."
**Abel**: with an *h* at the beginning <note>original: "met een h. inden beghinne"</note>, was a son of Adam, and is translated as "vanity."
**Abia**: the father of the Lord.
**Abiather**: an exalted father.
**Abigail**: a Father of rejoicing.
**Abimelech**: Father of the King.
**Abinadab**: a father of his good pleasure.
**Abisag**: the ignorance of the father.
**Abner**: the Lamp of the father.
**Abza**: a Greek word; means Chambermaid or servant girl.
**Abram**: exalted Father.
**Abraham**: a father of many.
**Absalon**: a father of peace.
**Acam**: Tribulation.
**Accaron**: barrenness.
**Achab**: a brother of the Father.
**Achaia**: pain or sadness.
**Achay**: seizing or possessing.
**Achimelech**: my brother the King.
**Achitop**: brother of the servant.
**Ada**: human, or from the earth, or reddish.
**Adon**: Lord or humility.
**Adonai**: my Lord; this is one of the names of God.
**Adonias**: Lord or Ruler.
**Egypt**: distress or tribulation; in Hebrew, *Mizraim* <note>original: "Misrahim"</note>.
**Aeneas**: praised.
**Ethiopia**: a Greek word; means heat. In Hebrew, *Cush* <note>original: "Cus"</note>: which signifies blackness or a black person.
**Agabus**: a Locust.
**Agag**: a roof.
**Agar**: a stranger.
**Aggeus**: lovely or pleasing.
**Ahob**: loving.
**Alexander**: a powerful helper.
**Alexandria**: in Hebrew, *No*; which is interpreted as mourning or provocation.
**Alleluia**: praise the Lord.
**Amalec**: a licking people.
**Amam**: mother or their fear.
**Aman**: stirring.
**Amana**: faithfulness or truth.
**Amasai**: with an *aleph* at the beginning; strong or powerful.
**Amasai**: with an *ayin* at the beginning; a present or gift of the people.
**Amen**: let it happen, so be it, let it be firm and steadfast.
**Amorites**: bitter ones, rebels, or the stubborn.
**Amos**: with an *aleph* at the beginning of the word, was the father of Isaiah, and is translated as "strong."
**Amos**: with an *ayin* at the beginning of the word, was the name of one of the twelve Prophets, and means "burdened."
**Omri**: with an *aleph*; means bitter, or speaking.
**Omri**: with an *ayin*; means a handful <note>original: "hanevol," likely a handful or a grip</note> or dominion; he was a Prince of the army of Israel.
**Anania**: cloud of the Lord.
**Anathoth**: answers or song.
**Andrew**: very strong.
**Anna**: gracious or merciful.

<column-break/>

**Antioch**: before a chariot.
**Aphik**: in Hebrew, *Pul*; that is to say, a fall or a ruin, Isaiah 66:19.
**Aphik**: in Hebrew, *Put*; that is to say, heavy or fat, Nahum 3.
**Apostolos**: one sent, or an Ambassador.
**Arabs**: those who are of the evening, or of the evening, 2 Chronicles 26.
**Arabs**: Psalm 72; in Hebrew, *Saba*; that is to say, conversion.
**Aram**: height or loftiness.
**Ararat**: a curse of fear, or fear.
**Arba**: a city named Hebron; that is to say, four.
**Arbel**: God has fought.
**Architriclinus**: a Master of the Feast <note>original: "Hofmeeister," a steward or head waiter at a banquet</note>.
**Areopagite**: from the mountain, or the street of the idol Mars.
**Areopagus**: that little street of Mars.
**Arenna**: a Coffer or song.
**Argob**: clay of the earth, or loam.
**Armenia**: in Hebrew, *Ararat*; a curse of fear or fear.
**Arnon**: leaping with joy.
**Arphaxad**: healing.
**Artaxerxes**: Light or relaxation.
**Asaph**: gathering.
**Asser**: with a *samekh* at the beginning; signifies "bound," a son of Kohath.
**Asher**: with a *shin* at the beginning; signifies "salvation" or "luck," a son of Jacob.
**Ahasuerus**: a Prince or a head.
**Asshur**: spying or well-fortunate.
**Ashtaroth**: Flocks or riches.
**Athalia**: the time unto the Lord.
**Athens**: without hope.
**Attalia**: increasing or nourishing.
**Ava**: wickedness.
**Asa**: adorned.
**Azaria**: the help of the Lord.
**Azor**: a Helper.
**Azotus**: in Hebrew, *Ashdod*; signifies Robbery.
**Baal**: an Idol or ruling.
**Baalim**: Idols or rulers.
**Babel**: confusion or mixing.
**Bilah**: aged or troubled; the maidservant of Rachel (with an *h* at the end).
**Bela**: devouring or destroying (a city, with an *ayin* at the end).
**Balaam**: age of the people.
**Balak**: destroying.
**Benaiah**: a son of the Lord.
**Barak**: a lightning bolt.
**Berechiah**: blessing the Lord.
**Bar-Jonah**: a son of the dove.
**Barnabas**: a son of comfort.
**Barsabas**: a son of conversion.
**Bartimaeus**: a blind son.
**Bartholomew**: a son of him who suspends the waters.
**Baruch**: blessed.
**Bethuel**: a childhood of God.
**Bath**: a measure of liquid things.
**Baal-Peor**: an Idol of the opening of the Earth.
**Beelzebub**: an Idol of the flies.
**Beera**: a Well.
**Behemoth**: four-footed beasts.
**Bel**: old.
**Bela**: devouring, destroying.
**Belial**: perverse, without a yoke.
**Ben-Hinnom**: a son of his riches.
**Benjamin**: a son of the right hand.
**Ben-Oni**: a son of my pains.
**Bera**: a Well.
**Genesis**: in the first, in the beginning; thus is the first book of the Law <note>the Pentateuch</note> named.
